16.4     Amortized causal inference inherits an identification
         model
Let M be a structural model drawn from a prior Π, PM its observational law, and θM the
requested causal functional. A prior-data fitted network can minimize the population loss

                                          n [− log qη (θM | Dn )].
                               EM ∼Π,Dn ∼PM
16.5. Proximal foundation models still face an inverse problem                                 149


With an unrestricted conditional density family and exact optimization, the optimum is the
prior’s conditional target distribution. A finite network trained on finitely many simulations
only approximates that optimum. If training labels are future outcomes rather than causal
functionals, the optimal distribution is different.
   CausalFM constructs priors on compatible observational/interventional distribution pairs,
using practitioner-supplied back-door, front-door or IV identification settings (Ma et al., 2026b,
Definitions 3.1 and 4.2). Its IV example uses an additive response and completeness conditions;
it is not an amortized solution for every valid binary-IV LATE problem. The paper’s Theorem
4.3 gives a prior-consistency necessity result for a linear query, with its stated noncancellation
and observational-class conditions. Identification is not a sufficient guarantee that an arbitrary
prior or trained network is calibrated for every new dataset.
  The finite case exposes the central restriction without an asymptotic argument. The two
models in Section 1.6 give exactly the same strictly positive distribution of (A, Y ), but have
ATEs zero and .36. If the second model has prior mass w, then, for every observational sample,

       P (M = 2 | Dn ) = w,       E[θM | Dn ] = .36w,       Var(θM | Dn ) = .362 w(1 − w).

The likelihood cannot revise the relative weights of equivalent models. More training examples
can approximate this prior conclusion more accurately; more observations from the same
experiment cannot identify which causal model generated them. Additional causal information
changes the experiment or the allowed model class.
   The same example bounds a learned classifier of those causal explanations. Under equal
prior probability, any classifier based only on the observed sample has average classification
error at least 1/2, since its input distribution is identical in the two cases. Identifiability
itself is a property of a target and an assumed model class, not a directly observed label of
one distribution. An output score can be meaningful under its training prior; it cannot be a
distribution-free certificate that a bank’s assumptions hold.
  The temporal PFN preprint Talupula and Sharma (2026, Sections 3.2–3.6) proposes time
encodings, a causal-judgment head, mixed structural priors, selected contexts and one-step
posterior correction. These are useful research questions, but a numerical identifiability score
cannot defeat the equivalence example. Nor does writing ψbPFN + Pn ϕb specify valid inference:
one must identify the target, derive its influence function for the actual longitudinal observation
model, control the remainder, account for context selection and dependence, and justify the
covariance estimate. The paper’s displayed generic correction is not accepted here as a theorem
covering arbitrary panel CATEs.


16.5      Proximal foundation models still face an inverse problem
ProximalFM targets τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x] by averaging over the proxies rather than
conditioning its target on them (Muller et al., 2026, Sections 2–3). Its causal route remains
the bridge equation in Section 4.3, together with latent exchangeability, proxy exclusions,
positivity, completeness and bridge existence. The network amortizes inference across synthetic
structural models; it does not make the integral operator injective.
   The distinction is acknowledged in the primary text. Proxy exclusions follow from its chosen
structural inputs and independent noises, and propensity clipping enforces positivity in the
simulator. General nonlinear completeness is not guaranteed. Proxy width and cardinality
constraints are used as heuristics, with relevance diagnostics (Muller et al., 2026, Section 3.1
and Appendix B.3.4).
  For a finite illustration, let U = (U1 , U2 ) contain two independent binary coordinates.
150                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


Construct five proxy bits as conditionally independent noisy measurements of U1 , with error
probability .2. The proxy vector has dimension five and 32 possible values, exceeding the latent
dimension two and four possible latent values. Nevertheless, its 32 × 4 conditional-probability
matrix has duplicate columns for (U1 , 0) and (U1 , 1) and rank two. Width and cardinality do
not recover the missing coordinate. To make the conditional argument explicit, let treatment
be assigned from U with strictly positive probabilities using noise independent of the proxy
noises. Writing the proxy vector as Z, this gives Z ⊥ (U2 , A) | U1 . For each treatment stratum
a, the nonzero function
                               ha (U ) = U2 − E[U2 | U1 , A = a]
satisfies E[ha (U ) | Z, A = a] = 0 by iterated expectation. Centering only on A would in general
be insufficient: conditioning on treatment can associate U1 and U2 . Thus incompleteness
persists after conditioning on treatment under the specified assignment law. The relevant
bridge and target must be examined as in Equation (4.1); even when a particular target
survives a null space, that requires an argument.
  The preprint’s Appendix A carefully separates the oracle from its trained network. Let
R(M ) = PM and fix a query x. Under measurability and integrability, the oracle posterior
mean converges, for Π-almost every model, to

                                gx (R(M )) = EΠ [τM (x) | R(M )].

Its Theorem A.4 makes oracle consistency equivalent to the target being a measurable function
of R(M ) almost surely under the prior. This is prior-almost-sure, pointwise-query consistency.
It is not uniform coverage over bank models outside the prior, and the completeness heuristic
does not establish the theorem’s identification premise for every generated SCM.
  Training labels introduce another distinction. If τbK (x) = K −1 k {Yk (1) − Yk (0)} uses
                                                                         P

independent downstream simulations conditional on the SCM and query, then

                                E[τbK (x) | Dn ] = E[τM (x) | Dn ].

Thus population squared-error training targets the oracle posterior mean even at finite K. The
full label distribution is convolved with simulation noise. Recovering a posterior distribution
needs an identified noise model or vanishing label noise. Appendix A.4 explicitly does not prove
that the finite-K Gaussian noise correction yields exact recovery. Individual-effect variation,
oracle posterior uncertainty, approximation error and frequentist coverage are four different
quantities.


16.6      History-dependent logging can make informative paths
          rare
A hidden-state model with few states can have a difficult value-estimation problem even when
actions are randomized conditional on recorded history. Jajoo (2026, Sections 2–5) constructs
two finite-horizon models that differ only in the hidden state reached by the first continue
action. Later continue actions preserve the state; either of two reset actions fixes it to zero or
one. Only the terminal observation reveals anything, with reward-one probabilities 1/4 and
3/4 in the two states. The target always continues, so its values are 1/4 and 3/4.
  The known logger chooses the first action uniformly. Before any reset it continues with
probability 2/3, while reset probabilities are 1/6 each. After a reset its history-dependent
action probabilities change, but every action remains at least 1/6. A reset erases the only
16.7. Dynamic bounds require a compatible joint causal model                                151


difference between the models. A trajectory is informative precisely when it never resets, with
probability
                                      1 2 H−2
                                        
                               pH =               ,   H ≥ 2.
                                      3 3
Reduce each trajectory to an erasure or its terminal bit. The two laws, in the order (⊥, 0, 1),
are
              Q0 = (1 − pH , 3pH /4, pH /4),     Q1 = (1 − pH , pH /4, 3pH /4).
The rest of the trajectory conditional on that symbol is distributed identically in both models.
Direct calculation gives DKL (Q0 ∥Q1 ) = pH log(3)/2. If an estimator is within 1/8 of the value
with probability 1 − δ in both models, for 0 < δ < 1/2, thresholding at 1/2 yields a test with
both errors at most δ. Data processing of relative entropy through that test therefore gives

                                              2 kl(1 − δ, δ)

No faster optimizer changes this missing information. For the reduced experiment, the exact
optimal test chooses model 1 when terminal ones outnumber zeros among nonerased episodes,
randomizing at a tie.
   The striking part of the source theorem is that its particular behavior-marginal state/be-
lief/revealing coverage constants remain bounded as H grows. The future distribution in that
definition averages over logger memory conditional on physical state; it need not equal the
continuation distribution after a fixed history. Augmenting state by logger memory repairs the
Markov description but reveals a rare never-reset state and a growing coverage cost. These
are not hidden confounding and not a claim of hardness for every POMDP. They show why
the conditioning set in an OPE theorem must be preserved by an adapter.
   In banking terms, many customers may visit every coarse delinquency band, yet very few
follow the uninterrupted action path of a proposed policy. The synthetic construction does not
quantify that frequency in a bank. It motivates measuring target-relevant trajectory support
and considering a shorter target horizon, additional information, or new randomized data
when the historical experiment is uninformative.


16.7     Dynamic bounds require a compatible joint causal model
Partial identification can replace a point forecast, but local uncertainty sets must correspond
to a common structural model. Alvarez and Ferrando (2026, Sections 2–4) studies a finite
observed-state model with stage-specific hidden confounding between At and St+1 . Its hidden
disturbances do not persist as an unrecorded customer characteristic across stages. At a
confounded supported cell (t, s, a), write

              ms′ = P (St+1 = s′ , At = a | St = s),         r = P (At ̸= a | St = s).

The default feasible next-state law is

                     Qt (s, a) = {q ∈ ∆(St+1 (s, a)) : ms′ ≤ qs′ ≤ ms′ + r}.

Equivalently, q = m + rv with v a probability vector on the allowed successors (with the evident
singleton when r = 0). The observed treated mass is fixed; the untreated counterfactual
mass is unobserved. Without support the set is the whole structural successor simplex; with
exchangeability it reduces to the observed transition.
152                                                                        Causal analysis for a universal bank


  For a fixed regime d and terminal reward y(s), rectangularity permits the lower recursion

                                                                           q(s′ )V t+1 (s′ ),
                                                                      X
                    V T (s) = y(s),     V t (s) =       min
                                                    q∈Qt (s,dt (s))
                                                                      s′

and similarly a maximum for the upper bound. The proof proceeds backward: one can choose
an attaining local kernel at every state while keeping all already chosen continuation kernels.
Compactness gives attainment, and the ability to paste those choices gives equality with the
global optimization. Without that ability, the recursion optimizes an enlarged model class.
   For example, if m = (.2, .4), r = .4, and the next-state values are (0, 1), the sharp local mean
interval is [.4, .8]. The source’s Theorem 3.8 proves global causal sharpness for its unmodified
default local sets and maintained causal model. Narrowed sensitivity sets, estimated confidence
regions or arbitrary POMDP ambiguity sets do not automatically inherit that conclusion.
  A project example makes the coupling problem concrete. Suppose a persistent unobserved
binary characteristic U produces two cash-flow components C0 = U and C1 = 1 − U , with
unknown distribution of U . Each marginal mean may range over [0, 1], but E[C0 + C1 ] = 1
under every allowed model. Replacing the coupled model by the Cartesian product of the two
marginal intervals gives [0, 2]. Such bounds are conservative but not sharp for the specified
model. Including sufficient state and preserving the structural successor restriction can restore
the relation; independently optimizing each marginal cannot.
   The 2026 paper takes the observational law as given. Finite-sample uncertainty in m, r
and the support is another problem. Estimating them and treating the resulting polytope as
known understates uncertainty. Joint confidence regions, moment-inequality inference or a
justified bootstrap for the bound endpoints need their own regularity analysis.


16.8      Irregular discovery and deconfounding must match the
          observation law
The ITSY preprint addresses missing entries on an underlying regular grid in a linear first-order
SVAR,
           Xt = AXt + BXt−1 + et ,        Xt = (I − A)−1 BXt−1 + (I − A)−1 et ,
with a contemporaneous DAG, causal sufficiency, structural stationarity and MCAR missingness
(Xu et al., 2026, Sections 3–4). Reformulation transforms the noise covariance:

                                 Ωred = (I − A)−1 Ωe (I − A)−⊤ .

Thus minimizing an unweighted error in the reduced equation can change the structural
objective. The source couples imputation and graph learning and corrects the residual
geometry. This is a meaningful algorithmic contribution inside its model; it does not turn
endogenous customer visits into MCAR grid omissions. Continuous-time monitoring requires
the event-likelihood analysis of Chapter 12.
   LUCID routes a discovery procedure between sparse and pervasive confounding using the
residual spectrum of a fitted VAR(1) (Fesanghary, 2026, Section 4). Its branches use post-
double-selection filtering or spectral trimming and contemporaneous recovery. The inspected
text explicitly calls its lag-zero orientation step a heuristic; a router-separation proof is
referred to an extended version. A low-rank residual component can reflect common causes, a
misspecified dynamic model, or common measurement effects. Removing a spectral component
changes the information used for discovery; it does not generally prove that the remaining
graph is causally sufficient.
16.9. Comparison at the level of scientific operations                                        153


   These proposals should be tested against the distinctions already derived: hidden common
causes versus mediators, full and summary graphs, lag errors versus direction errors, MCAR
versus informative observation, and observational equivalence versus structural identification.
Synthetic edge-recovery scores establish performance under their generating regimes. For
a bank decision the final question remains whether the graph class, including unresolved
orientations and latent structure, identifies the requested intervention or only a set of possible
effects.


16.9      Comparison at the level of scientific operations
The promising reusable operations are conditional-law learning, orthogonal moment solving,
prior-conditioned amortization, constrained graph search and robust value recursion. Each
returns a different mathematical object. A graph distribution is not a causal-effect confidence
interval; a posterior under an SCM prior is not a test of that prior’s identifying restrictions; a
Bellman bound over a rectangular uncertainty class is not necessarily a sharp causal bound.
   The appropriate comparison holds the target, information set and sampling unit fixed. For
neural g-computation, compare simulated intervention functionals and tail-dependent decisions
as well as prediction error. For orthogonal learners, inspect moment residuals, nuisance
products, split validity and weak conditioning. For foundation models, vary structural priors,
context selection, proxy strength and departures from the training experiment. For discovery,
retain equivalence information and propagate it to effect sets. For policy evaluation, inspect
target-relevant paths and logger memory. This leads directly to a software contract: an
estimator can be interchangeable only within a common, justified mathematical operation.
Chapter 17

Composing software without
changing the scientific question

The preceding theory makes software selection more demanding than choosing an estimator
with an attractive name. A deposit-retention analysis may ask for an average effect across
customers, across branches, or across balances. A collections analysis may ask for an effect of a
fixed schedule, a rule using available history, or a modification of the historical assignment law.
These distinctions change the estimand before any package is called. The common product
needs to preserve them as it moves between data engines, identification libraries, statistical
estimators and decision solvers.
   This chapter uses the preserved primary documentation and selected source interfaces of 44
projects. The scientific comparisons concern the inspected versions, using 7 October 2026 as the
publication/version cutoff where a dated revision could be established. Mutable documentation
accessed on 8 October has a separate access identity and does not establish its exact contents
at the cutoff. A documented interface, a successful package execution and a validated banking
analysis are different evidence. The broad comparisons establish source/document evidence.
Selected installed DuckDB and Polars revision operations, scikit-learn Lasso normalization and
SciPy optimization now have executed reference comparisons, recorded separately from the
historical documentation snapshots. Their versions and local source/license copies accompany
the receipts; qualification applies to those operations, not every feature of each package
(duckdb contributors, 2026a; polars contributors, 2026; scikit-learn contributors, 2026; scipy
contributors, 2026; numpy contributors, 2026). The selected DoubleML score and Tigramite
temporal-search executions in Sections 45.11 and 10.11 add substantive causal operations
with matched references and preserved endpoint semantics (doubleml contributors, 2026;
tigramite contributors, 2026). Published package versions, mutable documentation snapshots
and commit-pinned source files are kept distinct in the accompanying source register. No
speed ranking is inferred from repository activity or a maintainer’s benchmark.


17.1      An adapter maps mathematical objects as well as arrays
Let a request contain a causal model class M, observation operator K, intervention g, target
population ν and functional θ(M ; g, ν). Let P = K(M ) denote the observed law. The first
possible output is an identification statement

                          θ(M ; g, ν) = Ψ(K(M ))       for all M ∈ M.



                                               154
17.2. Effects, projections and the population carried by weights                               155


An estimator is then a numerical map from the observed sample to Ψ.     b An inference method is
a further construction whose validity depends on the sampling scheme and estimator remainder.
The input of a planner is different again: it requires an interventional transition/observation/re-
ward model, or an explicitly defined ambiguity set. None of these objects can be substituted
merely because its serialized form is an array of numbers.
   DoWhy exposes this separation in its interface. The inspected identify_effect selects its
ID implementation when requested; estimate_effect separately takes an identified expression
and an estimator method (py-why contributors, 2026b). An expression produced by graphical
identification need not have a matching numerical estimator in the chosen backend. Thus
the product must distinguish three outcomes: a supported identified functional, a valid
identification result whose estimation is not implemented, and nonidentification in the assumed
model class. The last requires a scientific witness such as the paired models of Section 1.6; a
missing Python method is not such a witness.
  There is a useful criterion for a data adapter. Suppose it transforms the observation through
T and the backend estimates ΨB . Target preservation requires

                     Ψ(P ) = ΨB (T# P ) for every allowed observed law P,                   (17.1)

where T# P is the distribution after transformation. Invertible relabeling usually satisfies this
with an appropriate inverse interpretation. Demeaning, history truncation, averaging time
bins, hard record linkage, weight normalization and imputation generally require additional
arguments. Equation (17.1) also shows why a common fit/predict signature is insufficient:
it says nothing about which functional survives the conversion.


17.2      Effects, projections and the population carried by weights
EconML, DoubleML, causalml and grf provide useful but overlapping learning components
(py-why contributors, 2026c; DoubleML contributors, 2026; uber contributors, 2026; grf-labs
contributors, 2026). The relevant comparison begins with the target. For binary treatment
under adjustment, the CATE is τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x]. A partially linear residual
coefficient instead solves an unconditional moment and, with heterogeneous effects, can weight
τ (x) by residual treatment variation. The R-learner calculation in Section 3.4 identifies that
difference. An IV learner introduces yet another moment and its exclusion, relevance and
effect-heterogeneity restrictions. A common effect-prediction interface cannot turn these
coefficients into a common CATE.
   The inspected grf::causal_forest documents the distinction explicitly: for binary uncon-
founded treatment it targets a CATE; for continuous treatment it uses

                                             Cov(Y, A | X = x)
                                    b(x) =                     .
                                              Var(A | X = x)

This is a local linear projection in the treatment dimension. It is not generally the dose-response
derivative at a nominated action. For example, if A is uniform on [−1, 1], Y (a) = a3 , and
no confounding is present, then b = E[A4 ]/E[A2 ] = 3/5, while the derivative at a = 0 is zero.
Both quantities can be meaningful; an interface must name the requested one.
   Population weighting is equally substantive. If branch c contains nc customers with average
effect τc , then                     P
                                         nc τc                1 X
                         θcustomer = Pc        ,    θbranch =      τc .
                                        c nc                  C c
156                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


For two branches with sizes 1 and 9 and effects 0 and 10, these values are 9 and 5. The
source of causal_forest states that equalize.cluster.weights=TRUE uses inverse cluster-
size weights when estimating average effects; it also requires sample.weights=NULL. The
default gives equal weight to units. This option changes the population aggregation, not merely
the reported standard error (grf-labs contributors, 2026).
   A balance-weighted bank target needs a further definition. A weight measured before
treatment can define a baseline exposure-weighted average. A balance measured after treatment
may itself change under intervention; using it as an ordinary sampling weight can select on a
treatment descendant. The product must carry the weight’s time, role and normalization with
the target. Frequency weights, sampling weights, treatment-density ratios, loss weights and
numerical importance weights cannot share a single undocumented field.
   DoubleML’s inspected data classes distinguish outcomes, treatments, instruments, covariates
and cluster columns. They do not make arbitrary dependent records satisfy a cross-fitting
theorem. causalml’s documentation supplies a CATE/uplift and benchmarking route; using
its predictions for contact allocation still requires the policy-value argument and independent
evaluation of Chapter 13. A package comparison should therefore hold the estimand, population,
nuisance information and evaluation sample fixed before comparing bias, coverage, policy value
or runtime.


17.3     A panel identifier does not specify a panel model
The same customer-period table can support a fixed-effect projection, a staggered-adoption
ATT, a dynamic GMM coefficient or a sequential blip. Chapter 8 derives different assumptions
for each. The software mirrors this division. linearmodels supplies linear panel, IV and
system baselines; PyFixest and fixest supply formula-based fixed-effect, IV and other regression
operations; pydynpd explicitly constructs difference and system GMM (bashtage contributors,
2026; py-econometrics contributors, 2026; lrberge contributors, 2026; dazhwu contributors,
2026). Absorbing many fixed effects quickly does not repair an invalid heterogeneous-treatment
TWFE estimand. Likewise, an automated search across instrument lags cannot validate the
orthogonality of those instruments.
   For a branch rollout, did::att_gt represents first-adoption cohorts and group–time effects.
Its inspected interface has important implications for a shared service. Time-varying sampling
weights are handled differently in balanced panels and repeated cross sections or unbalanced
panels. Fixing weights at an anchor period can remove units unobserved at that anchor.
Beyond individual clustering, this snapshot supports at most one additional coarser cluster
variable. Uniform bands require its bootstrap; setting compute_inffunc=FALSE produces
point estimates without inference and prevents the documented aggregation through aggte
(bcallaway11 contributors, 2026). Saving memory by dropping influence information therefore
also removes downstream operations.
   DoubleML’s panel container is not a substitute for an arbitrary sequential history object.
Its default static_panel=False interprets treatment values as first-treatment timing, and
the inspected constructor permits only one treatment column (DoubleML contributors, 2026).
An array of monthly credit-limit changes is not a cohort-date array. The conversion must be
rejected unless the requested analysis explicitly defines an appropriate adoption representation.
   DynamicDML illustrates the separate chronological contract. The inspected EconML
implementation requires equal group lengths and interprets each group’s occurrence order as
its period order. Only first-period X defines effect heterogeneity; later X is a time-varying
control. The fit method warns that sample_weight and sample_var are ignored and passes
17.4. Longitudinal libraries must preserve the intervention law                               157


neither into fitting (py-why contributors, 2026c). A bank adapter must therefore sort by a
validated decision clock, check for missing or duplicated periods, use a group-aware split, and
reject a weighted request this interface cannot honor. Padding a missing decision with zeros
changes the observation law and is not a general repair for an unbalanced panel.
   Alternatives change the identifying model rather than merely the optimizer. synthdid’s
documented input requires simultaneous treatment with a block adoption matrix. gsynth
imputes untreated outcomes through interactive fixed effects; its current README says that
it wraps fect and is maintained for backward compatibility, so that dependency needs its own
qualification (synth-inference contributors, 2026; xuyiqing contributors, 2026). HonestDiD
takes an estimated event-study vector and covariance and adds an explicit class of possible
trend violations (asheshrambachan contributors, 2026). That is a sensitivity operation on an
already defined contrast, not an automatic selection of a true trend restriction.
   CausalImpact and CausalPy provide further useful comparisons (google contributors, 2026;
pymc-labs contributors, 2026). CausalImpact’s primary documentation requires unaffected
controls and a stable counterfactual relationship after the intervention. CausalPy offers distinct
quasi-experimental designs with Bayesian or OLS estimation. The appropriate comparison
with a cohort estimator or factor model asks whether each model answers the same bank
intervention and whether its counterfactual restrictions are credible. Comparing interval widths
without those restrictions would reward unwarranted certainty.


17.4      Longitudinal libraries must preserve the intervention law
The longitudinal g-formula can be evaluated through fitted transition distributions, backward
outcome regressions or targeted/augmented constructions. gfoRmula, ltmle, lmtp and zEpid
expose different parts of this space (CausalInference contributors, 2026; joshuaschwab con-
tributors, 2026; nt-williams contributors, 2026; pzivich contributors, 2026). They cannot be
made interchangeable by renaming their output policy effect. The treatment law, censoring
intervention, endpoint and history are part of the mathematical input.
   gfoRmula’s inspected interface takes person-period data, conditional models, history func-
tions and named interventions. It returns survival risks or terminal means/probabilities. The
number of simulated persons, nsimul, controls Monte Carlo approximation; the number of
bootstrap samples, nsamples, concerns sampling uncertainty. Increasing the former cannot
compensate for a small observed cohort. The interface also exposes competing-event treatment,
visit processes and prebaseline lag conventions. Its sim_trunc option defaults to true for
specified continuous covariate families, restricting simulated values to the observed range. Such
a transformation must be part of the reported simulation law. For a simple project example,
P (L = −2, 0, 2) = (1/4, 1/2, 1/4) gives E[L2 ] = 2; clipping to [−1, 1] gives 1/2. The numeric
range may look safer while the tail-sensitive financial target changes.
   ltmle represents chronology through column order in wide data. Its treatment nodes must
be binary, its survival indicators must remain one after the event, and its probability bounds
concern cumulative treatment/censoring factors. Its output retains influence values and both
bounded and unbounded cumulative probabilities. Continuous outcomes can be scaled and,
when Yrange is supplied, truncated. Some robust-variance options are unavailable with
nonbinary outcomes, G-computation or other listed options (joshuaschwab contributors, 2026).
A sensible adapter constructs columns from a separately validated clock and records each of
these choices. Renaming an arbitrary real-valued bank action as a binary node would create a
different intervention.
  lmtp supplies targeted and sequentially doubly robust estimators for modified treatment
158                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


policies, with explicit ordered histories, censoring, competing events, sampling weights and
optional cluster identifiers. Its finite-history parameter k is a modeling restriction when
the full history is relevant. Its source also resolves a potentially serious terminological
ambiguity. The function ipsi implements a stochastic retention-or-replacement rule. For
e(h) = P (A = 1 | H = h), direct integration over the auxiliary uniform random variable in the
source gives                           (

                          qδ (1 | h) =                                                  (17.2)

The downward branch scales exposure risk; the upward branch scales nonexposure risk by
1/δ. This differs from the odds multiplier δe/(1 − e + δe) in Section 6.1. At e = .2, δ = .5
produces .1 instead of 1/9; δ = 2 produces .6 instead of 1/3. The corresponding policy means
and influence functions therefore cannot be interchanged. The comparison is a derivation from
inspected source, not a package execution.
   The score difference can be made explicit. For a one-time binary action and a differentiable
probability transform q = f (e), let ma (h) = E[Y | A = a, H = h] and µf (h) = (1 −
f (e(h)))m0 (h) + f (e(h))m1 (h). Differentiating the outcome regressions, the propensity and

                             Af (e)              (1 − A)(1 − f (e))

   zEpid offers useful Python references for weighting, g-computation, targeting and transport.
Its documentation specifically limits its IPMW description to monotone missingness and its
SNMM g-estimation to a single time point (pzivich contributors, 2026). An umbrella description
of g-methods must not be promoted to an implementation of every longitudinal method. For
collections, bankruptcy, settlement and exit should be represented as the substantive events
of Section 6.4; a library’s censoring switch does not decide which event the bank intended to
remove.


17.5      A fitted state model is not yet a causal planner
Dynamax is a natural numerical comparator for conditional state-space likelihoods. The
inspected HMM abstraction builds initial, transition and emission components, supplies
marginal_log_prob, filter, smoother, and an EM E-step (probml contributors, 2026). Its
optional external inputs enter through those components; the standard transition model can
be a fixed transition matrix. Thus an input argument does not prove that a selected subclass
has an action-dependent transition.
   More fundamentally, the conditional emission likelihood does not automatically contain a
private action logger. Under the common law of Section 5.7, observations of an action can alter
the posterior state through the factor qη (at | st , ht ). If logging is independent of hidden state
conditional on the recorded history, that factor may cancel from the state update. Otherwise
it must be represented in the observational likelihood. Replacing it by a proposed intervention
then changes the experiment. A state-space adapter must establish this factorization before
fitting; optimizer convergence cannot repair an omitted likelihood factor.
17.6. Discovery outputs must retain their unresolved information                              159


   PyMC and NumPyro can express richer probabilistic models and estimate their parameters
(pymc-devs contributors, 2026; pyro-ppl contributors, 2026). They provide numerical inference,
not a general identification theorem. PyMC’s inspected example distinguishes model interven-
tion and observation through do and observe; their causal interpretation still depends on the
supplied model. NumPyro supports HMC/NUTS, mixed discrete/continuous methods and
variational alternatives. Marginalizing a finite hidden state is often useful, but it is not the
only documented approach to discrete variables. Comparisons should hold the likelihood and
prior fixed and separately measure integration error, parameter uncertainty and sensitivity to
observationally equivalent causal completions.
   POMDPs.jl and pomdp_py solve another layer of the problem (JuliaPOMDP contributors,
2026; h2r contributors, 2026). They provide problem representations, planning and simulation
interfaces. The Julia core interface, POMDPTools, a solver and a Python bridge have separate
versions and dependencies. An adapter must state whether the observation occurs before
or after the transition, what information the policy receives and when reward is paid. A
smoothed state using future bank records cannot be used as an online decision belief. Solver
residuals and rollout error should be evaluated against the model-conditional value, while the
identification and model error are assessed through Chapter 7.
   d3rlpy, SCOPE-RL and Open Bandit Pipeline offer policy-learning and evaluation com-
parators (takuseno contributors, 2026; hakuhodo-technologies contributors, 2026; st-tech
contributors, 2026). Their natural objects differ: a fitted policy, a sequential return estimate
or return distribution, and a contextual-bandit reward. A one-period contact reward cannot
represent a multimonth recovery path with carryover. Occupancy-ratio OPE and trajectory-
ratio OPE also require different sufficient-information and coverage conditions. The rare-path
construction in Section 16.6 is a relevant stress case even when each logged action has a positive
probability.


17.6      Discovery outputs must retain their unresolved informa-
          tion
The graph is a scientific output with a type. Tigramite’s documentation distinguishes PCMCI,
PCMCI+, LPCMCI and other variants, and separately lists the restrictions of conditional-
independence tests (jakobrunge contributors, 2026). Selecting a nonlinear test does not remove
a stationarity assumption; adding a missing-value mask does not identify an informative
observation process. A temporal discovery result must retain lag convention, window, mask,
background knowledge, test and model class.
   The inspected causal-learn FCI interface returns a graph marked as a PAG and edge-property
objects. Its matrix distinguishes tails, arrowheads and circles (py-why contributors, 2026a).
Converting that matrix into Boolean adjacency would erase precisely the information needed
for effect identification. A circle endpoint expresses unresolved ancestral information; it is not
a weakly weighted arrow. Bidirected edges are not two ordinary causal arrows. The receiving
effect operation must reason over compatible graph completions or use a criterion valid for the
equivalence class, as in Chapter 10.
  NOTEARS and DAGMA supply useful continuous-optimization constructions, while gCastle
collects several algorithm families and Tetrad offers a separate Java ecosystem (xunzheng
contributors, 2026; kevinsbello contributors, 2026; huawei-noah contributors, 2026; cmu-phil
contributors, 2026). For the optimization methods, the acyclicity constraint is a statement
about a fitted graph; it is not a proof that the observed law uniquely identifies that graph.
Search tolerances, thresholding and initialization belong to the numerical output. For a toolbox,
160                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


the assumptions belong to the selected algorithm, not to the package name. gCastle’s inspected
module distinguishes IID and event-sequence algorithms and marks HPCI as under development.
Tetrad’s language bridge and runtime need separate qualification from a particular search
procedure.
   Causica combines graph and neural-mechanism fitting within an additive-noise structural
model, then simulates interventions (microsoft contributors, 2026). This is a useful comparison
where the structural restrictions are justified. A variational graph distribution conditional
on that model is not a frequentist graph-confidence set or a distribution-free certificate of
causal identification. The current README explicitly says Rhino and DDECI were removed
from the codebase and refers to an earlier release. Their paper descriptions cannot establish
the capability of the current snapshot. The initial CausalNex repository retrieval failed; that
historical failure is not evidence that the project is abandoned (quantumblacklabs contributors,
2026). The later pinned-source comparison recovers its StructureModel and selected NOTEARS
implementations. Default adoption remains deferred pending a justified consumer, an isolated
compatible environment and dependency qualification; source retrieval itself is no longer the
obstacle (mckinsey/causalnex, 2026a).


17.7      Data organization must preserve what was known
DuckDB and Polars provide relational and columnar execution paths; Pandera supplies explicit
schema and value checks (duckdb contributors, 2026b; pola-rs contributors, 2026; unionai-oss
contributors, 2026). These are useful building blocks for Chapter 11, but type-correct data
may still encode the wrong decision history. An event dated before a credit-limit decision may
have reached the bank after it. A later corrected value can also replace the value actually
used. The history constructor must therefore enforce event, availability and revision semantics
before exporting predictors to an estimator.
   Feast’s inspected historical-retrieval API makes the distinction concrete. It uses event time
and TTL, and offers filter_by_created_timestamp. The latter defaults to false; when true it
excludes later-created values only for feature views with a configured creation-timestamp field
(feast-dev contributors, 2026). Hence it is incorrect either to assume every point-in-time join
captures actual availability or to claim this capability is entirely absent. The bank must map
its availability semantics to the configured fields and test a backfill whose event precedes, but
creation follows, the decision. TTL governs freshness and retrieval scope; it cannot establish
that mapping.
   DataHub and OpenMetadata can supply asset descriptions, ownership, glossaries and lineage
(datahub-project contributors, 2026; open-metadata contributors, 2026). Their graphs record
how data are described and produced; they are not causal graphs of the customer or economy.
A transform that computes arrears from transactions produces a lineage edge, not evidence
that editing the arrears column would change past transactions. The product should reuse
the bank’s catalog and attach the causal interpretation to its stable asset identifiers. Broad
catalog marketing that mixes open-source and managed-cloud features is not evidence that a
particular local deployment has those features.
   OpenLineage supplies an extensible run/job/dataset event model (OpenLineage contributors,
2026). A causal-analysis extension should preserve the target, data snapshot, observation
clock, model/graph, split plan and estimator identity. These are proposed scientific facets, not
standard causal semantics already supplied by OpenLineage. Splink addresses another part
of the observation operator: probabilistic linkage supplies pair probabilities and estimated
entity clusters (moj-analytical-services contributors, 2026). Their uncertainty matters when a
false household merge changes the unit of treatment or uses post-treatment information. The
17.8. Distributed execution must preserve the score experiment                                        161


linkage-variance decomposition in Section 11.5 explains why a thresholded ID alone is not a
sufficient uncertainty record.


17.8      Distributed execution must preserve the score experiment
After identification and nuisance fitting, some estimates can be reduced through additive
scores. This creates an opportunity for local SQL, columnar or distributed execution. Ray
supplies tasks, actors and shared objects, while Polars documents streaming and optional GPU
execution (ray-project contributors, 2026; pola-rs contributors, 2026). Neither system specifies
the independent information in a causal analysis.
   For a scalar estimating equation ni=1 ψi (θ)
                                             b = 0, write Jb = n−1
                                    P                                       P
                                                                            i ∂θ ψi . If sampling clusters

                                d θ)
                                Var(                          ψi        ,                          (17.3)

before any stated finite-cluster correction. The reduction key is the statistical cluster, not
the worker partition. With score values (1, 1, −1, −1) in two clusters (1, 1) and (−1, −1), the
cluster meat is 8; treating rows as independent gives 4. Sharding each cluster across workers
and squaring partial sums before regrouping repeats that error. Correct distributed execution
first sums by stable cluster identity and then forms the outer products. Multiway clustering
and serial dependence require their own covariance constructions.
   Cross-fitting has the same constraint. A fold assignment must be a durable function of
the permitted sampling unit or time block, fixed before worker scheduling. A retry must not
duplicate a score contribution; repartitioning must not move a household between training
and evaluation. Floating-point reductions may differ across orders, so a declared numerical
tolerance is appropriate, but the statistical partition must be exact.
   The resulting qualification sequence is constructive. First verify a small finite-law functional
and its failure cases. Then compare the adapter’s actual target and outputs against a numerical
reference. Next evaluate sampling bias, coverage or policy regret under named experiments.
Finally measure the same scientifically valid computation under larger loads, including memory,
spill, retries and cost. A larger row count is useful only after these identities are preserved.


17.9      What the comparison assigns to the shared product
The reusable layer should own the intervention and observation representations, target-
preserving transformations, identification evidence, inference requirements and immutable
execution records. Existing libraries can then supply well-defined numerical operations.
A bounded first set includes adjustment-based effects, valid linear-IV moments, specified
panel/cohort contrasts, finite-horizon observed-history policies and graph-equivalence discovery
outputs. Controlled latent models require a separate observational/interventional likelihood
interface and evidence for the requested value; supplying a planner alone cannot complete it.
    This division also provides a substantive alternative to building the product. An expert
team can compose the same open-source libraries directly. The shared product has value only
if it preserves the scientific contracts more reliably, reduces repeated data and validation work,
and improves decision throughput at a measured total cost. An estimator wrapper with a
common name adds little. The next design step is to specify the exact operations, invalid
requests, numerical obligations and reusable artifacts that make that claim testable.
Chapter 18

Survey method and the common
causal software contract

18.1     Compare a scientific operation before comparing a pack-
         age
A bank considering a causal library faces several different purchasing and engineering decisions.
It may need a defensible effect of an invitation, a description of plausible causal directions
among funding variables, or a policy for repeated servicing decisions. A package that produces
a directed graph does not necessarily answer the first question. A package that estimates an
average treatment effect does not necessarily answer the third. The survey therefore takes a
scientific operation as its unit of comparison: an input with a declared observation law, a causal
target, assumptions connecting the two, and an output whose meaning survives conversion
into the bank’s units.
   This choice changes what counts as competitive capability. Consider a request to increase
deposit funding by changing the offered rate. A system that returns several compatible
effects has provided useful information if the observations cannot distinguish their underlying
mechanisms. A system that returns one number after choosing a convenient graph may have
answered a more restrictive question. The comparison must expose the restriction before
comparing accuracy, speed or convenience. Similarly, a symbolic expression for an effect and
an estimate of that expression are different accomplishments. The expression identifies what
information is needed; its numerical evaluation adds statistical and computational obligations.
  The proposed common request is

                                  q = (U, T , O, A, Y, Ψ, G, S),                           (18.1)

where U specifies the eligible population and sampling unit, T the decision and measurement
clocks, O the observed variables and their units, and A the feasible intervention. Y specifies
the outcome and horizon. The functional Ψ is the requested causal quantity; G contains the
graph or graph class and its substantive restrictions; S describes sampling and uncertainty.
For example, one row may represent one independently sampled eligible customer, the action
may be a 25 basis point increase offered before account opening, and the outcome may be
net funding value over the next quarter. These declarations are scientific inputs. A software
interface cannot establish them merely by accepting a table with suitable column names.
  For an observational law P and an admissible model class M, define
                                                       obs
                          IΨ (P, M) = {Ψ(M ) : M ∈ M, PM   = P }.                          (18.2)

                                               162
18.2. A bounded survey that can be extended without changing its claims                        163


This is the collection of target values compatible with the same observations and assumptions.
It is a population object. A finite-sample graph estimate, an estimated collection of effects, a
Bayesian posterior and a confidence set each add different operations to it. A common result
schema must distinguish these objects. Reducing all four to a scalar and two bounds would
make the schema convenient at the cost of its scientific meaning.


18.2      A bounded survey that can be extended without changing
          its claims
The landscape has two dimensions that should be searched separately. The method dimen-
sion includes observational, latent-variable and interventional discovery; identification and
counterfactuals; heterogeneous effects; instrumental variables and discontinuities; longitudinal
treatment and survival; policy evaluation; panels and differences in differences; synthetic con-
trols; time series; interference; mediation and sensitivity; transport and missingness; Bayesian
structural models; observation construction; and computational workflow. The implementation
dimension distinguishes R, Python, Java, C/C++, other language paths and commercial
offerings. A language binding, an underlying numerical engine and a commercial wrapper can
occupy different positions in that matrix without being three independent implementations.
   The publication cutoff is 7 October 2026. Acquisition time, software revision, manual
generation date and scholarly publication date are retained separately. This matters even for
apparently simple documentation: the inspected pcalg manual identifies version 2.7-12 and a
package date in 2024, while the manual itself was generated in May 2026. The bnlearn manual
identifies version 5.2.1 dated 17 July 2026. BiDAG’s inspected manual was generated in May
2026 but describes a release dated May 2023 (pcalg contributors, 2026; Marco Scutari and
contributors, 2026; Polina Suter and Jack Kuipers, 2026). None of these dates alone measures
current support quality, future maintenance or compatibility with the proposed product.
   A reproducible search records the query, source, date filter, returned identities, pagination
and stopping rule. For the R observational-discovery comparison developed here, the retained
bibliographic query was “R package causal discovery constraint score continuous DAG.” Its
saved first page contains ten records from a reported 1,648 matches. The primary comparison
starts from the inspected pcalg and bnlearn manuals, follows the BCDAG lead, and then
follows one package-reference step to BiDAG and mcmcabn. Those five paths define the
present comparison. Ten bibliographic results are not an exhaustive R census. The remaining
methodological leads do not establish either the presence or the absence of an R implementation.
   There are two useful stopping rules. A discovery pass can stop after a declared search budget
and report incomplete coverage. A capability decision must instead stop when the evidence is
sufficient for the particular claimed operation, or report that the decision remains unresolved.
The first rule controls search cost; the second controls the strength of the conclusion. Conflating
them would allow an arbitrary search budget to become evidence that a missing capability
does not exist. Conversely, insisting on an unbounded census before discussing any inspected
package would prevent useful comparisons indefinitely.
   Each included path needs a canonical identity, exact source or release, license information,
local source bytes, a digest, inspected technical anchors and a claim tied to those anchors.
Scholarly arguments use the original technical text, preserved as a real paper. Software behavior
uses the relevant manual or source. Search metadata establishes identity and discovery, not
algorithmic properties. A summary prepared by the project can explain a source but cannot
substitute for an unavailable original. An unavailable candidate remains visible with its
unresolved claim and the evidence needed to revisit it.
164                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


  Conflicting evidence also requires a dated resolution. The authentic BCDAG preprint from
2022 is useful for its Gaussian model and posterior construction. Its contemporary package
comparison cannot determine what bnlearn supports in 2026. The inspected bnlearn manual
now documents intervention and counterfactual operations (Federico Castelletti and Alessandro
Mascaro, 2022; Marco Scutari and contributors, 2026). The sensible conclusion is that the
comparison changed with the software. This does not establish the validity of any particular
causal use of bnlearn; it corrects a capability description at a named version.


18.3      What the five R paths actually return
The five packages illustrate why language and algorithm labels are insufficient. Table 18.1
compares their documented outputs. It is a source-based comparison, not a benchmark of
their implementations.
