   This table is evidence about named configurations in the retrieved vendor page. It is not a
runtime benchmark or an authenticated copy of the page as it stood at the 7 October 2026
literature cutoff. In particular, the Java Inference column’s documented model-modification
entry should be retained even though its name might suggest a narrower scope. Conversely,
the REST configuration cannot be credited with parameter fitting or discovery merely because
another configuration in the same product family offers those functions.
24.24. Choosing a commercial latent-model component                                           283


   The same table associates the three Java configurations with model files on the customer’s
servers and the REST configuration with model files on Bayesia servers in France. It describes
Java license validation through the Bayesia License Server, requiring an Internet connection,
and credentials in each REST call. Model residence and license-validation traffic are distinct
architectural questions. Customer storage alone does not establish offline operation. A bank
proposal should decide whether the intended task is model fitting, model modification or
inference, then examine the corresponding deployment path. (Bayesia, 2026a)
   For the proposed library, an adapter would translate an explicit model and variable/state
map into the selected engine contract. It would preserve the input version, configuration,
objective, initialization, convergence details, model output and uncertainty meaning. An
inference-only adapter would accept an already fitted model and supplied evidence. A learning
adapter would also need an exact data/observation specification and fitting controls. Neither
adapter would confer causal truth on an elicited or learned edge. Automatic selection among
these paths remains proposed functionality; no commercial engine was invoked in this review.


24.24.3     License scope and total cost

SMILE explicitly separates development licensing from embedding/deployment licensing. Its
manual distinguishes server deployment from end-user program distribution and directs readers
to obtain pricing details. Its academic conditions are not a general permission for commercial
banking use. The documented C++ implementation and Java, Python, R, .NET and COM
wrappers offer plausible integration routes, but wrapper equivalence and selected-platform
behavior have not been measured here. Reimplementation of proprietary code is not an adoption
route; using a licensed engine through its public contract is the candidate. (BayesFusion, LLC,
2024j,k)
  BayesiaLab Professional documents purchase and rental, individual and floating licenses,
and elastic licensing. The API page distinguishes development from production and describes
a production basis tied to simultaneously loaded model instances. Thus a bank that serves
many models concurrently may face a different license requirement from one that loads models
sequentially, even on the same physical machine. This is a licensing observation, not a claim
that either arrangement meets the bank’s latency requirements. The preserved API table links
a USD twelve-month price list but supplies no numeric fee in its inspected cells. No numerical
amount or binding quotation is available for the compared deployment. (Bayesia, 2026a,c)
   For the other selected engines, the technical examples do not establish the needed edition-
specific license, redistribution rights or full deployment price. The comparison therefore
distinguishes a vendor-requested quotation, a public price-list link whose amount has not been
verified, and an unavailable price in the inspected sources. None means zero cost. A proposed
experiment can still use generated data and an available open-source baseline while price and
license evidence for a commercial trial are acquired later if justified.
  Let L be the license expense allocated to the intended analysis period, I the integration
and maintenance allocation, D the data-preparation cost, H the human review cost, C the
computation/storage cost, and O the monitoring/recovery cost. For a candidate workflow,
compare
                              K =L+I +D+H +C +O
at the same accepted output quality. If m valid decisions are produced, K/m is an accounting
rate only when failed requests, manual corrections and retries remain in K and the definition of
a valid decision is held fixed. It is not a causal return-on-investment estimate. Faster inference
on a supplied model cannot be compared directly with a workflow that also constructs, reviews
and fits that model. The present evidence supplies some license categories and configuration
284                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


constraints; it supplies neither actual vendor workflow timings nor observed bank prices.


24.24.4     The bounded proposal and a useful next comparison

The observed local canonical service preserves supplied graph syntax, declared context, selected
simple effect/set operations and explicit unsupported results. It does not expose a commercial
latent fitter or a general latent-discovery engine. The proposal is to add evidence-linked
formulation, distinct graph and measurement objects, selected adapters and a decision interface
that preserves ambiguity and uncertainty. Those proposed controls are a reason to investigate
an integration; they are not an observed superiority claim against the vendors.
   Three matched comparisons would answer different investment questions. First, a supplied
finite latent measurement model can compare fitting and convergence under the same observa-
tion law, class count, prior and initialization budget. Second, a representation task can compare
class probabilities and predictive use while preserving the distinction from causal adjustment.
Third, a graph discovery task needs explicit latent/selection assumptions, equivalence-class
outputs and an effect query. A fitter or TAN predictor cannot enter the third comparison
as if it produced the required graph class. A randomized-compliance comparison is a fourth,
separate route when the actual design supports it.
   For each route, freeze generated observed inputs and reserve hidden truth for evaluation.
Preserve nonidentification, empty cells, label permutations, failed optimization, weak separation
and alternative missingness mechanisms in the denominator. Compare numerical outputs
only after checking that they represent the same object. Record full workflow resources and
unpriced components, then ask which additional information or implementation step could
change the recommendation. A successful generated comparison can justify a scoped later
licensed or bank experiment. It cannot retroactively authenticate a vendor version, create a
missing identification assumption or confer institutional acceptance.


24.25      Commercial temporal models and intervention discovery

24.25.1     The commercial comparison starts with the decision clock

A funding committee asks whether raising a quoted deposit rate by 25 basis points for one
month will increase retained balances enough to cover the additional expense. A forecasting
team asks whether past rates improve its balance forecast. A risk team asks whether the same
relationship survives a change in the historical pricing policy. All three questions use time
series, but they require different outputs. A predictive lag coefficient can answer the second
question without identifying either of the other two.
    The commercial landscape already provides substantial functionality relevant to these
questions. GeNIe and SMILE represent supplied dynamic Bayesian networks, update beliefs
over time, and learn parameters in a declared structure. IBM SPSS offers automatic selection
of predictive inputs in temporal models. SAS and Stata provide established multivariate
time-series interfaces, while Stata separately exposes structural restrictions and external-
instrument identification. Mplus supplies intensive-longitudinal models with random effects,
latent decompositions and explicit time-series syntax. BayesiaLab documents the distinction
between observation and intervention and provides graph-based causal-analysis workflows. The
proposal should explain how these capabilities can be used and where its own implementation
is less mature; their existence rules out a claim that commercial software offers only correlation
tables.
24.25. Commercial temporal models and intervention discovery                                  285


   This comparison is bounded to inspected official technical text. GeNIe’s manual identifies
itself as 5.0.R2, built in November 2024; the SMILE manual identifies itself as 2.2.4.R1, built in
April 2024. Other anchors are SAS/ETS 14.1, the Mplus 8.1 language addendum, IBM’s SPSS
Statistics 31.0.0 documentation route, and the retrieved Stata command manuals. Mutable
pages were acquired on 13 October 2026, after the 7 October literature cutoff. Edition labels
identify what was inspected; they do not independently authenticate the exact bytes served
on the cutoff date. No vendor engine or paid deployment was executed for this comparison.
(BayesFusion, LLC, 2024g,j,b; SAS Institute, 2026a; Muthen and Muthen, 2018; IBM, 2026a;
StataCorp, 2026c)
   The proposed request should state five things before selecting a package. The sampling
interval identifies the meaning of a lag. The information clock specifies which balances, quotes
and macro releases were available at each decision. The contemporaneous model specifies
whether a within-month response can precede another measured variable. The intervention
states whether the bank replaces an action once, maintains a policy, or responds to a structural
shock. Finally, the sampling law distinguishes a long calendar, independent experimental units
and branches sharing common shocks. These fields determine which commercial result can be
interpreted as an answer, and which can serve only as a diagnostic or candidate model.


24.25.2     Dynamic Bayesian networks: a strong supplied-model baseline

The GeNIe dynamic-model overview defines a dynamic Bayesian network as a discrete-time
model of a stochastic process. It explicitly says that the temporal extension does not itself mean
that the structure or parameters change over time: its described process is stationary. It permits
temporal observations and discusses both discrete and continuous examples. Those statements
concern the representation and evaluation of a supplied model; they are not a guarantee that
the model’s scientific mechanisms are stable under a bank intervention.(BayesFusion, LLC,
2024a)
   The parameter-learning page resolves an otherwise consequential ambiguity. It states that
GeNIe’s structure-learning algorithms do not learn the structure of dynamic models, while
the parameters of an existing DBN can be learned from time series. The network structure
must already be defined. Data columns use a node identifier followed by an underscore and
time-step number, except at time zero. The interface matches model nodes and states to those
columns and then applies EM; the structure remains unchanged and existing network evidence
is ignored during parameter learning. (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024b)
   This is a valuable comparator for a servicing or funding prototype. A bank can supply a
hypothesized state-transition graph, use the tool to fit its parameters and inspect temporal
predictions. It cannot infer from a successful fit that the same software discovered that graph,
identified a rate intervention, or selected between hidden-information alternatives. Nor does
the discrete-DBN parameter-learning page establish parameter learning for every continuous
model mentioned elsewhere in the manual.
   SMILE’s C++ tutorial makes the integration contract unusually concrete. It uses
SetTemporalType for plate nodes, AddTemporalArc with an explicit lag order, separate
initial and temporal conditional probability tables, and SetNumberOfSlices for unrolling.
SetTemporalEvidence receives a time index and an integer outcome index. Temporal beliefs
are returned in a matrix whose adjacent entries correspond to outcomes within a slice. An
adapter must preserve those outcome indices, the distinction between initial and transition
distributions, lag order and the number of slices. A swapped state ordering would change the
meaning of the result while leaving a superficially valid array.(BayesFusion, LLC, 2024c)
  The maintained C++ library and its documented Java, Python and R wrappers are plausible
286                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


integration routes. They are not evidence that every wrapper exposes the same temporal
operations or numerical behavior. The inspected license distinguishes development from
deployment, including server and distributed-program deployment. Academic use has stated
eligibility and purpose restrictions. The appropriate proposal decision is to consider a licensed
local adapter for supplied-model inference, with wrapper parity and deployment terms checked
for the chosen configuration. Porting its proprietary engine is not an available open-source
reuse strategy. (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024j,k)


24.25.3     Automated temporal prediction and the meaning of “causal”

IBM’s Temporal Causal Models page says that the procedure constructs an autoregressive
model for each target and selects inputs from candidate series. It then explicitly defines “causal”
in this context as Granger causality: past values of another series improve prediction beyond
the target’s own past. It supports column-based series and a multidimensional representation
in which categorical dimensions distinguish series. The GUI can produce TCM MODEL syntax.
These are substantive workflow capabilities that the proposed local causal library does not
presently reproduce. (IBM, 2026a)
   The correct comparison is with automated predictive model selection. Representing many
branch series does not by itself establish the sampling law for a policy-effect interval, and
selecting a controllable predictor does not establish that changing it will change the target. The
inspected overview links time-interval, aggregation, missing-value and model-build options, but
the retrieved detailed routes did not return their technical content. Defaults for lag selection,
transformation and aggregation therefore remain unverified here. The overview is sufficient to
establish the procedure’s stated Granger meaning; it is insufficient for a full configuration or
performance comparison.
  Stata’s vargranger is similarly explicit. It performs equation-specific Wald tests that the
coefficients on another endogenous variable’s lags are jointly zero. When it follows a structural
VAR command, these tests still concern the underlying reduced-form VAR. A structural
command name does not change the null hypothesis of the postestimation test. (StataCorp,
2026c)
   The SAS/ETS 14.1 CAUSAL statement also documents Granger tests based on a VAR of the
variables listed in GROUP1 and GROUP2, with the order supplied by MODEL. It is not applicable
with order zero. Its example treats the group declarations as material to the fitted test.
An integration must therefore record the actual series in each test and its lag specification,
including whether a contextual variable was excluded. A request for “causality” cannot be
translated merely by matching it to a command named CAUSAL.(SAS Institute, 2026a)
  Consider an exact project counterexample. Let an unobserved liquidity factor follow

                       Ut = 45 Ut−1 + et ,     var(Ut ) = 1,              9
                                                               var(et ) = 25 ,

  with stationary Gaussian initialization. Set the observed rate deviation and next balance
deviation to

                              At = Ut + νt ,      Yt+1 = Ut + ηt+1 ,

  where all measurement innovations are independent, centered, and have variance one; they
are also independent of the factor innovations. Rates are measured in percentage points and
balances in USD millions. This is a stipulated law, not an estimated banking relationship.
Conditional on the single balance lag Yt ,
24.25. Commercial temporal models and intervention discovery                                  287



                          cov(Yt+1 , At | Yt ) = 1 − (4/5)2 /2 = 17/25,
                                 var(At | Yt ) = 2 − (4/5)2 /2 = 42/25.

   The population predictive coefficient is 17/42. Adding the observed rate reduces prediction
mean squared error from 42/25 to 59/42. Thus it is a useful predictor relative to this declared
one-lag baseline. Replacing only the equation for At changes neither Ut nor the equation
for Yt+1 ; the rate intervention effect is zero. Treating the predictive coefficient as an effect
would attribute 14 (17/42) = 17/168 million dollars of balances to a 25-basis-point action in
this example. No such causal increase occurs. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026g)
   This calculation neither reports a vendor false positive nor proves a failure of its documented
prediction task. It shows why a bank action requires an additional identifying argument. It
also keeps the conditioning history explicit: the displayed coefficient is for the stated one-lag
predictor comparison, not an unproved statement about every possible infinite-history test.


24.25.4     Structural restrictions and external instruments deserve separate
            credit

Stata’s svar is an intervention-relevant comparator beyond a Granger test. Its manual allows
user-specified short-run or long-run restrictions on structural impulse responses and explains
their economic motivation. The interface records lag choices, exogenous variables and constraint
matrices. It also documents a local-identification check and warns that a model that is not
structurally identified can nevertheless converge. Disabling that check must not be interpreted
by an adapter as scientific approval. (StataCorp, 2026e)
   ivsvar supplies another route. The inspected manual describes a GMM estimator for
a single target shock and a minimum-distance estimator for multiple target shocks. An
instrument is correlated with the target shock and uncorrelated with nontarget shocks. The
additional information identifies the relevant impact column up to its normalization; it does
not identify all other shocks. Multiple-target designs require further restrictions. The GMM
interface exposes robust, cluster and HAC variance options and an impact scale. These are
documented capabilities, not a claim that a noisy bank announcement or an arbitrary policy
date satisfies the instrument conditions.(StataCorp, 2026d)
  The distinction can be developed without relying on a software run. Suppose a two-variable
monthly reduced-form process for rate and balance deviations has
                                                        !                      !
                                               1/2 0                   1 1/2
               Xt = F Xt−1 + ut ,       F =            ,       Σu =          .
                                               1/5 1/2                1/2 1

   Its eigenvalues are both 1/2, so a stationary Gaussian law exists. Two structural representa-
tions have coefficient matrices
                                           !                          !
                                   1   0                    1 −1/2
                          D1 =           ,         D2 =            .
                                  −1/2 1                    0  1

   Writing Dj Xt = Dj F Xt−1 + εjt , the disturbance covariances are respectively diag(1, 3/4)
and diag(3/4, 1). Both yield exactly the same F , Σu and stationary observed process. They
disagree about the contemporaneous ordering: the first permits a within-month rate effect on
balances; the second orders the balance before the rate. The structural lag matrices also differ,
as required to preserve the same reduced form.
288                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Replace the rate equation once at month zero, raising its value by δ = 1/4 relative to the
paired baseline, and then restore the ordinary equations. Keep prior histories and disturbances
fixed in that comparison. The impact changes are (δ, δ/2)′ under the first structure and (δ, 0)′
under the second. Subsequent expected differences propagate by F h . The resulting balance
responses are:

                               Rate precedes balance, USD        Balance precedes rate, USD
  Month after the action                           million                           million
  0                                                  0.12500                            0.00000
  1                                                  0.11250                            0.05000
  2                                                  0.08125                            0.05000


   With an assumed monthly net margin of 0.2 percent on each incremental balance, no
discounting over these three months, and an assumed total action cost of USD 500, the values
are USD 137.50 and minus USD 300. Every input is a planning assumption. An exact symbolic
calculation checks both structural covariance factorizations, both response recursions and the
monetary conversion.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026g)
   The intervention is a single equation replacement. A policy maintaining the higher rate in
every month is a different sequence of replacements; it cannot be inferred by silently reusing
this impulse response. Likewise, a unit structural-shock response needs its shock normalization
and its relationship to the controllable rate stated explicitly. A valid external instrument could
provide information that distinguishes particular shock responses, but its validity is additional
evidence rather than a consequence of fitting this covariance.
   SAS’s inspected dynamic-simultaneous-equations discussion provides a related warning.
It describes a lower-triangular representation obtained from the innovation covariance and
exposes it through PRINT=(DYNAMIC). That is a documented model representation. A triangular
decomposition alone cannot choose the economically correct contemporaneous order in the
constructed example. The HTML extraction omitted some equation images, so this comparison
uses the surviving prose and command description; the displayed matrix derivation above is
independently specified project work. (SAS Institute, 2026b; Causal banking proposal project,
2026g)

24.25.5     Intensive longitudinal models and intervention analysis

Mplus’s version 8.1 addendum distinguishes DSEM, which regresses an outcome on its past,
from RDSEM, which places autoregression on the residual after contemporaneous predictors.
RDSEM is documented for a single series and two-level models. Its syntax examples use
CLUSTER, LAGGED, TYPE=TWOLEVEL RANDOM and ESTIMATOR=BAYES, with random slopes and
within/between components. The addendum also includes linear-trend examples and lagged
categorical outcomes. These are valuable alternatives for heterogeneous customer histories
and measurement processes. (Muthen and Muthen, 2018)
   The time grid matters to the observation law. The addendum warns that a covariate missing
at one or more time points can exclude an observation, including missingness arising with
TINTERVAL. It illustrates bringing that covariate into the model through an autoregression
so missing-data theory can be used. This changes the modeled system; it is not a universal
permission to fill irregular bank records. The analyst still needs a meaningful time unit, a
missingness argument, and assumptions about the mechanisms and random effects.
   For the proposal, Mplus is a model-fitting and heterogeneity comparator, with richer
longitudinal syntax than the current narrow local prototype. The inspected addendum does
24.25. Commercial temporal models and intervention discovery                                      289


not establish automatic discovery of a causal equivalence class, identification of an observational
policy intervention, or calibrated uncertainty over unknown causal structure. A posterior for
a supplied dynamic model and a confidence set covering alternative intervention structures
answer different questions. Regime changes and nonstationary mechanisms must be modeled
and checked explicitly; a trend example is not evidence that arbitrary regime drift is supported.
  BayesiaLab should also receive explicit causal credit. Its feature page distinguishes hard
and uncertain evidence from intervention analysis and names Graph Surgery and Likelihood
Matching as causal-estimation workflows. Its technical e-book section distinguishes identifi-
cation from estimation: identification requires a causal model or partial knowledge of data
generation, with the chapter expressing the assumptions in a DAG. The text states that more
observations cannot compensate for absent causal assumptions.(Bayesia, 2026j,i)
   These sources support an intervention-analysis comparator for an asserted model. They do
not, in the pages inspected here, establish a temporal discovery algorithm that learns lags, latent
confounding, contemporaneous equivalence classes and regime changes together. A candidate
integration would first check the exact edition/API operation, graph semantics, supported
identification route, and representation of an unavailable effect. Commercial capability must
not be inferred from a feature label, but the proposal must equally avoid claiming graph-based
intervention analysis as its exclusive innovation.


24.25.6     Frequency, common calendars and uncertainty belong in the inter-
            face

The transition coefficient changes with the sampling interval. For the constructed monthly
process, observing quarter-end stocks gives

                      3                              2              3      1/8  0
             X3k = F X3k−3 + u3k + F u3k−1 + F u3k−2 ,            F =              .
                                                                          3/20 1/8

   The monthly cross-lag coefficient is 1/5, while the quarter-end coefficient is 3/20, not three
times the monthly coefficient. The quarterly innovation covariance is Σu + F Σu F ′ + F 2 Σu (F 2 )′ .
Quarterly average balances or cash-flow totals would require a different observation operator.
The exact example checks this covariance both by recursion and by a block covariance
calculation.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026g)
   Consequently, an adapter must preserve whether a field is a stock, a flow, an average or an
end-of-period observation. It must also preserve timezone, release lag and policy availability.
Merely converting a monthly timestamp to a quarterly label can change both the statistical
model and the banking target. A proposed regime intervention must state which equations are
invariant and which may change, instead of assuming that a historical forecast carries over.
   Common calendars create a separate uncertainty issue. Suppose a single date’s errors
across twenty branches are C + ϵi , with common variance 1/2, independent branch variance
1/2, and independence between the two components. The variance of the branch mean
is 1/2 + 1/40 = 21/40. Incorrectly treating all twenty errors as independent gives 1/20,
understating variance by a factor of 21/2. This is a specified example, not an estimated
correction for bank data. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026g)
   A package can expose cluster or HAC options, as the inspected Stata instrumental-SVAR
interface does, while the analyst still has to justify the chosen asymptotic units and dependence
assumptions. A collection of branch models is not automatically a collection of independent
calendars. Neither a Granger-test level nor a posterior interval in one supplied graph becomes
a simultaneous uncertainty guarantee over searched lags, selected models, alternative graphs
290                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


and intervention effects.

Reproducing every commercial estimator would add cost without demonstrating that the

prerequisites for writing this proposal. Until the evidence is available, the recommendation
remains a documented shortlist with the missing comparisons visible.


24.26      Temporal order, dynamic prediction and intervention
           regimes in R
A treasury analyst may ask which funding action today improves tomorrow’s contribution,
while a monitoring analyst asks which variables forecast tomorrow’s shortfall. The same
rectangular file can support both questions, but the required information differs. A row might
be an independent institution with variables measured at three waves, a daily observation from
one institution, or an observation under a known experimental regime. A tier orders variables
within a row; a lag relates rows; a regime describes how a mechanism changes. Giving these
objects distinct types is the first requirement for a useful R interface.
   The inherited pcalg pathway covers an important part of this territory. Its GIES interface
estimates an interventional essential graph, using intervention targets and a row-to-target index.
An empty target represents observation without intervention. The returned representative
DAG is one member of the estimated class. It must not silently become the uniquely established
mechanism. Likewise, an undirected essential-graph edge represents alternative directions
across DAGs: a plotting convention that renders it with two arrowheads does not turn it into
a latent-confounding PAG edge. FCI-JCI instead augments system variables with context
variables and explicitly selects context assumptions, including exogeneity and, when invoked,
absence of latent confounding between contexts and the system. A month-end dummy does not
establish these assumptions merely by being supplied to the API. These are distinct statistical
specifications, even though both can combine data from multiple regimes. (pcalg contributors,
2026; pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a)


24.26.1     Ordering variables is different from modelling a series

The inspected causalDisco 1.2.1 interface exposes TPC, TFCI and TGES with tiered back-
ground knowledge. Its examples of temporally ordered variables describe a useful cohort-wave
application: measurements at an earlier wave cannot be caused by measurements at a later
wave under the declared clock. That restriction does not supply stationarity, equal time
intervals, independent observations or a valid conditional-independence test for dependent
292                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


rows. The selected TPC/TFCI implementation wraps pcalg operations and converts their
results through caugi. The method name therefore describes a proposed workflow entry point,
not a complete uncertainty contract. (causalDisco contributors, 2026)
  Two details require qualification before conversion. First, the pinned TFCI help describes
a PAG stored with class UNKNOWN because native PAG support is unavailable, whereas
the runner in that same revision requests class PAG from the caugi constructor. The TPC
help describes a PDAG while its runner requests UNKNOWN. These are observed source/doc-
umentation disagreements; without the matching dependency and a runtime inspection we
cannot assert the actual returned class or whether conversion succeeds. The proposed adapter
should preserve the original endpoint matrix and labels, record the effective constructor and
dependency version, and refuse an unsupported conversion. Reading an UNKNOWN tag as
an ordinary undirected graph would discard scientifically relevant information. (causalDisco
contributors, 2026)
   Second, the tier-aware test wrapper returns zero without calling the underlying test when
a proposed conditioning variable is later than both endpoints. This sentinel prevents that
forbidden conditioning set from removing an edge. It is not an observed p-value of zero. A
diagnostic screen that reports every returned number as a statistical test would misstate the
evidence. The interface must distinguish a test executed on data from a restriction imposed by
declared knowledge, just as it distinguishes an oriented arrow from a fitted coefficient. TFCI’s
source places an arrowhead at the later endpoint of a cross-tier edge; it does not thereby
prove the earlier endpoint is an unconfounded causal parent. The remaining endpoint and the
equivalence-class semantics must survive export. (causalDisco contributors, 2026)
   The separate tpc 1.0 package is a useful comparator. Its API specifies a partial node order,
forbidden edges and global or tier-specific context variables, returning a pcalg-style pcAlgo
object. Its source forces particular context adjacencies and removes others; supplied forbidden
edges can override those context constraints with a reported conflict. Thus labelling a business
variable as context can insert substantive structure rather than simply add a column to the data.
A reviewer should see the effective constraints after precedence rules, their business rationale
and which arrows follow only from those constraints. This tpc package and causalDisco’s
TPC pathway have different package identities; their names alone establish neither identical
implementations nor identical scientific behavior. (tpc contributors, 2023)
   For cohort applications, we would first use such tools as comparators with independent
subjects and an explicit measurement order. Repeated accounts sharing calendar shocks require
an additional sampling argument. For example, suppose 100 banks have residual Rit = Ct
on each of 20 dates, with independent mean-zero, variance-one Ct across dates. The grand
mean is the mean of the 20 calendar shocks. Its variance is 1/20, whereas an independent-row
formula using 2,000 rows gives 1/2000. The standard errors differ by a factor of ten. This
exact special case does not assign a universal effective sample size to panels. It demonstrates
why adding a time ordering to graph search cannot repair a wrong replication unit. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026an)


24.26.2    Dynamic Bayesian networks and admissible rows

dbnR 0.8.0 provides a different route: Gaussian dynamic Bayesian-network learning with an
explicit number of unrolled slices. Its size argument includes the present slice, so size two
corresponds to one historical lag. The structure wrapper permits a previously folded data
set through f_dt and forwards it to the selected search method; the reviewed wrapper does
not by itself establish the guarantees of each downstream search engine. This is a promising
prediction and lag-construction baseline. A learned DBN or a Gaussian conditional forecast
24.26. Temporal order, dynamic prediction and intervention regimes in R                        293


still requires causal assumptions before it supports an intervention query. (dbnR contributors,
2026)
   The data preparation source supplies a concrete safeguard worth reusing. Ordinary fold_dt
shifts rows and removes incomplete leading rows. filter_same_cycle compares the identifiers
across slices, and filtered_fold_dt combines folding with that filter. The integration obligation
is to select the appropriate pathway, supply the correct identifiers, and verify the rows it
produces. The selected functions do not establish chronological sorting or equal physical
intervals from timestamps. Equal bank identifiers are necessary but insufficient for a one-day
lag when days are missing. (dbnR contributors, 2026)
   Consider the deliberately small table of bank A values 1, 2, 3 on days 1, 2, 3, followed by bank
B values 101, 102, 103 on the same three days. Positional one-lag folding produces five pairs,
including the invalid transition from bank A’s last observation to bank B’s first. Requiring
equal bank identity and a one-day increment retains four pairs. Conversely, two observations
from bank A on days one and three pass an identity-only filter but do not form a one-day
transition. These are exact constructions of required adapter behavior, not reports of running
dbnR or demonstrations that its documented ID filter fails. (Causal banking proposal, 2026an)
   The same source contains reduce_freq, which averages batches whose size is the ceiling
of the requested interval divided by the current interval, with optional identifier grouping.
A physical-calendar adapter must consequently record the achieved spacing and aggregation
convention, especially when the ratio is noninteger or timestamps are irregular. Averaging is
not merely a computational reduction: it changes the variables and potentially the estimand.
(dbnR contributors, 2026)
  An exact daily example makes the change visible. Let the action At be independent
Rademacher variables, taking values minus one and one with equal probability, and let the
outcome be Yt = At−1 . At the daily scale the structural response is a one-day lag. With
nonoverlapping two-day averages,
                                 A2k−1 + A2k              A2k−2 + A2k−1
                         Āk =               ,    Ȳk =                 .
                                      2                         2
Independence gives Var(Āk ) = 1/2, while both Cov(Āk , Ȳk ) and Cov(Āk−1 , Ȳk ) equal 1/4.
Because successive action-block averages are independent, the population linear projection
of Ȳk on current and previous action-block averages has coefficients one half and one half. A
daily lag thus appears at both current and previous block positions. (Causal banking proposal,
2026an)
   Even the meaning of an intervention on a block average is incomplete without its within-
block timing. Increasing the first day’s action by two changes the current action average by
one and the current outcome average by one. Increasing the second day’s action by two makes
the same change to the current action average, but changes the next outcome average by
one instead. These perturbations have identical aggregate action size and different response
timing. A service cannot answer an aggregate-action query with a unique response path until
it specifies which intervention is intended. The source data, aggregation map, information
clock and action policy all belong in the request identity. (Causal banking proposal, 2026an)


24.26.3     Invariant prediction: the exact scope of the guarantee

seqICP 1.1 targets a response’s invariant parents rather than returning a complete temporal
graph. Its linear API distinguishes an iid model from an autoregressive model; lag order
may be supplied or selected up to a maximum by AIC. It also provides a nonlinear interface
with an additive iid-noise model and a regression function intended to approximate the
294                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


target relation. These alternatives require different justification. The manuals explicitly warn
that reducing max.parents below the predictor count sacrifices the stated confidence-interval
coverage, and that the default early stop when the accepted intersection is empty loses coverage
for coefficient values different from zero. The source also distinguishes an empty intersection
from modelReject, which records rejection of every tested model. Both can display an empty
parent set, yet communicate different evidence. (seqICP contributors, 2017)
   The genuine sequential-invariance original explains why these distinctions matter. Its
Definition 2.1 assumes a fixed linear Gaussian target relation with iid innovations, and its
causal interpretation additionally requires structural independence conditions. Suppose S ∗ is
the invariant true parent set and A is the family of accepted candidate sets. The estimator
     T
Sb = S∈A S, with the declared empty-family convention, satisfies

                                        Pr(Sb ⊆ S ∗ ) ≥ 1 − α

when the relevant tests have the required level. If the true set is accepted, its presence in
the intersection ensures containment; erroneous inclusion of a nonparent therefore requires
rejecting that true set. This is a guarantee against false included parents, not a guarantee of
recovering every parent, selecting the whole graph, or covering an intervention value with a
numerical interval. Failure to discover an edge is not a certificate that its effect is zero. (Pfister
et al., 2017)
   Section 6 of that original adds the past p lags of all variables to each candidate regression and
targets instantaneous parents under a fixed linear Gaussian higher-order Markov relation. The
level statement is given as the Monte Carlo resampling count B tends to infinity. It does not
justify calling the package’s finite default B = 100 an exact finite-simulation guarantee. The
paper explicitly discusses lag selection and post-selection difficulties; one proposed alternative
considers multiple lag choices with a multiplicity adjustment. AIC is a useful operational
option, but its mere availability does not remove that inferential issue. Moreover, Remark 3.2
labels the residual permutation extension to nonlinear or non-Gaussian settings heuristic. We
must not borrow the linear fixed-lag theorem for every supplied nonlinear regressor. (Pfister
et al., 2017; seqICP contributors, 2017)
   Invariance also changes the usual conversation about stationarity. A stable target mechanism
can coexist with changes elsewhere in the system; those changes may help rule out incorrect
parent sets. Full-system stationarity is not a universal desirable prerequisite for this route. A
bank policy revision that directly changes the target mechanism, however, can violate the very
invariance being tested. The specification should name which mechanisms may change, which
remain fixed, how blocks or smoothing comparisons are chosen, and whether calendar shocks
enter the innovation or observed predictors. An invariant coefficient fit under an unjustified
partition cannot establish that these declarations are true. (Pfister et al., 2017)


24.26.4     A funding counterexample and integration choices

Temporal precedence and excellent prediction remain insufficient for the funding question.
Let Ct and Et be mutually independent Rademacher sequences, with the calendar driver
Ct unobserved. In both of two worlds the recorded action is At = Ct . In the first world,
Yt+1 = 2Ct + Et+1 ; in the second, Yt+1 = 2At + Et+1 . Their complete stationary observed
processes agree: each daily pair (At , Yt+1 ) takes (−1, −3), (−1, −1), (1, 1), (1, 3) with probability
one quarter. Conditional forecasting and temporal order cannot distinguish the worlds. Yet
replacing the action equation with At = 1 versus At = −1 changes expected next-day outcome
by zero in the first world and four in the second. If the outcome is stipulated to be thousands
of dollars of funding contribution and that action change costs one thousand dollars, the
24.27. Python discovery across clocks, contexts and interventions                            295


net consequences are minus one and plus three thousand dollars. These values illustrate
a missing-information decision, not an estimate of bank return. (Causal banking proposal,
2026an)
  The example is intentionally elementary. The practical implication is a typed pipeline:
separate graph candidates, predictive responses, identified effect sets and monetary scenarios.
Preserve interventions as mechanism changes rather than row labels; retain lag direction,
contemporaneous endpoints, measurement frequency, within-period timing, regime membership
and shared-calendar structure. Return unknown when the requested effect lacks identification,
and preserve model rejection, unsupported conversion and insufficient test precision as different
reasons. A graph with plausible arrows should not bypass these checks. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026am)
   Our proposed reuse choice is conditional integration of causalDisco for tiered graph ex-
ploration, dbnR for checked lag/forecast baselines, and seqICP for a declared target-parent
invariance service. The separate tpc and inherited pcalg paths remain reference comparators.
No adapter is enabled by this comparison. Direct adoption waits for dependency rights, pinned
execution and semantic qualification; porting is not selected because it would add a second
implementation before the original contract is understood. Declared licenses are GPL-2 for the
inspected causalDisco release, GPL-3 for dbnR and seqICP, and GPL version three or later for
tpc. Their dependency and distribution obligations need a separate review; a process boundary
is not assumed to settle those questions. (causalDisco contributors, 2026; dbnR contributors,
2026; seqICP contributors, 2017; tpc contributors, 2023; Causal banking proposal, 2026am)
   A useful first prototype can use public data for measurement conventions and generated
mechanisms for known truth. Predeclare tests for separate-series boundaries, irregular calendars,
aggregation timing, graph-endpoint round trips, forced context constraints, all-rejected models,
lag selection and finite simulation settings. Compare a prediction-only baseline with correctly
declared and deliberately misspecified causal requests, keeping refusals and failures in the
denominator. The original R engines must actually run before we claim runtime behavior or
measured accuracy. Further screening should cover additional nonlinear and mixed-frequency
methods and the tsGFCI/Tetrad interface family; the bounded repository-name search did not
resolve that family’s R route. None of these local omissions blocks developing the remaining
proposal areas. (Causal banking proposal, 2026am)


24.27       Python discovery across clocks, contexts and interven-
            tions
A bank comparing discovery libraries must first say what changed in its data. A funding-
rate movement can be a decision, a response to a common calendar shock, a change in the
mechanism setting that rate, or simply the next observation of a persistent process. These
possibilities require different inputs and support different conclusions. A library accepting
several data matrices does not, by that fact, identify an intervention; a time-series library
does not recover the physical clock from a row number. This comparison therefore separates
temporal search, context and regime search, and discovery from labelled or partially known
interventions. The proposed service should return the relevant graph object and assumptions
before attempting an effect query. The reuse decisions below are proposed adapter and research
choices, with no enabled integration or upstream execution established by this review. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ak)
296                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


24.27.1     The structural object and its decision horizon

Write a linear structural time-series model using column vectors as
                                                p
                                                X
                                 xt = B0 xt +         Bℓ xt−ℓ + εt .
                                                ℓ=1

Here Bℓ [j, i] is the coefficient from variable i at lag ℓ to variable j now. The within-period
matrix B0 describes an acyclic ordering, while the lag matrices allow feedback through
time. Premultiplying by (I − B0 )−1 gives reduced-form coefficients Φℓ = (I − B0 )−1 Bℓ and
reduced-form innovations (I − B0 )−1 εt . A forecasting coefficient, a structural coefficient and
an impulse response are thus different quantities even in this small model. Identifying the
contemporaneous structure needs additional restrictions. The DYNOTEARS paper studies
independent realisations of a stationary series with independent innovations, and discusses
non-Gaussian innovations or standard Gaussian innovations as identifiable cases. Its within-
slice acyclicity condition does not itself establish stability of the dynamic process. (Pamfil
et al., 2020)
  For an exact banking illustration let the two coordinates be standardized funding pressure
and liquidity contribution, and stipulate
                             !                            !                         !
                       0 0                   1/2 0                         1/2 0
              B0 =          ,        B1 =            ,             Φ1 =            .
                      1/2 0                  1/4 1/2                       1/2 1/2

The direct lagged funding coefficient in the second equation is 1/4; the reduced-form counterpart
is 1/2. A unit innovation to the funding equation, with zero initial deviations, produces
immediate deviations (1, 1/2)T . The next two liquidity responses are 3/4 and 5/8. Since both
eigenvalues of Φ1 are 1/2, the infinite-horizon sum is

                                 (I − Φ1 )−1 (1, 1/2)T = (2, 3)T .

If each liquidity unit is valued at a stipulated USD 100 and the one-time action costs USD
60, the immediate net is minus USD 10 whereas the undiscounted cumulative net is USD
240. These are conditional arithmetic examples. They do not estimate a bank return, and
changing the action to a sustained rate policy, adding discounting, or allowing feedback into the
decision rule changes the target. A reusable interface must therefore distinguish an innovation,
an equation replacement and a sustained policy, and retain the horizon and units. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026al)
   Sampling frequency is equally substantive. Consider two stationary Gaussian processes
Xt = ρXt−1 + ϵt , with independent innovations of variance 3/4 and ρ equal to either 1/2 or
−1/2. Both have marginal variance one. If the bank retains only every second day, both
satisfy an observed autoregression with coefficient 1/4 and innovation variance 15/16. Their
complete stationary observed laws agree, but their one-day impulse responses have opposite
signs. Recovering the original day-level response is therefore impossible from this coarsened
law alone within this two-world comparison. A daily timestamp declaration cannot repair
information that was discarded; the response must retain the observation frequency and the
unresolved finer-clock target. (Causal banking proposal, 2026al)


24.27.2     Tigramite: three distinct questions behind one ecosystem

Tigramite offers a useful primary family of proposed adapters because its documented graph
classes distinguish PCMCI, PCMCI+, LPCMCI, RPCMCI and J-PCMCI+. PCMCI+ com-
bines lagged and contemporaneous search under causal stationarity and sufficiency, while
24.27. Python discovery across clocks, contexts and interventions                             297


LPCMCI retains the partial ancestral graph needed when latent confounding is admitted.
Neither endpoint ambiguity nor the restrictions of the chosen conditional-independence test
should disappear in a common wrapper. Earlier selected installed operations are separate evi-
dence from this static extension review. (Runge, 2020; Gerhardus and Runge, 2020; tigramite
contributors, 2026; jakobrunge/tigramite contributors, 2026)
   J-PCMCI+ addresses multiple datasets with system variables and temporal or spatial
contexts. Its primary paper requires a joint acyclic structural model, context exogeneity,
restrictions excluding context–system confounding, complete observation of system nodes, and
a particular context-determinism construction. A temporal context is shared across datasets; a
spatial context is constant within a dataset. This offers a route for common funding calendars
and bank-specific characteristics, but does not license arbitrary unobserved common causes.
Coding a bank identifier or calendar as a context is a scientific assertion about the model.
(Günther et al., 2023)
   The inspected implementation makes those assertions operational: it accepts five node classes,
orients context-to-system links as exogenous, and removes specified reverse and dummy links.
A generic graph adapter must preserve the effective constraints after these transformations,
the pooled datasets, time offsets, masks and conditioning choices. Before enabling this
candidate, generated comparisons should separately vary shared-calendar dependence, bank-
specific fixed contexts and hidden system-to-system confounding. The last case deliberately
violates this J-PCMCI+ model and should not be used to award it a latent-variable guarantee.
The raw conditional-test results and final endpoint graph should remain distinguishable.
(jakobrunge/tigramite contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ak)
   RPCMCI answers a different question: it alternates regime learning and causal search
under a finite persistent regime structure, with stationarity within regimes. Its paper initially
develops lagged structural relations with independent stationary innovations. A recovered
regime can describe different behaviour without representing a randomized or externally
assigned intervention. In the inspected constructor, only one multivariate series with scalar
rather than vector-valued nodes is accepted and a supplied mask is replaced by an all-false
mask; missing values have a separate flag. The adapter must either reject an unsupported user
mask or require an explicit, reviewed transformation before calling this path. It must retain
the regime count, transition limit, annealing settings and convergence information. Regime
membership should not be exported as an observed experiment label. (Saggioro et al., 2020;
jakobrunge/tigramite contributors, 2026)
   Tigramite’s preserved root terms specify GPLv3 and its README declares version 3 or later.
That is useful source evidence for a reuse decision, but a process boundary or command-line
interface is not, by itself, a completed distribution-rights analysis. The proposal should compare
a versioned adapter with the cost of independently maintaining a port and qualifying its
numerical equivalence. The immediate recommendation is separate, explicitly scoped adapters
for the different temporal methods. (jakobrunge/tigramite contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal, 2026ak)


24.27.3     CausalAI, VARLiNGAM and DYNOTEARS as contrasting base-
            lines

Salesforce CausalAI’s inspected PC and Granger paths enumerate candidate parents at strictly
negative lags. Its VARLiNGAM wrapper separately exposes lag-zero coefficients, preserving
the dependency’s target-row convention. The time-series data helper forms lagged observations
inside each supplied array and then concatenates those slices, which avoids simply linking
the last row of one array to the first of another. However, the selected interface has no
298                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


physical timestamp argument: a missing business day and a regular one-step transition can
look identical after the caller has formed the arrays. Its optional complete-case deletion also
does not establish an ignorable missingness law. (salesforce/causalai contributors, 2025)
  The uncertainty interface deserves particular caution. The inspected Granger routine fits
LassoCV coefficients and then evaluates a t-tail expression using a residual sum of squares
and inverse design cross-product. The source does not establish the additional justification
needed after selection and under dependent observations. When the cross-product is rank-
deficient, that routine substitutes a vector of p-values equal to one; the VARLiNGAM wrapper
has a similar branch. An operational refusal is then numerically indistinguishable from a
valid large p-value if the wrapper discards the diagnostic. The proposal should preserve a
separate uncertainty unavailable status, effective sample/design rank and the selected model.
A successful coefficient fit is insufficient evidence for a calibrated interval or a causal graph.
These are static-source findings, with no claimed runtime failure frequency. (salesforce/causalai
contributors, 2025)
   The inherited direct LiNGAM inspection provides a clearer starting point for a declared
linear non-Gaussian structural model: fit the lag process, discover contemporaneous structure in
its residuals, and preserve B[target, predictor]. Its residual bootstrap reconstructs a sequence,
unlike the generic row bootstrap, but the inspected bootstrap loop fixes the lag-selection
criterion to None. Consequently its existence does not establish uncertainty including lag-order
selection. Before an adapter is enabled, the proposed generated study must include Gaussian
innovations, hidden common causes and persistent residuals as explicit scope violations,
alongside the eligible non-Gaussian innovation cases. (LiNGAM project, 2026a; cdt15/lingam,
2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ak)
   DYNOTEARS supplies a simultaneous optimization comparator. The inspected CausalNex
path minimizes a penalized residual loss based on X(I − W ) − Xlags A and constrains the
within-slice matrix W to be acyclic. Its dataframe transformer checks numeric columns and
sorted integer indices, splits gaps larger than one, and constructs lags separately for each
resulting realisation. This is more specific than assuming that every row is adjacent. It still
admits a nondecreasing sequence with duplicate indices: the authored sequence (1, 2, 2, 3, 6, 7)
creates two segments and four retained one-lag pairs, only three of which have a strictly positive
unit step. The proposed adapter must reject duplicates, define the calendar and record every
exclusion. It should also preserve raw weights, threshold choices and optimization diagnostics.
(mckinsey/causalnex contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026al; Pamfil et al., 2020)
   The inherited maintenance review records CausalNex’s discontinuation notice. That supports
retaining DYNOTEARS as a methodological and conversion reference, while deferring default
dependency adoption. A port would require an explicit maintenance owner and equivalence
tests; it is not a free substitute for a maintained upstream package. CausalAI’s inspected
BSD terms and LiNGAM’s inspected MIT terms likewise do not certify their entire resolved
dependency environments. (mckinsey/causalnex, 2026b; salesforce/causalai contributors, 2025;
cdt15/lingam, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ak)


24.27.4     Intervention data need a mechanism contract

An intervention label must include the target set, mechanism type and assignment context.
To see why, let H, U, W be independent standard normal innovations, define A = H + U ,
Y = 2A + H + W , and observe (H, A, Y ). A perfect stochastic intervention replaces the action
equation with A = δ + Z, where Z ∼ N (0, 2) is independent of the other innovations. A soft
intervention instead sets A = H + U + δ. In both cases E(A) = δ, var(A) = 2, and E(Y ) = 2δ.
Nevertheless, cov(H, A) is zero under replacement and one under the soft change; cov(A, Y ) is
24.27. Python discovery across clocks, contexts and interventions                            299


respectively four and five. The action margin and its label alone cannot tell the library which
graph truncation is justified. If H is hidden, the same example additionally violates a causally
sufficient observed-variable model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026al)
   Python GIES is a useful known-perfect-intervention baseline. The original paper defines
stochastic interventions by replacing targeted mechanisms and requires a conservative target
family: every variable remains unintervened in at least one environment. Observational data
satisfy this particular requirement, although they do not supply all other assumptions. The
paper’s interventional equivalence theory concerns graph classes under the stated intervention
family. Independent observations from several environments are not automatically the same
sampling model as repeatedly observed banks on a shared calendar. (Hauser and Bühlmann,
2012)
   The inspected Python Gaussian score centres data within each environment, forms co-
variances from observations in which the target variable was not intervened on, and checks
conservative target coverage. Its output is an estimated I-essential graph: reciprocal nonzero
matrix entries denote an undirected edge, not a two-cycle. A proposed adapter should validate
unique target indices, dataset/target alignment, environment sizes and the effective score before
preserving these endpoints. It should refuse to present the score as an effect or confidence
interval. This candidate is attractive for a transparent generated perfect-intervention compari-
son; soft targets and dependent panels need their own justified treatment. (juangamella/gies
contributors, 2025; Causal banking proposal, 2026ak)
   Unknown-target IGSP offers another route when intervention targets are partially known.
Its primary paper requires observational data and an I-faithfulness condition relating invariance
to separation; its theorem identifies an interventional equivalence class and targets under those
conditions. The algorithm needs both a conditional-independence tester and a conditional-
invariance tester. An unknown target is therefore not recovered merely by dropping a target
column from a known-target method. (Squires et al., 2020)
   The pinned CausalDAG facade reexports external graph and learning packages, while its
older tutorial points to an implementation path absent from the selected tree. The recovered
graphical-model-learning implementation defaults to depth four, five starts, and tuple scoring.
Its default score orders edge count and variant count lexicographically, whereas the inspected
paper defines their sum. The distinction can matter: candidate counts (3, 5) and (4, 0) are
ordered in opposite ways by these rules. This arithmetic example does not claim those
two candidates are reachable in a particular search. It identifies a precise theory-to-code
question that must be resolved before transferring the theorem to a wrapper’s default. A
public prototype should pin all three facade dependencies, retain score mode and search
restrictions, and compare oracle-level and finite-test behaviour separately. (uhlerlab/causaldag
contributors, 2022; uhlerlab/graphical_model_learning contributors, 2022; Squires et al., 2020;
Causal banking proposal, 2026al)


24.27.5     Differentiable discovery: optimization and evidence remain separate

DCDI’s primary score theorem concerns a global population optimum with a sufficient density
class, positivity, finite entropy and I-faithfulness. Its finite nonconvex optimization is not
guaranteed to attain that optimum. The inspected constructor implements perfect interven-
tions with known or unknown targets and imperfect interventions with known targets; the
combination of imperfect interventions and unknown targets explicitly raises an unimplemented
error. Known perfect targets are removed from the mechanism likelihood using a retention
mask, while the other implemented branches use regime-specific parameters. These distinctions
should be visible service variants, with the original masks, regime identities and optimizer
300                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


diagnostics returned in the evidence bundle. They should not be compressed into one boolean
intervention option. (Brouillard et al., 2020; slachapelle/dcdi contributors, 2022)
   ENCO provides a contrasting parameterization of edge existence and orientation. Its
documented array format indexes intervention samples by the single targeted variable. The
inspected gradient path suppresses incoming-edge updates at that variable and treats orientation
updates separately. The primary theorem and supporting argument require informative
interventions, sufficiently accurate conditional models, suitable regularization and the stated
data conditions. The paper itself distinguishes the extension to fewer intervention targets, for
which the same convergence guarantee is unavailable. A comparison should report actual target
coverage and cycle handling instead of treating the method’s title or learned edge probabilities
as a finite-sample confidence guarantee. (phlippe/ENCO contributors, 2022; Lippe et al., 2022)
  SDCD is worth considering for numerical stability and its two-stage structure. The primary
paper’s stability result concerns the acyclicity constraint; its first-stage screening argument
uses exact population optimization and explicit model, faithfulness and positivity conditions.
Neither result establishes that every finite training run retains every true parent. The inspected
output helper sorts weighted edges and omits those that would form cycles. A caller receiving
only that DAG loses the distinction between a learned low-weight edge and an edge removed to
impose acyclicity. The proposal should return raw adjacency, the retained graph, the threshold
and a record of the removed edges. (Nazaret et al., 2024; azizilab/sdcd contributors, 2024)
   There is also a concrete input risk. SDCD’s inspected dataset helper maps unmatched
perturbation labels to a sentinel, drops those entries, and turns an empty target list into an
all-ones retention mask. In the authored two-variable example, the label rate gives mask
(0, 1) but the misspelling raet gives (1, 1). This traces the selected transformation; it is not
an observed frequency in user data. The proposed wrapper must distinguish an explicitly
observational record from an unresolved target, validate all labels before conversion, and
refuse unknown or duplicate targets with the original input preserved. Successful optimization
after an unintended input reinterpretation would not resolve the mistake. (azizilab/sdcd
contributors, 2024; Causal banking proposal, 2026al)


24.27.6     A bounded reuse portfolio and the next evidence

The immediate portfolio has distinct roles. Tigramite supports proposed endpoint-preserving
temporal/context adapters; LiNGAM and DYNOTEARS supply declared linear structural
comparators; CausalAI provides an additional interface and benchmark reference with explicit
uncertainty restrictions. Python GIES supplies a transparent known-perfect intervention
baseline. UT-IGSP adds an invariance-based unknown-target comparison once its scoring and
dependencies are reconciled. DCDI, ENCO and SDCD provide complementary neural research
comparators, each restricted to its reviewed data and intervention contract. Direct adoption is
deferred; no port is selected merely because source terms permit modification. A port must
justify its maintenance and numerical-equivalence cost against a versioned adapter. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ak)
   The first prototype can use generated structural laws with known graphs, observed inter-
vention assignments and saved observation clocks. Separate strata should vary lag order,
contemporaneous links, hidden common causes, shared calendars, regime persistence, regular
versus coarsened sampling, target knowledge and perfect versus soft intervention. Eligible and
deliberately ineligible cases must be reported separately. Software acceptance cases should
include duplicate clocks, unknown target spelling, rank failure, an unsupported RPCMCI
mask, an unsupported DCDI combination, raw-to-DAG conversion and the UT-IGSP score
switch. These cases test whether the adapter preserves or refuses meaning; they cannot by
24.28. Java temporal discovery: clocks, regimes and the meaning of a learned network         301


themselves establish statistical recovery. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ak,al)
   A matched scientific comparison must then keep each method’s assumptions, search budgets
and target objects explicit. A selected DAG cannot be ranked against a PAG as though
every unresolved endpoint were an error. Report coverage of eligible requests, refusals, graph
and intervention-target errors, downstream identified effects or ambiguity, runtime and full
preparation costs. For dependent series, use a design justified for that process rather than
an independent-row bootstrap by default. Public datasets can test ingestion and observable
diagnostics; unless they supply independently credible intervention truth, they cannot award
causal correctness by agreement between algorithms. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ak)
   This is a developed comparison, not a complete census. The bounded search retains
unresolved families including amortized discovery, subsampled proxy methods, periodic/nonsta-
tionary discovery, Bayesian unknown-intervention methods and event-process methods. CUTS
and CD-NOD aliases still need primary identity and embedded implementation resolution.
Their unresolved status is an evidence gap, not evidence that the capability is absent. Further
work should acquire the original methods and implementation paths, classify their clock and
intervention assumptions, and compare their marginal contribution against this portfolio.
These follow-ups can proceed independently of prototype qualification and whole-manuscript
acceptance. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ak)


24.28      Java temporal discovery: clocks, regimes and the mean-
           ing of a learned network
A treasury analyst may have thousands of branch observations but only a few distinct funding-
shock dates. A package can turn these observations into a lagged network without answering
whether changing a deposit offer improves next-day net funding. A Java backend must preserve
three different objects: the observation clock, the statistical model fitted to the observations,
and the intervention whose consequence matters. Confusing them can produce a plausible
diagram with an incorrect economic interpretation.
   The comparison develops six repository routes: Tetrad, a modified BANJO distribution,
Weka’s forecasting package, learnDBN, learnDBM and BayesNetBuilder. The two learn-
ing repositories share substantial code; these are not six independent algorithm families.
Selected historical revisions through 7 October 2026 support the discussion, without estab-
lishing a complete Java census. Tetrad offers a candidate for a restricted graph adapter.
Discrete dynamic-network learners provide another modeling route, while Weka supplies a
forecasting and preprocessing comparison. Their scientific acceptance conditions differ. (cmu-
phil/tetrad, 2026d; daniel-315/slingshot-modified-banjo, 2026b; Waikato/weka-3.8, 2022b;
SSamDav/learnDBN, 2020; SSamDav/learnDBM, 2020; selrach/BayesNetBuilder, 2011)


24.28.1     The observation clock and the population

Let i index a branch or customer series, t a physical event date, Ait the action available at
that date, and Yi,t+h the funding outcome at horizon h. An effect for a typical customer, an
effect for a typical branch, and a bank-wide monetary total require different weights. The
information set must contain only values available when the decision is taken. A later-revised
balance cannot silently become a decision-time covariate. A lag of one row also needs a declared
relationship to the physical horizon.
   Tetrad’s inspected TsUtils.createLagData creates a matrix with n − L rows and p(L + 1)
columns from n rows, p variables and maximum lag L. Output row r at lag ℓ takes its value
302                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


from input row r + L − ℓ. Temporal tiers order the lagged variables. This method has no
physical timestamp or subject-boundary argument and reserves the colon in variable names for
lag notation. An external clock and identity validator is therefore necessary: the constructed
tiers do not establish the meaning of the original row order. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d)
  For dates (0, 1, 4, 5), positional lagging yields (0, 1), (1, 4), (4, 5). Only two pairs represent a
one-day transition. The middle pair includes a three-day gap. Two independent series (1, 2, 3)
and (10, 20, 30) likewise provide four within-series transitions. Concatenating first adds 3 → 10,
which corresponds to no observed history. These are exact bookkeeping examples, not findings
about a bank dataset. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aw)
  The adapter should construct admissible windows before dispatch or refuse a clock it
cannot represent. It should retain event time, availability time, series identity, gap policy
and aggregation rule. An inserted missing row is different from an observed zero; carrying
a balance forward is a modeling choice. Resampling or aggregating to regular dates changes
the information supplied to discovery and needs justification. For branches sharing a market
shock, protecting series boundaries does not establish independence. (Causal banking proposal,
2026av)


24.28.2     Tetrad: temporal infrastructure and its limits

The inspected September 2026 Tetrad snapshot’s FCI wrapper constructs lagged data, supplies
the selected conditional-independence test, and passes knowledge, replication and other settings
to the FCI core. IMaGES lags each dataset separately, constructs component scores and
invokes BOSS permutation search. A lag parameter does not transfer every temporal-discovery
theorem to every test, sampling law and graph class. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d)
   A saved SvarFCI help page describes time order, homologous edge removal under a repeated
structure, and contemporaneous connections unless forbidden by knowledge. It distinguishes
that contemporaneous allowance from assumptions of the research it references. The current
wrapper inspected here invokes the FCI core. The help page and wrapper cannot serve
interchangeably as proof of a specialized algorithm. The earlier static FCI review’s possible-
DSEP and orientation findings remain relevant; adding lag columns does not repair them.
Qualification must match the algorithm, test, representation and assumptions. (cmu-phil/tetrad,
2026d,c)
   Graph storage requires equal care. The inspected TimeLagGraph.addEdge accepts directed
edges, checks selected temporal conditions and propagates repeated edges over lags. The
separate addDirectedEdge delegates directly to the underlying graph without using that
validation path. A container’s name therefore cannot guarantee that every mutation enforces
the same conditions. A directed time-lag container also cannot losslessly represent an arbitrary
PAG: circles, latent confounding marks and unresolved orientations have meanings that a
directed completion would remove. Validate the actual entry point and preserve a typed graph
before creating a simplified display. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d; Causal banking proposal, 2026av)
   The bootstrap path contains a useful, limited repair. For tabular data and a wrapper
accepting knowledge, BootstrapTimeLag constructs lagged tuples before resampling, resets
the core’s lag parameter to avoid lagging twice, and restores knowledge afterward. The base
class uses this preparation on inspected single- and multiple-dataset paths. If knowledge
cannot be accepted, the helper leaves the inputs unchanged and logs a warning. This does not
guarantee the repair for every wrapper. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d)
  Original observations (10, 20, 30) contain transitions 10 → 20 and 20 → 30. Resampling raw
indices (2, 0, 1) before lagging fabricates 30 → 10. Resampling already formed tuples prevents
this particular error, but does not make tuples independent or establish bootstrap coverage.
24.28. Java temporal discovery: clocks, regimes and the meaning of a learned network       303


The helper’s comment acknowledges residual dependence and the absence of a block bootstrap
in that path. Dependence conditions need justification for the actual statistic, rather than
acceptance from a comment. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d; Causal banking proposal, 2026aw)
  For a concrete law, set Zt = εt + εt−1 with independent, centered unit-variance innovations.
The variance of Zt is two and adjacent covariance is one. For four observations,
                                4·2+2·3·1  7                            2  1
                    Var(Z̄) =         2
                                          = ,           Varind (Z̄) =     = .
                                    4      8                            4  2
Enumeration of the 32 equally likely configurations of five Rademacher innovations reproduces
the first value. This discrepancy is a property of the law, independent of faithful lag-column
storage. For four branches and five dates, suppose outcomes contain independent common
date shocks of variance four plus independent branch-date shocks of variance one. The grand
mean has variance 4/5 + 1/20 = 17/20. Treating the 20 rows as independent gives 5/20 = 1/4.
Separate within-branch bootstraps do not automatically restore the missing cross-branch
covariance. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aw)


24.28.3     Multiple datasets, intervention regimes and weights

IMaGES needs more than a list of matrices. The inspected one-argument ImagesScore con-
structor is documented as selecting SAMPLE_UNIFORM, but its body selects DATASET_WEIGHTED.
With component sizes Nk , their mean N̄ , and positive user weights uk , the latter normalizes

                                             uk N̄ /Nk
                                       wk = P             .
                                              j uj N̄ /Nj

The alternative uses 1/K on the component scores. Since scores can scale with sample size, the
two modes have different objectives. IMaGES uses the one-argument constructor. A nonfinite
component makes the aggregate undefined rather than being silently dropped; the sample-size
accessor returns the rounded mean size, not total rows. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d)
   For component differences 100 and −20 with sizes 1000 and 100, the plain average is 40.
The actual equal-uk default uses weights 1/11, 10/11, giving −100/11. The sign changes.
This is arithmetic for stipulated component differences, not a claim about a particular search
trajectory. The sample-size accessor gives 550 while total rows are 1100. Calling 550 the
pooled count, or putting 1100 into an uncertainty formula without a dependence argument,
each misstates the evidence. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aw)
   Economic targets can change sign too. Suppose branch effects are 1 and −2 outcome units
per action, with 1000 and 100 eligible customers. The customer-weighted effect is 8/11; the
equal-branch effect is −1/2. At a stipulated USD 20 per outcome unit and USD 8 per action,
net values are USD 72/11 and USD −18. No action has value zero here. These are different
targets, not estimators of an unspecified common target. Score weights are not automatically
causal target-population weights; the request must declare both and their relationship. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026aw)
   Intervention information is another distinction. The inspected InterventionalColumn
holds value/status column metadata. That class alone does not show that a discovery
score recognizes perfect versus soft interventions, excludes intervened mechanisms or handles
unknown targets. Branches can differ through selection, hidden conditions or measurement.
Intervention interpretation requires regime identity, targets and types, assignment evidence,
and assumptions about unchanged mechanisms. The selected inspection supports no universal
absence claim about Java interventional algorithms. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d; Causal banking
proposal, 2026av)
304                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


24.28.4     BANJO: discrete longitudinal search and a reuse boundary
