The modified BANJO repository applies network search to gene expression ordered by pseudo-
time. Its sample configuration chooses lag one, discretization policy i2, mandatory identity
edges at lag one, up to five parents and a five-minute search budget. These are application
choices. An edge at pseudotime lag one does not mean a bank intervention acts over one
calendar day. Mandatory autoregressive edges also cannot be presented as discoveries made
without prior restrictions. (daniel-315/slingshot-modified-banjo, 2026b)
   The observation code demonstrates a useful series boundary rule. Usable rows subtract the
maximum lag separately for each input file. The window loop reads only within the current file,
preserving independent series. The inspected BDe evaluator uses discrete parent-configuration
counts and equivalent-sample- size parameters. That model differs from continuous funding
dynamics. Discretization can discard magnitudes essential to a monetary decision; category
definitions, fitted cutpoints and outcome-to-money conversion need joint review. Transforma-
tions for prospective prediction also need to be learned using permitted training data. Using
all dates to fit cutpoints would require a different information claim. (daniel-315/slingshot-
modified-banjo, 2026b)
   Commercial reuse is not settled by a public mirror. Source headers state Duke ownership, a
possible noncommercial license and a need to contact the owner for commercial use. They
do not establish a permissive commercial grant for this derivative. The proposed decision is
reference-only use while official version and rights remain unresolved; direct adoption and source
porting are deferred. Independently specifying series-safe windows and explicit lag constraints
remains useful without declaring this code cleared for incorporation. (daniel-315/slingshot-
modified-banjo, 2026b; Causal banking proposal, 2026av)


24.28.5     learnDBN and learnDBM: combinations of options matter

learnDBN declares tDBN, cDBN and bcDBN structure learning for multivariate longitudinal
observations, missing-value handling and a dynamic multinet clustering route. The inspected
revision includes an Apache2 license. The CLI defaults to a stationary network, with an option
for a separate network at each transition, a maximum Markov lag and a likelihood or MDL
score. Its observation format places subjects in rows and time-indexed attributes in columns.
This differs materially from concatenating panel rows into one series. (SSamDav/learnDBN,
2020)
   The missing-data path does not consistently honor the stationarity option. The CLI passes
literal true to parameter EM, missing-value filling and scoring, even when the requested
flag is false. With two nonstationary transition networks, the filling routine therefore selects
network zero across transitions. If parameter learning is reached, its stationary branch throws
an exception because multiple transition networks exist. This is a finding from the caller
and callee, not an executed Java failure or a claim that no earlier error could occur. The
complete-data path instead passes the actual flag to parameter learning. Support for an option
and support for missing values separately do not establish support for their combination.
(SSamDav/learnDBN, 2020; Causal banking proposal, 2026aw)
   Malformed time headers can call System.exit(1), which is unsuitable inside a shared
host process. The inspected parameter-EM method and outer structural loop continue while
scores strictly improve, without an explicit iteration cap in those loops. Missing-value filling
enumerates category combinations and allocates arrays from their counts. Resource budgets
and overflow/allocation checks are therefore part of the prototype contract. Finally, the
compact graph option explicitly omits intra-slice edges. That display cannot be the canonical
24.28. Java temporal discovery: clocks, regimes and the meaning of a learned network          305


scientific graph. (SSamDav/learnDBN, 2020)
   The engineering repair route is concrete: propagate the declared stationarity flag through
all relevant calls, or refuse the unsupported combination; isolate process-level failures; impose
termination and memory budgets; and export the full graph with lag and intra-slice information.
Native tests should cover complete and incomplete data under stationary and nonstationary
settings. These repairs do not justify the missingness mechanism, guarantee a global optimum,
or turn a score-selected graph into a causal confidence set. (Causal banking proposal, 2026av)
   learnDBM is a related implementation. At the selected revisions, 15 of the 17 shared
paths in the repositories’ dynamic-network source directory have identical Git blobs. Their
observation classes and CLI entry points differ: learnDBM accepts a cluster count and
invokes MultiNet.clust with the requested stationarity flag. The inner clustering path is
not inspected here. The learnDBN CLI finding cannot automatically be attributed to this
different caller. Nor do learned clusters necessarily represent externally assigned intervention
regimes; that interpretation needs another identification argument. (SSamDav/learnDBN,
2020; SSamDav/learnDBM, 2020)


24.28.6     Weka and BayesNetBuilder: alternatives with different outputs

Weka’s declared forecasting package version 1.0.27 dates to October 2019 and uses GPL3 in
the inspected mirror. It creates lagged and date-derived features for regression, with CLI and
graphical interfaces. The actual TSLagMaker import is forecasting-core TimeSeriesTranslate;
the similarly named generic filter is a different class. The caller copies an attribute and
applies a negative instance shift. The core translator copies selected historical values; its base
maintains a queue with offsets counted in instances. The selected history method receives
neither physical timestamps nor subject identities. Calendar preprocessing elsewhere does not
remove the need for adapter-level clock and series validation. (Waikato/weka-3.8, 2022b)
   Weka is therefore useful as a forecasting or feature-construction comparator with explicit
transformations and information availability. This does not qualify it as a causal-effect
estimator. Consider a fair binary hidden risk indicator U , an independent E equal to one
with probability 1/4, and A = U xor E, Y = U . All four observed (A, Y ) cells have positive
probability. The conditional means are E[Y | A = 1] = 3/4 and E[Y | A = 0] = 1/4. Yet
setting A changes no outcome equation, so the intervention contrast is zero. With USD 20
per outcome and USD 8 per action, the conditional proxy for net benefit is USD 2, while the
actual intervention net value is USD −8 in this stipulated law. Perfectly fitting its conditional
distribution would not resolve that distinction. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aw)
   BayesNetBuilder offers parameter learning in a supplied dynamic model. Its inspected
EM entry point defaults to 1000 steps and tolerance 0.0001, computes expected sufficient
statistics and maximizes parameters, and logs when the limit is reached without convergence.
Its author’s README describes graduate research code requiring major refactoring and
documentation. No root license was identified in the selected complete-tree review; rights
remain unresolved. These observations justify a reference candidate for model-supplied
EM. They do not establish structural discovery, intervention identification or a dependable
production service. (selrach/BayesNetBuilder, 2011)


24.28.7     A public and generated prototype to resolve the known issues

The immediate proposal should fund a restricted prototype. A first comparison would retain
Tetrad behind a typed adapter, consider a repaired learnDBN path for discrete longitudinal
data, and use Weka for forecasting comparison. An exact small oracle and a conservative
306                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


no-discovery decision provide further baselines. BANJO and BayesNetBuilder remain reference-
only pending rights and version clarification. learnDBM needs an inspected clustering path
before becoming an enabled backend. Porting is a later option where rights, numerical
equivalence and maintenance advantages are established. Wrapping software does not remove
its rights or scientific conditions. (Causal banking proposal, 2026av)
   Generated mechanisms can vary clock regularity, series boundaries, shared shocks, regime
changes, missingness and hidden causes while retaining known interventions. Public observa-
tions supply realistic calendars and measurement patterns. Documented public assignments
may supply stronger causal evidence for their stated populations and interventions. The com-
parison should report window and graph fidelity, unsupported/refused requests, graph-family
retention where truth is known, justified effect-set coverage and width, decision loss and full
workflow cost. Whole mechanisms or trajectories form evaluation units, with common-calendar
clusters retained. Sources, settings, evaluation units, replications and stopping rules must be
frozen before a final study. This is a prospective design, not an executed Java experiment.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026av)
   Remaining uncertainty has distinct remedies. Broader candidate searches, missing originals,
release matching, rights review and native option- combination trials are concrete acquisition
and engineering work. Useful graph and effect uncertainty under hidden causes, dependence
and potentially invalid regime assumptions remains a research problem. Where two models
fit the observations but disagree about an action, the product must report an identified set,
obtain justified additional information, or decline the point- effect claim. Another package
name, larger panel or successful EM termination does not supply that missing premise. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026av)


24.29      Native temporal and interventional engines: preserving
           the scientific request
A bank considering a native discovery engine first needs to specify what is to be learned. A
graph of relationships among funding rates, balances and market conditions is different from
the response of balances to a controlled rate change. A transition model for delinquency
is different again: it can predict the next recorded state without identifying the effect of a
servicing action. The R, Python and Java comparisons above make these distinctions at their
language boundaries. The same distinctions govern a C++ implementation, even when its
numerical kernel is fast and its graph output looks familiar.
  Five families illuminate different parts of this choice. The C++ kernel in pcalg implements
search using known intervention targets through an R interface. aGrUM supplies a native
probabilistic-model engine, while the inspected dynamic network helper is Python. Mocapy++
supplies dynamic-model inference and parameter learning for structures supplied by the user.
sDBN contains native temporal structure-training paths. BayesNetty contributes a constrained
genetic-network search reference. Their capabilities overlap in representation and numerical
work, but their statistical experiments and result meanings differ. The comparison uses
cutoff-compatible source revisions and the technical content of the original GIES paper; it
does not treat repository search metadata as evidence of implemented capability. (cran/pcalg,
2024; agrumery/aGrUM, 2026b; juliusHuelsmann/MocapyPP, 2019; JBSants/sDBN, 2021;
NewcastleRSE/BayesNetty, 2025; Hauser and Bühlmann, 2012)
24.29. Native temporal and interventional engines: preserving the scientific request        307


24.29.1     A common banking question and two indistinguishable observed
            laws

Let X be a centered, standardized funding-rate decision variable and Y a centered retained-
balance index. Consider two deliberately small causal models:

                                 W1 : X = UX , Y = 21 X + εY ,
                                 W2 : Y = UY , X = 12 Y + εX .

In each world the root variable is standard normal, the error has variance 3/4, and root and
error are independent. Both observational distributions are centered Gaussian with covariance
                                                         !
                                                1 1/2
                                        Σ=            .
                                               1/2 1

Consequently a better fit to this observational law cannot distinguish the two directions.
Temporal labels alone do not repair this example if both variables describe the same decision
interval and their within-interval order has not been justified.
   Now replace the equation for X by an independently randomized draw with variance four.
In W1 , the intervention yields Var(Y ) = 7/4 and Cov(X, Y ) = 2; in W2 , it yields variance one
and covariance zero. This is an information change, not merely an extra argument supplied
to an optimizer. The known intervention must actually replace the appropriate structural
mechanism while preserving the other stipulated mechanisms.
  For a finite increase from do(X = 0) to do(X = 1), suppose that one unit of Y is worth
USD 20 and the action costs USD 4. The net effects are

                        V1 = 20(1/2) − 4 = 6,        V2 = 20(0) − 4 = −4.

These are exact authored examples, not bank measurements. Their purpose is to show why
a representative graph cannot silently become the bank’s selected causal truth: the same
observational fit permits opposite action decisions. Acquiring useful intervention information
may be worth considering, but its value depends on the decision and acquisition cost, not the
number of arrows that a search happens to orient. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bd)


24.29.2     pcalg: a native interventional kernel with an R contract

The selected pcalg version is 2.7-12, represented by its September 2024 CRAN source revision.
Hauser and Bühlmann formulate independent observations with known intervention targets;
the data need not be identically distributed across targets. Their conservative-target condition
leaves each variable unmanipulated in at least one regime. These conditions explain the local
score: observations from regimes that intervene on node j do not estimate that node’s original
conditional mechanism. In the paper’s DREAM4 application, uncertain-target perturbations
are excluded. This establishes a limit of that application and formulation, not a finding that
all later methods fail with unknown targets. The paper also leaves consistency of its GIES
procedure as a question; that statement must not be turned into a claim about all subsequent
consistency literature. (Hauser and Bühlmann, 2012)
  The implementation preserves this experiment through several layers. The R constructor
validates target membership and row counts, sorts rows by target index, and constructs a
nonintervened-row index for each node. The C++ entry converts one-based R vertex and row
indices to zero-based indices. The score factory distinguishes raw Gaussian, scatter-matrix
Gaussian and R callback paths. A proposed bridge must therefore preserve row identities,
308                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


target families, labels and score configuration together. Copying a numerical matrix and an
adjacency list into a nominally equivalent native routine is not a complete port. (cran/pcalg,
2024)
   For node j, write Nj = {i : j ∈
                                 / Ii }, where Ii is the known intervention target for row i, and
let nj = |Nj |. Up to constants that do not affect the relevant search comparison, the inspected
Gaussian local score has the form
                                      "          (            )#
                                    nj               RSSj,P
                        sj (P ) = −    1 + log                     − λ(1 + |P |).
                                    2                 nj
Here P is the candidate parent set and RSS is the residual sum of squares on the nonintervened
rows, with the configured intercept. The default penalty uses half the logarithm of the total row
count. The likelihood expression is not a dependent-panel uncertainty correction. Overlapping
time windows and shared calendar shocks need their own statistical justification before this
independent-row experiment is claimed.
   Configuration identity matters even before any temporal extension. The manual constructor
lists intercept=FALSE, while the inspected R constructor defaults to TRUE. For a parentless
response (8, 10, 10, 12), fitting its mean gives RSS 8, whereas fixing its mean at zero gives
RSS 408. Holding the penalty fixed, the score difference is 2 log(51), approximately 7.86365.
This is an independent calculation from the displayed score, not an observed pcalg execution.
The remedy is to set and report the intercept explicitly and test both documented and actual
defaults in a future bridge. The same contract must reject fractional identifiers before the
wrapper’s integer coercion, reject zero effective row counts and nonfinite scores, and retain
diagnostics for failed factorizations. The native Cholesky and QR paths can return NaN on
failure; that must not become a valid zero effect. (cran/pcalg, 2024; Causal banking proposal,
2026bd)
   GIES returns an estimated interventional essential graph and a representative DAG. Those
are different objects. Its symmetric fixedGaps represents forbidden adjacency, and adaptive
modes can revise the set of gaps. A banking constraint such as “an earlier decision cannot
be caused by a later balance” is directional; representing it as forbidden adjacency would
also delete a permitted forward relationship. A bridge should require an explicit constraint
type and validate the returned graph against the requested hard constraints. The proposed
reuse route is a versioned R bridge around the existing native kernel. A standalone C++
port remains a separate effort because the inspected interfaces include Rcpp objects, callback
support, R preprocessing and RcppArmadillo/BH dependencies. The GPL-at-least-2 package
declaration also requires a distribution-specific rights review; a language bridge alone does not
settle that question. (cran/pcalg, 2024)

24.29.3     aGrUM: unrolling a model while preserving state meaning

The inspected aGrUM dynamic helper, at its 6 October 2026 revision, checks time-slice suffixes
and selected domain sizes, creates time-indexed variables, reconstructs parent order, and copies
conditional-probability arrays into the unrolled model. This is valuable model-construction
support. It is a Python helper over the native engine, and the inspected path does not itself
learn a causal temporal structure. An inference engine can answer questions about a supplied
model without establishing that the supplied arrows are causal. (agrumery/aGrUM, 2026b)
   Equal cardinality is weaker than equal state identity. Suppose the initial slice lists states as
(current, delinquent), while the repeated slice lists them as (delinquent, current). The intended
transition has
                 P (Dt+1 = 1 | Dt = 0) = 0.1,          P (Dt+1 = 1 | Dt = 1) = 0.8.
24.29. Native temporal and interventional engines: preserving the scientific request         309


Starting current, the correct two-step delinquency probability is 0.9(0.1) + 0.1(0.8) = 0.17. If
a conversion blindly reuses the numeric parent-state positions after the ordering changes, it
instead computes 0.9(0.8) + 0.1(0.1) = 0.73. For a stipulated value 100 − 40p, this changes
USD 93.2 into USD 70.8, a USD 22.4 error. This is an authored conversion counterexample
motivated by the source path; it is not an observed pyagrum runtime result. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bd)
   The helper’s is2TBN checks cardinality without checking identity of the ordered state
labels. The unrolling function’s particular invalid-slice guard combines two conditions with
conjunction, so some incomplete slice sets evade that guard. This is a static control-flow
observation; it does not establish which later operation fails for every malformed model. A
proposed adapter should validate complete slice pairing, ordered state identities, physical
period, dimensions and permitted arrows before unrolling. A deliberate relabeling needs
a probability-preserving permutation of every affected tensor axis, followed by comparison
with a small independently enumerated model. The inspected file permits LGPL-3-or-later
or MIT, supported by the same-revision license texts; dependency and distribution closure
still need checking. Conditional adoption of supplied-model unrolling is reasonable. Calling
that adoption a newly qualified discovery method is unsupported. (agrumery/aGrUM, 2026b;
Causal banking proposal, 2026bc)

24.29.4     Mocapy++: latent-state modeling is a different investment

Mocapy++ can serve a supplied dynamic model in which an unobserved borrower state emits
recorded behavior. The inspected manual, version 1.05 from January 2010, explicitly states
in Section 3.7 that structure learning is absent. Its worked source example adds within-slice
and between-slice edges before performing expectation and maximization steps. The sequence
masks distinguish observed, hidden and missing entries. A hidden entry is not an intervention,
and an EM fit of a hidden-state model does not establish that changing a recorded action would
change the hidden state according to the fitted model. The bounded decision is therefore to
reject this version as the proposed structure-discovery backend while retaining it as a reference
for supplied DBN inference and parameter learning. (juliusHuelsmann/MocapyPP, 2019)
   An engineering evaluation would need to justify the legacy environment and source custody.
The inspected mirror is dated February 2019; its build uses C, C++ and Fortran, and its
instructions discuss compiler-matched Boost and LAPACK. Moreover, the root license contains
LGPL2.1 text while the inspected DBN, EM engine and example headers specify LGPL3-or-
later. These observations require per-file clarification and cannot honestly be compressed into
one unqualified package-license label. Modernizing this code may cost more than using another
permitted inference engine with the same supplied model. The comparison should measure the
cost of preserving the model, masks, numerical behavior and diagnostics, rather than reward
a port merely because its output has the same shape. (juliusHuelsmann/MocapyPP, 2019;
Causal banking proposal, 2026bc)

24.29.5     sDBN: temporal training, dependent rows and output interpretation

The inspected September 2021 sDBN revision contains a C++14 dynamic-network training
program with stationary, nonstationary and already-rolled input paths. Lag zero means all
available time steps. The stationary loader turns m wide subject records with T time points
and lag L into (T − L)m overlapping transition rows. The node-training code excludes future
parents and parents outside the specified lag, while allowing contemporaneous candidates.
These are concrete temporal mechanisms; they do not by themselves identify intervention
effects or validate a stationary law for irregular bank records. (JBSants/sDBN, 2021)
310                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   For example, three independent subjects with four observations and lag one produce nine
transition rows. Suppose each subject has one independent, mean-zero, variance-one shock
repeated through its three transition rows. The mean of all nine rows is the mean of three
shocks. Its true variance is 1/3, whereas an independence calculation using nine rows gives
1/9. An exact enumeration of eight equiprobable sign-shock worlds reproduces the first result.
Overlap can increase numerical work without increasing the independent information count
by the same factor. Likewise, dates (0, 1, 4, 5) have adjacent gaps (1, 3, 1): a row lag of one
does not specify a constant physical interval. Preserving original subject and calendar labels is
necessary for splitting, uncertainty and transport to a future decision. Shared calendar shocks
create an additional dependence problem even when subjects have distinct identifiers. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026bd)
   The output path also deserves a literal reading. The regularization stage produces allowed
directed pairs. The serializer calls this array a skeleton; it adds a separate directed structure
and likelihood only when a directed-search result is supplied. With –no-hill, the caller passes
no such result. That array should therefore retain its candidate-edge meaning, rather than be
advertised as an acyclic causal graph, an essential graph or a partial ancestral graph. With
directed search enabled, the called header checks paths before adding edges and restricts
reversals to equal-time nodes with a cycle check. The inspected reversal branch does not
explicitly check membership of the reversed pair in the allowed list. A future prototype must
test and enforce the intended meaning of those restrictions, especially when starting from a
supplied graph. (JBSants/sDBN, 2021)
   There is a further transport issue. The CLI uses standard output for its result when no
output file is supplied. The directed-search routine also prints diagnostics to standard output
inside the result-producing call. Static tracing therefore predicts a mixed diagnostic/result
stream for that path; no native execution was performed here. A proposed CLI bridge
should use a dedicated result file or separate channel, validate the entire result, and return a
transport failure when parsing fails. It should not silently remove arbitrary text until something
resembling JSON remains. The existing binary hot-start serialization also motivates an explicit
version and platform contract before checkpoints cross environments. (JBSants/sDBN, 2021;
Causal banking proposal, 2026bc)
    Reuse remains conditional. The complete inspected tree contains no README or license
file, so public access does not establish permission to copy or redistribute the implementation.
The build depends on Eigen, LBFGS, FlatBuffers and OpenSSL, with optional MPI/MKL
paths; its release configuration enables fast-math and contains a host-specific include directory.
Resolve terms, replace that path, freeze dependencies and compare numerical behavior with
conservative compiler settings before considering a bridge. Until then, sDBN is a source
reference and prototype candidate, not an adopted backend. Independent generated temporal
examples remain possible without copying its implementation. (JBSants/sDBN, 2021)


24.29.6     BayesNetty: constraints and failure values need precise translation

BayesNetty’s selected June 2025 source documents genetic-network modeling, greedy search
and random or jittered restarts. Its score documentation assumes multinomial discrete nodes
and normal continuous nodes. These sources make it a useful constrained-network reference,
but do not qualify a temporal or interventional banking estimator. The input documentation
gives ordered blacklist edges. If both directions appear in a whitelist, an adjacency is required
while either orientation is allowed. A whitelist/blacklist conflict is documented as an error.
(NewcastleRSE/BayesNetty, 2025)
  These conventions differ from pcalg’s symmetric gaps. In a two-node DAG universe, a
24.29. Native temporal and interventional engines: preserving the scientific request           311


forbidden adjacency permits only the empty graph; banning only A → B also permits B → A;
requiring adjacency permits either one-edge orientation. Two whitelist lines do not represent an
unmeasured common cause with a bidirected edge. The proposed conversion must preserve the
predicate being asserted, with endpoint semantics carried separately from input-file conventions.
(NewcastleRSE/BayesNetty, 2025; cran/pcalg, 2024; Causal banking proposal, 2026bd)
  Failure values must also retain their meaning. The inspected serial search method returns
numeric zero when its initial network has a loop. Its caller has not been traced in this
comparison, so this does not establish the final CLI behavior. It does establish why a wrapper
cannot assume that every numeric return is a successful score. The prospective contract
needs an independent acyclicity check and an explicit failure status. The GPL3 source and
documented compiler route support a conditional reference decision, with dependency, licensing
and target semantics checked before a wider integration is enabled. (NewcastleRSE/BayesNetty,
2025; Causal banking proposal, 2026bc)


24.29.7     Reuse choices and the next affordable experiment

The resulting choices are complementary. Their common prerequisite is an explicit scientific
request, not a universal adjacency-matrix interface.

   A proposed CLI or MCP request should bind the population, independent sampling unit,
physical and availability clocks, intervention family, regime-to-row map, state dictionaries,
hard constraints, score options and intended output class. The response should retain the
selected graph class, candidate-versus-final status, diagnostics and uncertainty scope. An
unqualified regime is an unsupported request; a failed factorization is a computation failure;
an equivalence class is unresolved orientation, not a parser failure. Neither transport should
convert one category into another. This is a proposed interoperability contract, not a report
that these external engines have already been integrated. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bc)
   The next affordable experiment uses generated regimes and finite models with known
answers. It compares the two Gaussian worlds, intercept settings, permuted regime/row
identifiers, reordered state dictionaries, repeated subject windows, irregular dates, contradictory
constraints and malformed output. Where reuse terms and an environment are available,
a frozen upstream run can then be compared with the independent reference on identical
312                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


inputs. All requests, failures and unavailable results remain in the accounting. Public credit
or mortgage records may supply realistic covariate ranges, missingness patterns and calendars
under their applicable terms; generated assignments and responses must remain labeled as
generated. Such observations cannot retroactively supply authentic intervention truth.
   Measure preparation, rights review, compilation, conversion, diagnostics, scientific review
and maintenance as well as numerical runtime. The USD 10 decision difference between the
Gaussian worlds and USD 22.4 conversion error show which meanings deserve early tests; they
are not estimates of prototype profitability. A costly bank experiment becomes justified only
when a permitted prototype resolves a consequential uncertainty and specifies what extra bank
information could change the decision. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bd,bc)
   The search remains bounded. The inherited scholarly query includes duplicate and pub-
lication aliases, and the native repository queries leave relevant families such as DBN++,
EISALab/DBN and pdbntk uninspected. Name and language metadata cannot decide their
causal capability. Missing originals and rights have concrete acquisition routes; broader search
requires additional pinned technical inspection. Useful dependent graph/effect uncertainty,
latent confounding, unknown interventions and bank transport require further scientific work
and cannot be promised by completing that acquisition. These open branches do not prevent
the proposed contract or the generated reference experiment from progressing. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026bc)
Chapter 25

Commercial identification,
counterfactuals and the information
a bank must supply

A lending manager asks whether offering a temporary rate reduction will improve twelve-month
repayment among existing borrowers. A second manager asks whether one particular borrower
would have repaid without the offer. A third asks how much of the effect operates through
an intermediate change in payment behavior. These requests share business language and
variables, but they demand different causal information. Purchasing a package with a causal
menu does not make them the same statistical problem. Nor does implementing a common
API remove their different assumptions.
   The proposed product should first identify the requested quantity and then compare the
information and computation required to answer it. Commercial software provides substantive
precedents: graphical intervention workflows, treatment-effect estimators, mediation models
and, in at least one inspected guide, an explicit abduction workflow. Those are capabilities
against which the proposal must be assessed. Their documentation also illustrates why a
numerical answer needs a stated model and why an unsupported question must remain visible.
   This comparison draws on a declared set of sixteen commercial families and 27 bounded
public document requests, together with the preserved commercial corpus. It inspects technical
documents for BayesiaLab, Stata and Bayes Server; an Mplus resource index supplies additional
leads. Other families retain specific unresolved comparisons. The literature cutoff remains 7
October 2026. New document copies were acquired on 13 October, and mutable pages do not
authenticate their exact contents at the cutoff. Stata’s inspected PDFs carry 2025 copyright
and release-19 data references; the Bayes Server guide names specific version thresholds. These
identities are more informative than an undated search result, but they do not eliminate the
historical-copy limitation. No licensed vendor engine was executed for this comparison (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026f).


25.1     Four questions that require four capability descriptions
Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote the offer and Y (a) repayment by a specified date under offer state a.
The outcome is defined for every existing loan, including loans receiving no offer. The first
target is
                                   τ = E{Y (1) − Y (0)}.


                                             313
314                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


The population, date, treatment version and accounting meaning are part of this definition.
A target among recipients, conditional on pre-offer history, or under a sequence of actions
needs a different expression. An analysis of only newly approved loans would additionally face
selection and possibly a different outcome definition; it cannot silently reuse this target.


25.1.1    Adjustment and general identification

An adjustment method starts from a justified observed set X. Under consistency, conditional
exchangeability and suitable positivity, it evaluates
                                        Z
                           E{Y (a)} =       E[Y | A = a, X = x] dP (x).

The integral is an identification statement; fitting its regression and averaging predictions is a
subsequent estimation problem. A tool can implement the latter while relying entirely on the
analyst for the former.
   A broader identification request supplies a graph class, observed variables, available obser-
vational or experimental distributions and an intervention query. For example, it may ask for
P (Y | do(A = a)) in a graph with unobserved common causes, or for a conditional intervention
distribution P (Y | do(A = a), Z = z). Claims about ID or IDC must name the algorithm and
its supported graph and query classes. Support for one valid adjustment set does not establish
those broader capabilities.
   The response contract should distinguish an identified functional, a justified nonidentification
result within the declared model class, and an unknown result because the available method
does not cover the request. Failure of a back-door search belongs to the third category unless
a separate argument establishes the second. The exact mediator example below shows the
practical importance of this distinction.


25.1.2    Individual counterfactuals and mediated effects

For a borrower who received the offer and repaid, a different query is

                               q = Pr{Y (0) = 0 | A = 1, Y = 1}.

It concerns a relationship between the factual and alternative worlds for the same unit. Knowing
both marginal distributions P {Y (0)} and P {Y (1)} need not identify their joint distribution.
A structural model with specified exogenous variables can supply that relationship, but the
relationship is then additional model information. A workflow that infers those exogenous
variables from evidence, changes an action and predicts the result must preserve the assumptions
connecting the worlds.
  Mediation makes another distinction. Let M (a) be a mediator, measured after the offer,
and Y (a, m) the outcome under joint interventions. One decomposition of the total effect uses

                             NDE = E[Y (1, M (0)) − Y (0, M (0))],
                              NIE = E[Y (1, M (1)) − Y (1, M (0))].

Their sum is the total effect under the corresponding composition assumptions. These are
population averages of nested potential outcomes. They are neither the same target as an
individual borrower’s q nor automatically identified by randomizing A. The mediator–outcome
relation and treatment-induced confounding still matter. Stata’s one-mediator manual makes
these assumptions explicit rather than presenting the word “counterfactual” as an unrestricted
capability (StataCorp, 2026b).
25.2. BayesiaLab: a documented graphical adjustment workflow                                  315


25.1.3    Partial identification and uncertainty

When the information identifies a set rather than a point, the product should return that set
and explain which restrictions would narrow it. This differs from a confidence interval for a
point parameter. A finite-sample confidence region for an identified set requires an additional
sampling argument. A software comparison must therefore record separately whether a package
computes a point functional, logical bounds, a sensitivity region or statistical uncertainty, and
how failed or empty requests are represented.


25.2     BayesiaLab: a documented graphical adjustment workflow
The inspected graphical-identification chapter explains causal and noncausal paths, adjustment
in a supplied DAG and a particular hidden-common-cause obstruction. Its discussion supports
a comparison of adjustment semantics. It does not specify a complete general ID/IDC
implementation (Bayesia, 2026f). In particular, its example in which a new hidden cause
defeats adjustment should not be generalized to every graph with hidden confounding.
   The graph-surgery walkthrough is operationally more specific. An analyst draws the causal
graph, associates data columns and state values with its nodes, estimates the probability tables,
and inspects the paths to a selected target. The intervention menu removes the treatment’s
incoming arcs for the causal query. The displayed probabilities then change without treating
the action as ordinary observed evidence. This is a documented supplied-model intervention
workflow, including a visual explanation of the observational/interventional distinction (Bayesia,
2026h).
   For the proposed bank tool, data-to-node association is a substantive capability. An offer
flag recorded after acceptance may not represent the assigned offer; a repayment field may
be available after the declared decision date. A graph display that preserves node names
but loses this mapping can give a convincing diagram of the wrong question. The proposal
should make each node’s unit, clock, state coding and source field reviewable, and make the
intervention status visible alongside the graph. These are concrete requirements suggested by
the documented commercial workflow, not evidence that the local prototype already implements
a comparable visual environment.
   The likelihood-matching walkthrough documents another route for the same example. It
uses probabilistic evidence and a Fix Probabilities operation to hold a confounder’s marginal
distribution fixed while varying treatment evidence. Its reported example matches the graph-
surgery calculation. The important mathematical question is whether the variables and
distributions being held fixed supply a valid adjustment for the requested target (Bayesia,
2026g). A numerical balancing operation does not establish that an unmeasured common
cause has been removed.
   Bayesia’s contribution-analysis page uses generated data, a learned network, expert assump-
tions about confounder selection and Likelihood Matching to compare factual and intervention
conditions. That supports a documented contribution workflow. The inspected text does not
fully specify a general individual-level abduction model or the coupling of alternative outcomes.
Its linked slides and recording were not inspected in this comparison (Bayesia, 2026e). The
proposed product should therefore ask whether a request is a population intervention contrast,
a contribution allocation or a conditional individual counterfactual before choosing an adapter.
  The reuse recommendation is conditional: treat these workflows as commercial benchmarks
and possible licensed integration targets. Obtain the exact API, edition, export semantics and
deployment rights before promising an adapter. Porting proprietary implementation is not an
316                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


available reuse strategy on the basis of public documentation. Independently implementing a
justified mathematical method requires its own provenance and validation.


25.3     Stata: treatment effects and mediation with explicit as-
         sumptions
The inspected teffects introduction documents average treatment effects, effects among
treated subjects and potential-outcome means. It covers regression adjustment, inverse-
probability weighting, augmented weighting, weighted regression adjustment and matching.
Its caveats discuss independent sampling, conditional independence and overlap, including why
unmeasured determinants of treatment and outcome can invalidate an estimate (StataCorp,
2026a).
  This is a substantial estimator baseline. The proposal needs a defensible reason to build
another estimator rather than a thin, licensed workflow around an existing one. A possible
reason is preservation of the business target, information clock, graph ambiguity and source
provenance across several tools. That reason becomes persuasive only when a minimal
prototype demonstrates the behavior and a comparison measures the total effort of obtaining
an acceptable answer. Merely presenting additional estimators or claiming a common CLI
does not establish superiority over an established analysis workflow.
   For the lending request, an analyst could supply pre-offer covariates and fit one of the
documented treatment-effect estimators. The output then inherits the asserted covariate
sufficiency and the relevant sampling law. The selected manual’s IID discussion does not
establish validity for every repeated monthly loan record or shared-calendar shock. Likewise,
an overlap diagnostic concerns observed treatment support; it cannot certify that an omitted
repayment driver has been measured. The proposed wrapper must record these distinct
obligations instead of converting a successful command exit into an identification pass.
   The mediate manual supplies a separate, developed capability. It describes continuous,
binary and count outcome/mediator models, several treatment types, interactions, direct and
indirect effects, potential-outcome means and variance options. It explicitly addresses un-
measured confounding in the treatment–outcome, treatment–mediator and mediator–outcome
relations, and excludes treatment-induced mediator–outcome confounding under its stated
identification conditions (StataCorp, 2026b).
   Consider an offer that changes a borrower’s monthly payment burden, which then affects
repayment. The offer might also trigger a collections contact that affects both payment behavior
and repayment. That contact is a possible treatment-induced mediator–outcome confounder.
Adding it mechanically to every regression is not a justification of the natural-effect estimand.
The business request may need a different mediated target or a richer design. A common
API should carry the precise nested expression and its assumptions rather than label every
coefficient product an indirect causal effect.
  The inspected manuals support these estimator and mediation comparisons. They do
not establish generic graphical ID/IDC, arbitrary individual abduction or complete latent-
graph coverage. Other Stata commands may address other endogeneity models; those require
their own technical comparisons. The current product proposal should prioritize matched
documented targets and keep unreviewed extensions explicit. Exact licensing, embedded
execution and price comparisons remain outstanding; no commercial runtime result is reported
here.
25.4. Bayes Server: intervention, abduction and the need for an exact API contract             317


25.4      Bayes Server: intervention, abduction and the need for
          an exact API contract
The Bayes Server causal guide distinguishes ordinary evidence from intervention, describes
discrete and continuous variables, and gives a concrete individual counterfactual workflow.
Its example enters factual evidence, uses an Abduction dialog to infer characteristic variables,
applies a changed intervention, and reads the resulting outcome. The guide describes helper
functions from version 10 onward and says the example calculations can be performed from
version 9.4 (Bayes Server, 2026a).
   This is stronger evidence of a documented abduction workflow than a generic “what if”
feature label. It reveals another capability gap for the proposal: the local reference service does
not yet offer this general structural-model workflow. The architecture should represent the
exogenous-variable model, conditioning evidence, action and resulting distribution as separate
objects. It should also retain whether abduction produced a unique value, a distribution or an
unresolved set. A model-specified answer can be useful while remaining conditional on the
model’s cross-world assumptions.
   The guide also lists back-door and front-door adjustment, instruments, disjunctive-cause
reasoning and do-calculus, stating that many approaches are available from version 10 onward.
That phrasing does not identify which exact algorithms are implemented, the graph classes for
which they are complete, or the supported failure certificates. The linked Advanced Causal
Query and Abduction technical pages are specific next sources. The comparison therefore
records the documented workflow while leaving complete ID/IDC and arbitrary counterfactual
identification unknown.
   An adapter proposal needs more than the guide’s terminology. It needs exact node and edge
encodings, latent-variable treatment, allowed interventions, conditioning behavior, numerical
types, export format, method/version identity and a licensed execution boundary. Until those
are inspected and tested, the recommendation is a focused commercial benchmark candidate.
It is not a promise of immediately reusable functionality or a claim that a general causal
identification engine is absent from the product.

25.6      Exact lending examples that separate the required capa-
          bilities
The following are project constructions, evaluated with exact rational arithmetic. They are
neither fitted vendor outputs nor bank observations. Their purpose is to make identification,
partial identification and counterfactual semantics reviewable before an expensive experiment
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026e).


25.6.1    The same observed loan table can support different effects

Consider an observed law
                                           Y =0 Y =1
                                       A=0  3/8  1/8
                                       A=1  1/8  3/8
with all four cells positive. The observed repayment difference is 3/4 − 1/4 = 1/2. One
generating model has a binary pre-existing repayment type U with probability 1/2, an
independent bit V with probability 1/4, offer A = U xor V , and outcome Y = U . Changing
the offer does not change repayment in this model: τ = 0.
   A second model randomizes A with probability 1/2. With an independent uniform four-state
variable W ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3}, let Y (0) = 1{W < 1} and Y (1) = 1{W < 3}. Its effect is τ = 1/2,
yet its observed table is identical. Enumerating both finite models verifies the equality exactly.
Additional rows from the same observed law cannot choose between them. Observed positivity
does not resolve hidden confounding.
   If the analyst commits to the second model’s randomized assignment, a treatment-effect
estimate has a causal interpretation. If the information allows both models, the same calculation
is an association with unresolved causal meaning. A commercial adapter and the local service
should preserve that difference even when they display the same number.


25.6.2    Sharp bounds remain useful information

With only consistency and binary potential outcomes, the observed successful treated borrowers
contribute 3/8 to E[Y (1)]. The unobserved Y (1) values among the untreated can contribute
anything from zero to 1/2. Similarly, observed successful untreated borrowers contribute 1/8
to E[Y (0)]. Thus

              E[Y (1)] ∈ [3/8, 7/8],     E[Y (0)] ∈ [1/8, 5/8],        τ ∈ [−1/4, 3/4].

These bounds are jointly attainable. Allocate each of the four observed (A, Y ) cells to either
value of its missing potential outcome. The 24 = 16 resulting vertices preserve the table and
attain both effect endpoints. Every fractional allocation is a convex combination of the vertices,
so a linear effect cannot exceed these extrema. The exact program checks this enumeration
separately from the missing-outcome algebra.
   For a hypothetical planning value of USD 1,000 per incremental repayment and a USD 20
cost per offer, net value is 1000τ − 20. The two equal-observed-law models imply respectively
minus USD 20 and plus USD 480 per offer. The consistency-only range is minus USD 270 to
plus USD 730. This is an assumed value mapping, not a measured ROI or a full loan-accounting
model. Its purpose is to show why the unresolved scientific distinction can reverse a decision.
  The range includes both profitable and unprofitable offers. It can justify considering a
better information design, but it does not by itself establish that any particular experiment is
320                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


worth its cost. That further argument needs the experiment’s expected resolution, the affected
decisions and their costs.


25.6.3    Hidden confounding does not always prevent identification

Now assume the precise structural graph U → A, U → Y , A → M → Y , with no additional
arrows and independent disturbances. Let

                                      Pr(U = 1) = 1/2,
                              Pr(A = 1 | U = u) = 1/4 + u/2,
                             Pr(M = 1 | A = a) = 1/5 + 3a/5,
                     Pr(Y = 1 | M = m, U = u) = 1/10 + 2m/5 + 2u/5.

The mediator intercepts all directed effects of A on Y in this stipulated law. The observed
functional                     X            X
                        µa =      P (m | a)     P (Y = 1 | m, b)P (b)
                                m            b

equals the intervention mean here. To verify rather than assume this equality, note that U
and M are conditionally independent given A, so

                            P (Y = 1 | m, b) = 1/5 + 2m/5 + b/5.

Averaging over P (A = b) = 1/2 gives 3/10 + 2m/5; averaging over P (M = 1 | A = a) gives
19/50 + 6a/25. Independently summing the intervened structural law over (U, M ) produces
the same two means, 19/50 and 31/50. The effect is 6/25 = 0.24, while the ordinary observed
difference is 11/25 = 0.44.
   The example is a useful front-door fixture, not a guarantee for every mediator. It would
require another argument if the offer had a direct effect on repayment, if an unmeasured
cause affected both offer and mediator, or if the measured mediator failed to represent the
stipulated variable. The immediate software requirement is nonetheless clear: a failed observed
back-door adjustment must not be reported as a universal nonidentification proof. Under the
hypothetical USD 1,000/20 mapping, this model’s identified net value is USD 220 per offer;
the model assumptions carry that interpretation.


25.6.4    Even complete randomized margins can leave an individual question
          open

Let A and U be independent fair bits. In one world set Y (0) = Y (1) = U ; in a second set
Y (0) = U and Y (1) = 1 − U . Both worlds have P {Y (a) = 1} = 1/2 for each action, the same
randomized observed law, and average effect zero. In the first world, a treated borrower who
repaid would also have repaid without the offer, so q = 0. In the second, that borrower would
not have repaid, so q = 1.
   The same margins allow the population probability of benefit P {Y (1) = 1, Y (0) = 0} to
range from zero to 1/2. A randomization result can identify an average effect while leaving
this cross-world association unresolved. An abduction engine supplied with one complete
structural model may return an answer, but the evidence must say which coupling it used. A
language model’s plausible borrower narrative is not additional identifying information.
25.7. A proposal architecture that can be compared fairly                                    321


25.7      A proposal architecture that can be compared fairly
The smallest coherent prototype should expose a query object containing the population,
outcome clock, intervention, conditioning event and target units. It should attach the supplied
graph or structural model, observed-variable map, permitted data laws and assumptions. The
method registry should state the exact domain of each method. A response should then carry
its expression or set, derivation/certificate where available, unresolved premises and the next
permissible operation.
   Estimation belongs after an identified functional has been selected. A licensed Stata adapter,
a documented graphical intervention adapter, or an open-source estimator could occupy that
stage. The comparison should hold the query, data, adjustment set and sampling assumptions
fixed. Method-specific diagnostics, missing values and failed requests remain part of the result.
Numerical agreement is meaningful only when both tools answered the same question under
the same assumptions.
   For individual counterfactuals, a separate structural-model path should retain the posterior
exogenous distribution after abduction and the exact action used in prediction. It should
refuse to imply unique individual identification when the available observations permit several
couplings. For partial identification, the interface should preserve closed/open endpoints,
unions and empty sets where the method requires them. These are proposed requirements;
the local back-door reference implementation and deterministic workflow checks establish only
their documented subset.
  The exact fixtures above permit a useful next experiment with no authentic bank data.
First compare each proposed method’s supported-domain response to the independently
derived truth: equal observed laws, a front-door functional, sharp bounds and differing cross-
world couplings. Then add finite public or generated samples under a frozen observation
law, with uncertainty, availability and width criteria declared before final draws. A vendor
runtime comparison can follow once technical contracts and licensing are resolved. Neither an
unavailable commercial manual nor a deferred paid trial needs to block the public prototype
route.
   The investment case should consequently distinguish three decisions: adopt an existing
estimator/workflow where its domain and rights match; build the missing scientific contract
and cross-tool explanation where that provides demonstrable value; and defer claims requiring
undocumented or unidentified capabilities. This makes the commercial landscape consequential
for the proposal while retaining honest limits on source coverage and implementation.


25.8      Edition and integration choices for the lending query
An actionable comparison must connect the banking request to the particular operation
that an edition exposes. The population effect of a repayment offer, the effect transmitted
through payment behavior, and an alternative outcome for an already observed borrower
should therefore have different request contracts. More detailed Bayes Server documentation
supplies a useful test of this distinction. Its Advanced Causal Query guide describes back-door
and front-door criteria, subsequent adjustment calculations, multiple treatments and joint
outcomes. Support for hidden confounders and direct effects varies with the selected algorithm.
Those are documented capabilities with which the proposal must compete; the list is not
evidence of a complete general identification algorithm (Bayes Server, 2026e).
  The version evidence has several layers. The guides describe the features as available from
version 10. The acquired release history associates advanced causal queries, back-door and
322                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


front-door algorithms, causal effects analysis and the abduction helper with version 10.2
beta, dated 19 June 2022. Its highest listed release is 11.4.0.0, dated 17 April 2026. These
observations support a version-family comparison; they do not identify the bytes of an installed
assembly or establish equivalence across its interfaces (Bayes Server, 2026j). The copies were
acquired on 14 October 2026. As elsewhere in this survey, dated release entries and copyright
notices do not authenticate a mutable page’s exact contents on the 7 October cutoff.


25.8.1    A narrow identification adapter has a concrete contract

The documented FrontDoorCriterion class takes a supplied network. Its Identify methods
receive interventions, outcomes, other evidence and options, and return criterion-specific
identification information without performing estimation. Associated methods, IdentifyXZ
and IdentifyZY, address the adjustment subproblems between treatment, front-door nodes
and outcomes. The documentation explicitly envisages using the identified node sets outside
Bayes Server. It also distinguishes a Boolean validity check from validation that raises an
exception (Bayes Server, 2026d). This is a much more useful integration lead than a claim
that a product “supports causality.”
   For the repayment example, a proposed adapter would receive the offer variable A, a
mediator M , repayment Y , an observed-variable map, a supplied causal network and the
desired intervention. It would return the criterion, the identified node sets, the input model
identity and the query to which they apply. An external estimator would then require the
observed distributions and support conditions needed to evaluate the functional. The exact
front-door calculation developed earlier illustrates that separation: returning a mediator name
is not the same as fitting the required conditional distributions, and fitting them is not proof
that the graph describes the bank.
   A useful minimal adapter could therefore export a reviewed identification result before
undertaking a much larger attempt to embed an entire modeling environment. The export must
preserve node identity, intervention versus ordinary evidence, treatment coding, relevant clock
and units. Its response should distinguish a valid criterion result, invalid input, unsupported
options and failure to find a set. In particular, failure of this one criterion must not become
a universal nonidentification certificate. That conclusion would need a complete algorithm
for the declared graph/query class or an independent argument. The selected documentation
establishes neither general ID/IDC completeness nor unrestricted counterfactual identification.
   The local reference service has a narrower current boundary: supplied-DAG back-door checks,
supplied-moment Gaussian residual inversion and explicit sensitivity and clock operations.
It does not expose this front-door adapter, a general abduction engine or a fitted mediation
service. The proposed scientific contract can organize those future capabilities, but it does
not erase the present functional gap. An investment case should demonstrate the value of
preserving scientific meaning across an existing estimator and a specific identification service
before proposing another broad implementation. (Causal banking proposal, 2026g)


25.8.2    Effect labels need mathematical definitions

The Advanced Causal Query guide describes total and direct effects using paths. One illustrative
total-effect list includes a path of the form A ← C → Y . That is a back-door association path,
not a directed causal route from A to Y . This wording should not be adopted as the definition
of total effect, and it does not by itself demonstrate an implementation error (Bayes Server,
2026e). A wrapper must bind the requested quantity to an explicit mathematical expression
and then determine whether the selected vendor operation computes it.
25.9. Abduction must preserve uncertainty about the borrower                                  323


   For example, the total contrast is E[Y (1) − Y (0)]. A controlled direct contrast at mediator
level m is E[Y (1, m) − Y (0, m)], while a natural direct contrast uses the unit-specific mediator
M (0) inside a nested potential outcome. A menu label about direct links does not settle
which of these interventions and cross-world premises is intended. Stata’s specified mediation
workflow provides a useful contrast because it states its natural-effect targets and confounding
restrictions (StataCorp, 2026b). The proposal should compare matching estimands, not merely
similarly named report columns.


25.9      Abduction must preserve uncertainty about the borrower
The Bayes Server abduction dialog describes querying characteristic variables given factual
evidence, removing evidence for the individual and setting evidence on those characteristics.
Its .NET Abduction.Update signature separates current evidence, the variables supplying
abduction evidence, the characteristic variables and additional options. This is explicit support
for an abduction step. The selected pages do not fully specify how an uncertain multivariate
posterior is represented or propagated through every supported case (Bayes Server, 2026b,c).
That remaining question matters even when the conditional mean of each characteristic can
be computed accurately.
  Let U represent latent repayment capacity in normalized units. For an illustrative required
payment burden a, define
                         U ∼ Uniform{0, 1, 3},       Y (a) = 1{U ≥ a}.
Assignment of the burden is independent of U in this stipulated model. For a borrower observed
at A = 1 with repayment Y = 1, Bayes’ rule eliminates U = 0 and retains U = 1 and U = 3
with equal posterior mass. Under the alternative burden a′ = 2, the individual-conditional
query is
                                          X                                         1
       Pr{Y (2) = 1 | A = 1, Y = 1} =            1{u ≥ 2} Pr(U = u | A = 1, Y = 1) = .
                                         u∈{1,3}
                                                                                    2

The population intervention probability is instead 1/3. Replacing the posterior of U by its
mean, E[U | A = 1, Y = 1] = 2, gives the indicator 1{2 ≥ 2} = 1. All three calculations concern
the same structural equation, but they answer different questions or use a lossy approximation.
The finite enumeration reproduces the fractions exactly; it is a project construction, not a test
of Bayes Server (Causal banking proposal, 2026h).
   More generally, a model-specified individual counterfactual averages the alternative struc-
tural response over the posterior of the same exogenous state that generated the factual
observations. Applying a nonlinear response to a posterior mean need not equal that average.
For several exogenous variables, preserving only separate marginal distributions can also
discard dependence needed by the response. A capability contract should state whether
the operation returns a uniquely recovered characteristic value, a posterior distribution, a
point approximation or a set of compatible states. It must also identify the extra structural
assumptions that connect alternative outcomes for the same borrower.
  To make the financial consequence explicit, stipulate a USD 1,000 payment upon success
and a USD 20 cost under the alternative scenario. The posterior calculation gives an expected
payoff of 1,000(1/2) − 20 = 480 dollars. The mean substitution gives 1,000(1) − 20 = 980
dollars, an overstatement of USD 500 in this model. These are alternative-scenario payoffs,
not incremental policy profit: a decision comparison would additionally specify the baseline
payoff and all costs. Neither the amounts nor the latent law are bank measurements (Causal
banking proposal, 2026h).
324                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The immediate public/generated test is therefore precise. Supply a small structural model
whose exogenous posterior has more than one possible state, compare its exact enumerated
counterfactual distribution with the returned object, and repeat with dependent exogenous
variables. Test removal of factual evidence separately from the intervention. Retain unsup-
ported or approximate behavior explicitly. The inspected signature is sufficient to motivate
this prototype experiment; it is insufficient to declare the result in advance.


25.10      Sweeps, units and uncertainty in the commercial output
The Effects Analysis guide describes sweeps over intervention values. Discrete treatments use
their states; continuous treatments are discretized conditional on current evidence. For discrete
outcomes the requested state probability is reported; continuous outcomes can produce a
mean and variance. The guide also normalizes the chart’s horizontal axes when treatments are
compared (Bayes Server, 2026f). Those choices affect what an exported plot means.
  A lending manager should be able to recover the actual payment burden or interest-rate
change corresponding to every displayed point. A normalized coordinate without the original
dose, unit and transformation is not an actionable pricing instruction. If the grid depends
on factual evidence, a different borrower’s curve may use different underlying values. A
prospective adapter must carry the dose grid and conditioning evidence as data, rather
than reconstructing them from an image. The intervention guide further describes discrete,
continuous and dynamic-network interventions, which must remain distinct from ordinary
observational evidence (Bayes Server, 2026h).
   The reported variance of an outcome under a fixed fitted model is also a different object
from uncertainty about its estimated causal mean. If θ denotes parameters fitted from data,
then Varθ {Y (a)} describes outcome variability at that model, while sampling variation of
an estimator of Eθ {Y (a)} requires an estimation and sampling law. Uncertainty about the
graph or about an unmeasured causal premise is another layer. A mean/variance pair from an
intervention sweep cannot be relabeled as a calibrated confidence interval for the offer effect.
The proposed result format should identify these layers and report which are included.


25.11      Reuse choices across the compared families
BayesiaLab’s supplied-graph and data-mapping workflow remains a credible commercial
comparator. Its Engine API overview distinguishes Java modeling, learning and inference
configurations from REST inference. The table places Java model files on customer servers
and REST model files on Bayesia servers in France; production capacity is tied to permitted
concurrent instances, with documented license-validation connectivity. These facts matter
to an integration design, but they do not establish that every graphical causal function is
exposed by every configuration (Bayesia, 2026a,c). The proposed route is a narrowly specified
graph/query export followed by verified interpretation of the returned result. The missing
causal API mapping must be acquired before committing to an inference-only endpoint for a
more elaborate task.
   Stata supplies a mature treatment and mediation baseline for specified targets. Its treatment-
effect documentation is more directly relevant to a one-time offer ATE or ATT than a generic
graph-learning comparison (StataCorp, 2026a). The license-options text distinguishes an
identified user’s installations from concurrent network use at a physical site. This is useful
deployment context, but the options page does not settle the entitlement for a proposed
multiuser service (StataCorp, 2026f). A first comparison can use an appropriately authorized
25.12. Published prices and conditions for a justified comparison                            325


analyst workflow and complete output artifacts. Any subsequent CLI/MCP service needs a
separately resolved execution and export contract.
   JMP should now receive a substantive treatment comparison in this chapter. The earlier
search left its primary causal source unresolved; preserved 19.2 documentation acquired for the
heterogeneous-effects comparison supplies the missing prose. The JMP Pro Causal Treatment
personality describes ATE and ATET for binary treatment, and potential-outcome means
for continuous treatment. Its assumptions distinguish consistency, positivity and conditional
exchangeability. Its binary estimators use specified propensity and outcome models, with
weighting, regression adjustment and augmentation alternatives (JMP, 2026). These are
meaningful commercial capabilities that the local reference runtime does not yet provide.
   The documentation’s potential-outcome predictions should not be described as identified
missing individual outcomes. Model-based conditional means and population averages have
their own legitimate roles; they do not supply the cross-world dependence in the borrower
example. A proposed file-based comparison should preserve target weights, observation exclu-
sions, nuisance specifications and treatment coding before attempting unattended automation.
Only inspected prose supports this comparison; image-only equations were not treated as
inspected technical evidence. Installed build, automation rights and selected deployment prices
remain unresolved.
   BayesFusion’s SMILE documentation provides a compiled C++ library and named wrap-
pers, as well as separate development and deployment licensing categories (BayesFusion, LLC,
2024j,k). That is adjacent integration evidence, not yet the missing matched intervention/-
counterfactual contract. For HUGIN, Netica, SAS, IBM, Mplus, MathWorks, causaLens,
EViews, OxMetrics, LISREL and Analytica, the technical or edition-specific questions retained
earlier in this chapter remain open at different levels. Some have useful adjacent manuals or
original-paper leads; inaccessible or incomplete pages do not establish absent functionality.
Broader ranking should wait for the matching source rather than borrow a conclusion from
another software area. (Causal banking proposal, 2026g)

The acquired Bayes Server purchase page explicitly selects Commercial and GBP in its form.

local service. Next build a generated/public-data prototype that demonstrates the missing

25.13      Commercial heterogeneity tools: from a conditional ef-
           fect to a servicing decision
A servicing manager deciding whom to contact needs more than a ranking of predicted
recoveries. An account may have a high probability of repayment without a call, a large
incremental response to a call, or a large response whose delivery cost exceeds its value. These
are different quantities. Commercial comparison must therefore start with the population,
intervention, outcome horizon and decision rule, then ask which documented estimator matches
that question. A label such as individualized effect cannot establish that both potential
outcomes of a particular customer have become observable. The Stata manual itself defines
its individualized average treatment effect as an average for individuals sharing the specified
characteristics StataCorp (2025).
   The comparison here concerns a declared universe of seventeen commercial families. Com-
plete primary documents support a detailed comparison of Stata and two distinct JMP
pathways, together with a more limited DataRobot weighting workflow. Saved technical
material was acquired on 13 October 2026. Its version and publication cues precede the 7
October literature cutoff, but those cues do not authenticate every byte as it appeared on
the cutoff date. The incomplete family coverage, failed requests and unreviewed rights are
substantive limits, not evidence that a competitor lacks a feature. No commercial product was
executed for this comparison Causal banking research project (2026b).

25.13.1    One population, several legitimate answers

Let D denote a binary servicing action, Y (d) the recovery in dollars over one fixed horizon
under action d, and G a risk group measured before the action. In the generated example,
lower-risk accounts have population mass 3/4, action probability 1/10, effect 2 dollars and
delivery cost 1 dollar. Higher-risk accounts have mass 1/4, action probability 4/5, effect 10
dollars and cost 12 dollars. Potential outcomes are stipulated, with Y (0) = 8 and 4 in the
respective groups and Y (1) = Y (0) + τG . Treatment is randomized within each group. Thus
conditional exchangeability and positivity hold by construction; they are not conclusions
drawn from a bank dataset. The exact finite-population review uses thirty lower-risk and ten
higher-risk accounts, with three and eight treated respectively. This representation realizes
the declared probabilities exactly Causal banking research project (2026a).
  The average effect in the eligible population is
                                   τATE = 34 (2) + 41 (10) = 4.
The treated fraction is 11/40, and the average effect among treated accounts is instead
                                 (3/4)(1/10)(2) + (1/4)(4/5)(10)  86

                                              11/40               11
The larger second number reflects the concentration of treatment in the higher-effect group.
Reporting it as the gain from treating every eligible account would change the target population.

Conversely, the ATE does not answer a question restricted to the accounts currently receiving
treatment. These differences require a target label in an interchange record, even if two
interfaces both expose a field called effect Causal banking research project (2026a).
  Residualization introduces a further distinction when effect modification is omitted from
the conditioning set. Write W for all nuisance controls, e(W ) = Pr(D = 1 | W ) and
h(W ) = E[Y | W ]. If the requested effect model is constant while the actual effect varies with
W , the population least-squares residual slope is

                                      E[(D − e(W ))(Y − h(W ))]
                                bPO =
                                            E[(D − e(W ))2 ]
                                      E[e(W )(1 − e(W ))τ (W )]

                                         E[e(W )(1 − e(W ))]

The second equality follows by conditioning on W , using the Bernoulli variance of D and
the stipulated conditional treatment law. It is an overlap-weighted effect, which is 214/43 in
this example, rather than the ATE of 4. This is a target-under-misspecification calculation,
not a claim that the inspected Stata implementation silently promises an unrestricted ATE.
Its partialing-out derivation specifies an effect τ (x) that does not additionally vary with
nuisance-only controls w. Changing that scientific restriction changes the interpretation of the
residual moment StataCorp (2025); Causal banking research project (2026a).
   For comparison, define µd (W ) = E[Y (d) | W ] and the oracle augmented inverse-probability

                        ψ = µ1 (W ) − µ0 (W )
