events is needed for the bound. Neither premise has been established for arbitrary language-
assisted temporal discovery here. The formula exposes what would have to be supplied, rather
than supplying it.
   CPDAG and PAG representations encode ambiguity that should survive serialization and
explanation. Circle marks, bidirected relations and unoriented edges cannot be replaced with
arrows merely to produce a cleaner diagram. A PAG is not an assertion that every latent
variable has been named. Similarly a finite list of proposed DAGs is not automatically a
complete equivalence class. The declaration validator preserves the marks and the declared
alternatives while delegating full class recognition and identification to a formal engine.


38.7      Temporal discovery is not longitudinal policy inference
The word “sequential” refers to several distinct problems. Verma and colleagues process
successive batches of contemporaneous observations while querying a language model as a
noisy expert and retaining PAG information Verma et al. (2025). The query budget and
answer histograms concern the information supplied to a discovery procedure. They do not
identify the value of a sequence of treatment decisions. Semantic entropy of model answers
does not by itself establish simultaneous graph coverage.
   RealTCD combines language-derived initialization with numerical optimization over temporal
graphs and intervention targets Li (2024). Its setup assumes causal sufficiency, a known
observational regime and an unrolled finite-lag DAG. The inspected theorem conditions its
population optimization result on model capacity, intervention faithfulness, positivity and
finite entropy. A stochastic optimizer with a thresholded adjacency matrix requires additional
analysis before it can inherit any finite-sample guarantee.
   The real cooling-system study does not have a complete ground-truth DAG. It uses selected
expert physical-location rules to assess edges. That is useful domain evidence but a different
evaluation from full known-truth graph recovery. The method also models abnormal windows
as intervention regimes. In a bank, a sudden spread movement could reflect a common market
shock, a changed selection mechanism or measurement failure. Treating it as an exogenous
intervention requires substantive evidence, not a threshold crossing.
  Kougioulis and colleagues’ Large Causal Model is an adjacent numerical transformer rather
than a language-model wrapper Kougioulis et al. (2026). Its inspected scope includes additive-
noise, stationary, causally sufficient, lagged-only systems. These conditions can be useful for a
declared class; they exclude several concerns in private banking states and common shocks.
The external pretrained weights have not been audited or executed locally. A language interface
should not rename this restricted temporal predictor as a general latent-graph solution.
   For longitudinal servicing, the analyst instead needs a sequence of decisions, available
histories, treatment-confounder feedback, censoring and a value target. A graph of temporal
dependence is only one ingredient. The intermediate account state can be affected by an earlier
action while confounding a later action’s effect. The correct question and inferential law must
be specified before an agent chooses an estimator. None of the inspected temporal discovery
results closes the project’s general latent temporal effect-set problem.
456                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


38.8     New interventions, mechanism proposals and information
         value
Lampinen and colleagues show how passive learning from expert demonstrations can support
active causal strategies Lampinen (2023). Their constructive argument first acquires causal
information through experiments, then exploits it. The evaluated learner can intervene in
its test environment. This is a valuable qualification: passive training is compatible with
active information acquisition, but the new interventions supply information that an analyst
restricted to historical bank records may lack.
  The inspected empirical settings use small finite acyclic systems and constrained observations
and actions. A banking translation must specify which interventions are feasible, who can
authorize them, their costs and their effect on future information. Merely asking a model
another question is not an intervention on the customer or the funding market. The two
actions have different likelihoods, costs and ethical or operational constraints.
   Murphy’s Model Discovery Agent proposes executable mechanisms with an LLM and fits
and compares them numerically Murphy (2026). The inspected studies include algebraic
mechanisms, latent ODEs and stochastic latent dynamics. The LLM expands the candidate
library; BIC or SMC approximations provide model evidence, and a model-disagreement
surrogate approximates expected information gain for experiment selection.
   This architecture gives each component a clearer role than requesting a final effect directly
from the model. It also exposes new obligations. An adaptive library may omit the true
mechanism. Pruning can discard a mechanism that would become useful later. BIC weights
within a retained pool are conditional model weights, not uniform graph-confidence statements.
Residual checks can reveal some misspecification but cannot certify that no policy-relevant
mechanism is absent.
   The paper explicitly states that its finite held-out prediction tests do not establish causal
identification. The experiments use open-loop policies, and the reported comparisons focus
on sample efficiency rather than matched total compute. The chemistry comparison retains
matched evaluable cells from a larger attempted collection. Those denominators must ac-
company the gains. For a bank, the value of information is the expected improvement in an
actual decision after paying acquisition and implementation costs. Information gain within a
model pool can be a design surrogate, but it is not that monetary quantity without an explicit
connection to the bank’s loss.


38.9      An auditable discovery interface
Zheng and colleagues describe causal-learn+ with agents assisting data inspection, assumption
elicitation, tool choice and interpretation around a formal discovery core Zheng (2026). They
emphasize separate objects for suggestions, user decisions, algorithm settings and graph outputs.
The design is a useful default for a banking library because it makes changes to scientific input
visible. It is not a universal impossibility result for hybrid discovery; a hybrid can be evaluated
as its own fully specified method.
  CausalAgent supplies another conversational architecture, including MCP tool interfaces
Zhu et al. (2026). Static source review finds that an inspected OLC tool calls a function
not imported or defined in that module, and a parser can return an empty dictionary after
malformed JSON. These are integration findings about pinned source, not measurements of a
running service. They show why transport success, parse success and scientific success need
separate dispositions. A successful model message is not a valid graph.
38.10. What would establish useful progress                                                   457


  For each request, an auditable interface should retain the business target, variable definitions
and clocks, numerical-data identity, retrieved-source identity, model and prompt version,
proposal, applied restrictions, selected algorithm and returned graph class. A reviewer should
be able to distinguish an expert’s asserted exclusion from an algorithmic orientation and from
a model’s suggestion. Changed restrictions create a new analysis identity; they should not
overwrite the prior result invisibly.
   Failure recovery must preserve scientific meaning as well as computation. If a job stops
after producing a partial graph, replay must not publish it as a complete answer. If a source
or data hash changes, an earlier identification claim cannot simply be reused. A report should
expose a refused or unknown effect when that is the formal outcome. The completed local
operation contract provides a bounded implementation surface; new discovery adapters still
need their own source, semantic and execution qualification.


38.10      What would establish useful progress
A meaningful comparison begins with a fixed question and information set. The numerical
baseline, language-only baseline, retrieval condition, hybrid and agent-assisted workflow should
receive explicitly matched information or have their information advantage declared. Accuracy
on familiar graphs is only one outcome. The study also needs identification correctness,
retention of compatible alternatives, valid abstention, effect-set coverage where a guarantee is
claimed, interval or set width, decision loss and full cost.
   Every request belongs in the denominator. Failed parsing, unavailable models, timeouts,
nonidentification and legitimate refusals have different meanings and should be recorded
separately. A graph metric conditional on successful requests can be informative, but it must
accompany the success probability and the selection rule. A narrow accurate set emitted only
in easy cases is not the same product as one that delivers useful valid output reliably.
  The proposed remedies are correspondingly bounded. Novel labels test one shortcut;
counterevidence tests retrieval dependence; correctly typed constraints prevent a specific
semantic conversion; fixed prompts and budgets make an experiment reproducible; and
preserved graph classes prevent one form of overstatement. None of these repairs creates
missing bank assignment truth, resolves observational equivalence by itself, or proves arbitrary
dependent-sample calibration.
   The immediate adoption position is therefore to use language assistance for explicit proposals
and reviewable workflow support, while qualifying each hybrid method separately. The original
unresolved temporal graph and useful precision results remain unresolved. New scientific
information, stronger assumptions justified in a declared regime, or additional experiments
may change those conclusions. More fluent explanations alone cannot.


38.11      Temporal predictions and interventions on conversations
A time series can support a useful prediction without identifying a useful intervention. The
distinction remains necessary when a language model produces a graph and an accompanying
explanation. Augur offers a concrete example: a teacher model proposes relations between
covariates, a student learns from selected explanations, and the downstream task predicts a
future trend. The inspected preprint evaluates air, power, traffic and finance settings, using
classification F1 and AUROC for prediction. These are relevant forecasting outcomes; they do
not estimate the value of a deposit rate change or a sequence of servicing actions. Zhiqing Cui,
Binwu Wang, Qingxiang Liu, Yeqiang Wang, Zhengyang Zhou, Yuxuan Liang and Yang Wang
458                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


(2025)


38.11.1     What a temporal graph proposal establishes

Augur first retains highly correlated pairs using Spearman ranks, asks a language model to
choose among directed, confounded and spurious relationships, and repairs graph cycles. Its
stability score measures agreement across candidate graphs. Its groundedness score checks
that a summary agrees with the graph from which it was generated. Each component has a
clear engineering purpose, but the latter two can be high when all candidates share the same
wrong causal premise. Acyclicity is a structural property; agreement with one’s own graph is
an internal consistency property. Zhiqing Cui, Binwu Wang, Qingxiang Liu, Yeqiang Wang,
Zhengyang Zhou, Yuxuan Liang and Yang Wang (2025)
   The authors explicitly acknowledge causal sufficiency and the possibility that correlation
pruning misses nonlinear or lagged dependence. Asking the model to output “confounded’ ’
does not independently demonstrate hidden-state identification. Nor does a chronological
train/test split create exchangeability of a proposed action. In a deposit application, funding
cost and deposit outflow may respond to an unobserved liquidity shock. A predictor can
exploit that relationship while remaining unable to answer what outflow would have been
under a different offered rate.
   The proposal should retain this architecture as a forecasting and hypothesis generation
comparator. A causal evaluation needs a separate target and separate truth: for example,
generated lagged mechanisms with known interventions, omitted common causes and nonlinear
dependence deliberately missed by marginal screening. Report predictive performance and
intervention performance separately. A failure of intervention recovery can coexist with a
useful forecast and should lead to a restricted product role, rather than erasing the forecast
result or relabeling it as policy evidence.


38.11.2     A directly relevant longitudinal method

Zhang, Wang and Dhillon study sequences of human edits and model replies. Their Causal-
Collab method proposes an Incremental Stylistic Effect (ISE), uses a conditional variational
autoencoder to represent editing styles, and combines a fitted outcome model with Monte
Carlo evaluation of a longitudinal functional. Their identification theorem explicitly assumes
sequential exchangeability and positivity for the style interventions. Thus there is a concrete
literature route for studying longitudinal human–LM collaboration; its existence should not be
obscured by a search that returns mostly generic causal-inference papers. Bohan Zhang, Yixin
Wang and Paramveer S. Dhillon (2024)
  For clarity, let Lt denote information presented before editing step t, At the human edit, and
Ht = (L̄t , Āt−1 ) the recorded history. A potential terminal outcome is Y (āT ). Exchangeability
requires the recorded history to remove the common causes of the edit and its downstream
outcome. An analyst’s private customer knowledge, skill or intention can violate this require-
ment even when every message has been logged. The low dimensionality of a style score also
does not establish overlap: legally required text may allow little variation in some histories,
and certain kinds of edit may never occur for distressed customers.
   The source defines the outcome associated with a style functional through a conditional
mixture over text versions having that style. This matters for implementation. A learned
coordinate and an instruction such as “make this more reassuring’ ’ need not describe the same
intervention. A model can make a response more reassuring by changing tone, by promising
compensation, or by omitting a warning. Those changes can have different effects and costs.
38.12. What additional information can language actually supply?                                459


Before adopting the estimand, the proposal must specify which distribution of complete edits
implements the change and which content must be held fixed.
   Consider a second project-generated reference example. Two proposed messages receive
the same “polite’ ’ label. Their stipulated response probabilities are 1/5 and 4/5, while the
reference message has response probability 1/10. Suppose an editing policy selects the second
message with probability q. Its effect against the reference is

                                       1   4  1    1  3
                                (1 − q) + q −   =    + q.
                                       5   5 10   10 5
   The effects are 1/10, 2/5, 7/10 at q = 0, 1/2, 1, respectively, despite an identical style label.
These are exact values under an invented law, not observed customer effects. They show
why the mixture is part of the intervention definition. A randomized choice among fixed text
variants is a substantive alternative to inferring a latent stylistic effect. It has a narrower
target but makes treatment versions directly inspectable.


38.11.3     What the available evidence leaves open

CausalCollab constructs counterfactual edits with ChatGPT, uses model-assigned outcome
labels, and changes the association between a confounding signal and the outcome in its
evaluation data. Its three sources include human–model collaborative writing, model self-chat,
and a hybrid dialogue setting. They should not all be described as independently observed
human intervention outcomes. Performance under this constructed design is useful evidence
about that design, but is not a direct measurement of how real users would have responded to
unchosen edits. Bohan Zhang, Yixin Wang and Paramveer S. Dhillon (2024)
   This supports an affordable proposal-stage evaluation. Begin with public or generated
interaction histories, fix a small set of content-preserving edit policies, and expose the evaluator
to known latent intentions and missing history in deliberately adverse cases. Compare a
fixed editing policy, an observed-association rule, a correctly specified numerical longitudinal
method, and the proposed representation-based method. Keep the true generator inaccessible
to the method. Assess policy-value error, support, refusal and total review effort, in addition
to language quality. Generated labels should be identified as such and their sensitivity to a
second label rule should be reported.
   A live human or bank experiment becomes valuable when this work identifies a consequential
uncertainty that the generated law cannot answer. It is not a prerequisite for specifying the
architecture or exposing its failure mechanisms. Conversely, neither the inspected theorem
nor a generated experiment entitles the proposal to claim identification under unrecorded
human intentions. Direct replication still requires review of the exact representation training,
integration scheme, outcome labels and source-code versions.


38.12      What additional information can language actually sup-
           ply?
The preceding comparisons leave a practical design question. If an assistant can explain
a sensible causal story but the data identify only an equivalence class, which additional
information is the explanation contributing? This can be answered precisely before choosing a
model provider. A restriction extracted from a dated policy document may eliminate a graph
because the policy fixes the order of decisions. A recollection about lending in general may
merely express a prior preference. A paraphrase of the same empirical association contributes
460                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


no new identifying information. The interface should make these three roles visible to the
analyst.
  Write P for the observed-data law and G(P ; A) for the set of graphs compatible with that
law under assumptions A. A numerical discovery procedure estimates features of this set. A
text-derived restriction R instead proposes the smaller set
                            GR (P ; A) = {G ∈ G(P ; A) : R(G) = 1}.
This is a useful operation if the restriction is applicable and justified. It is also a way to
manufacture certainty when an erroneous restriction deletes the true graph. The source, date,
population and interpretation of R are therefore part of the scientific object. A statement that
an account review occurs before an offer concerns a time order; it does not by itself assert that
review has no other causes or that all such causes were measured.
   For a deposit-pricing question, a policy may establish that a national rate is announced
before branch offers are made. That justifies a temporal restriction for the relevant dates.
It does not establish that managers did not anticipate the announcement, that the national
rate has no other effect on deposits, or that branch offers were assigned independently of
unrecorded local risk. A language assistant should return the restriction actually supported by
the passage and list the stronger restrictions that would be needed for the desired intervention
calculation. This follows the distinction between an assumption and its observable implications
in graphical model construction (Pablo Geraldo Bastías, 2024).
   An empty GR is an informative conflict. It can result from an incorrect text interpretation,
an unsuitable statistical model, sampling error, a missing variable or inconsistent restrictions
supplied by different owners. The proposed tool should return the smallest diagnosed conflicting
subset when it can compute one, and otherwise retain the full conflict. It should not silently
discard low-ranked edges until a DAG appears. The original evidence and all relaxations
remain visible. Producing a graph after changing the restrictions is a new analysis whose
identifying content has changed.
  A soft restriction makes a different tradeoff. A score of the form S(G; D) + λRM (G; T )
combines statistical fit with a model-derived preference. The regularization weight λ determines
how much the language preference can change the selected structure. Neither its numerical
scale nor an edge frequency from repeated prompts supplies a posterior probability that the
banking mechanism contains an edge. A meaningful sensitivity analysis varies the strength of
the preference, keeps the data term and feasible graph family fixed, and traces which decisions
change. Soft-constraint discovery is a legitimate alternative to a hard restriction, but it must
be compared under its stated meaning (Darvariu et al., 2024; Le et al., 2024).

38.12.1    An observational equivalence bound for an assistant

A short project derivation explains a limit that a more fluent assistant cannot remove without
new information. Suppose two structural models M0 and M1 generate the same observed law
for every available record and the same admissible documents, while their target effects are θ0
and θ1 , with ∆ = |θ1 − θ0 | > 0. Let the assistant, numerical code and critic together be any
randomized procedure using only those records and documents. Its internal randomization has
the same distribution in both worlds and contains no world-specific oracle. Then its reported
interval C also has the same distribution in both worlds.
  If the procedure claims coverage at least 1 − α under each model, the two events {θ0 ∈ C}
and {θ1 ∈ C} have probabilities at least 1 − α under that common report law. The elementary
union bound gives
                  Pr{θ0 , θ1 ∈ C} ≥ 1 − 2α,     Pr{diam(C) ≥ ∆} ≥ 1 − 2α.                  (38.6)
38.13. From edge accuracy to the bank’s decision loss                                         461


The diameter statement also holds for a set-valued report. It does not require normality,
a particular discovery algorithm or a claim that an LLM is statistically calibrated. It says
what uniform coverage would require in this two-world experiment. For nominal 95 percent
coverage and an effect separation of 2/5, diameter at least 2/5 is necessary with probability at
least 9/10. An algorithm that always returns a narrower interval cannot satisfy both coverage
claims. A refusal is an allowed scientific result; counting it as a successful narrow interval
would change the claim.
   The same argument has a decision form. If the correct binary action differs between the
two worlds, let q be the probability that the workflow selects action one. With unit loss for a
wrong action, its risks in the two worlds are q and 1 − q, in one order. Their maximum is at
least 1/2. More independent prompt draws can estimate q more precisely; they cannot make
both risks small when the observations and applicable text are the same. The way to improve
the decision is to obtain a discriminating restriction or intervention, accept a robust action, or
state the unresolved risk. The source of a useful restriction may be a person or a document,
but its validity is additional information.
   This limitation is directly relevant to the funding equivalence example in the Java adapter
discussion, where several Gaussian models share an observed covariance yet differ in the
intervention response. It also sharpens a fair language evaluation. If the supplied narrative
explicitly tells the model which world generated the data, the task assesses use of that
information. It must not be described as identification from the numerical observations alone.
If model pretraining contains relevant proprietary policy information, that information is also
part of the effective input and raises a provenance and transport question; it is not an invisible
extension of a statistical theorem.


38.13      From edge accuracy to the bank’s decision loss
The discovery target must be defined before a leaderboard is useful. A DAG, a CPDAG,
a PAG and an RFCI-PAG make different assertions. A DAG adds directions that may be
unresolved in a CPDAG. A PAG can retain circles because ancestral relations differ across
compatible latent-variable models. An RFCI adjacency can have a weaker meaning than an
FCI adjacency. Comparing all four as lists of directed edges against a single chosen DAG
can reward unwarranted certainty and punish scientifically correct ambiguity (Colombo et al.,
2012; pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a).
   A proposed evaluation should therefore publish separate losses for the skeleton, endpoint
marks, invariant ancestral claims, extra assumptions and the downstream estimand. If E ⋆ is
the true adjacency set under a declared reference and Eb the reported adjacency set, precision
and recall answer whether proposed links are right and whether reference links are found. An
orientation score computed only on E ⋆ ∩ E
                                         b answers a conditional question; it can look excellent
when most links were missed. Unknown endpoints should have their own accounting, with
a penalty only for claims the task actually requires. The interpretation of retrieval-assisted
orientation rates depends on precisely this denominator (Zhang et al., 2024).
   For an intervention, graph error matters through a loss function. Let Θ(G)  b collect effects
compatible with a reported graph class and other stated restrictions. A proposed action can
maximize worst-case utility, maximize utility under an explicitly elicited model distribution, or
request more information. These are different decision rules. The assistant must not silently
replace the first with the second by selecting the graph it finds most plausible. The nominal
effect interval and the range over graph models are also different objects; combining them
requires a stated procedure.
462                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Consider an exact planning example in which an offer costs 3 units per account and its
incremental gross return is either 0 or 8 under two observationally compatible models. The
net value of offering is either −3 or 5, whereas not offering has value zero. The worst-case
expected-value rule selects no offer. If an elicited probability q is placed on the high-return
model, the expected net value is 8q − 3 and offering is chosen only for q > 3/8. This threshold
makes the consequence of the extra belief visible. A language-model vote frequency cannot be
substituted for q without a model relating votes to which world is true. The costs and returns
are stipulated units, not bank prices or measured ROI.
   An ideal, free observation that perfectly reveals the model would yield value 5q, since the
offer would be made only in the high-return world. The value of that information before
paying for it is
                                     5q − max(0, 8q − 3).
At q = 1/2 it equals 3/2 units per account. A proposed experiment costing more than that
amount per account could not be justified by this particular perfect information calculation,
and a noisy experiment cannot exceed its value under the stipulated model. This is a planning
bound, not a recommendation to conduct a bank trial now. It identifies what an inexpensive
public or generated prototype should measure: whether the workflow preserves the ambiguity
and correctly reports the threshold for a decision.
   The criterion changes when loss includes customer harm, regulatory constraints or uneven
effects across groups. Those obligations must enter the feasible action set and utility definition
explicitly. A large mean return cannot by itself authorize an infeasible offer. Similarly, a loss
expressed per account requires care when one customer holds several accounts; the intervention
and interference units may differ. The graph workflow should surface these choices before
performing a cost comparison, rather than use the presence of a currency symbol as evidence
that the causal problem has been economically specified.


38.14      Two channels of uncertainty and a calibrated refusal
Graphical ambiguity and statistical uncertainty should survive into the same report without
being conflated. The first arises when the same population law is compatible with more than
one target effect under the stated information. The second arises because that law is estimated
from a finite sample. A third source, uncertainty about whether the variables and assumptions
are meaningful, is not automatically represented by either a confidence interval or a PAG. A
language assistant is often most useful on this third source: it can find an ambiguous definition
or an unsupported restriction. That usefulness does not make its confidence score a measure
of the first two.
   One proposed report therefore has a target object, an identification object, a sampling
object and an evidence-review object. The identification object states “identified under
these assumptions”, “nonidentified in this model class”, or “unknown because the available
procedure or input is inadequate”. Failure to find a back-door adjustment set with a restricted
implementation is not a proof of nonidentification. The sampling object states the estimator,
method of uncertainty calculation, population and any trimming or weighting. The evidence
object links assumptions to inspected sources and distinguishes missing evidence from a
retrieval failure. A failed numerical test is neither independence nor evidence of an unobserved
common cause.
   CausalDS is a useful comparator because it makes abstention on specified nonidentified
tasks part of the evaluation, and separates conceptual variables from their noisy observation
layer. Its finite benchmark findings remain reported evidence for those tasks. The source-level
38.15. Recent agent systems as competing scientific workflows                                   463


adaptations needed for our prototype are explicit three-state identification metadata, finite
output checks and denominators that distinguish principled abstention from missing files,
parsing errors and numerical failures (Leban and Sun, 2026; Netflix-Skunkworks/oci-agent;
andleb/causalds, 2026).
   A refusal can be correct without being useful enough for a product. The comparison should
score whether it names the missing assumption, unsupported operation or conflicting clock and
whether a feasible next action is supplied. A rule that refuses every request avoids some false
causal claims while failing all identifiable tasks. A rule that returns a number for every request
has high completion while failing nonidentified ones. Plotting error and returned-answer rate
over a frozen threshold is more informative than a single completion percentage, provided
the threshold was selected separately from the held-out assessment. All attempted requests,
including refusals and malformed outputs, remain in the operating-cost denominator.
   A critic can select which analyses reach the report, but acceptance by a critic is not
automatically conditional statistical coverage. As an exact counting example, six covered
intervals among six accepted requests, with two refusals, give selected coverage one and an all-
request return-and-cover rate of 3/4. Neither denominator alone shows a nominal conditional
guarantee. To investigate that claim, a prospective experiment must define the selection rule,
tasks and repeated sampling law, and report uncertainty for its empirical rates. The critic’s
access to a reference answer must be separated from the estimator’s information. Reviewing
one’s own answer with the same model adds an interaction, not independent scientific evidence.


38.15      Recent agent systems as competing scientific workflows
Recent systems should be compared by the boundary at which the agent’s output becomes
authoritative. In one architecture the agent directly proposes edges. In another it chooses
settings for a numerical engine. In a third it edits a shared data model or proof statement. A
fourth retrieves evidence for a human reviewer. All can be described as causal agents, but
they place different obligations on the scientific core and on the person who accepts the result.
The banking prototype should choose a boundary that can be tested with the information it
actually has.
   Zhu and colleagues’ CausalAgent combines data processing, structure learning and reporting
with MCP tooling and a Sachs demonstration. The inspected paper places quantitative effect
estimation and counterfactual modules among its future directions. Its strongest immediate
contribution to this proposal is a workflow pattern for moving from data and a question to
a structured report. The proposal cannot use the presence of MCP tools as evidence that
an early arrears-review effect has been identified, or that the future quantitative module is
already available. A direct integration decision must inspect the called implementation and
what it does when parsing or a backend call fails (Zhu et al., 2026; DMIRLAB-Group, 2026).
   Han and colleagues’ separately authored Causal Agent is a different source. It illustrates
named graph objects stored in tool memory and a generated question benchmark. This is useful
for persistent state: an analyst should be able to distinguish the graph before a restriction
from the graph after it, and the target before trimming from the target after it. Yet storing a
graph under a durable name does not validate its construction. The proposed service binds a
graph’s content, variable definitions, information clock and added assumptions together. Two
graph objects with the same edge list can still be different scientific inputs if their variables or
populations differ (Kairong Han, Kun Kuang, Ziyu Zhao, Junjian Ye and Fei Wu, 2026).
   ORCA places more emphasis on relational state, including joins, variable roles, graphs and
estimation configuration. This addresses a real banking problem: joining an account table
464                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


to a customer table can multiply rows, change the unit and create a misleading apparent
sample size before discovery begins. Its reported PAG-to-DAG step, however, makes additional
orientation or editing choices. Those choices must be visible as assumptions. The inspected
report also contains a discrepancy between the abstract’s 42-percentage-point completion
improvement and a table with completion rates .83 and .75. Completion is defined there by
production of an ATE without requiring accuracy. The proposal retains the discrepancy and
avoids treating either a completion figure or the existence of a final estimate as evidence of
correct causal inference. No corrected experiment is invented (Joanie Hayoun Chung, Sumin
Lee and Sungbin Lim, 2026).
   The causal-learn+ position puts assistance around a protected discovery core. Agents can
help inspect data, explain algorithms and interpret results while formal algorithms retain
responsibility for the numerical discovery operation. That division is the preferred initial design
here because it makes the scientific method and the agent’s added assumptions separately
inspectable. It still requires a correct core: a well-typed call to a flawed algorithm is not a
sound discovery result. It also leaves measurement, latent structure and sampling assumptions
open to review. The paper’s call for future evaluation supports a candidate architecture, not a
measured banking advantage (Zheng, 2026).
   CausalSmith adds a different kind of protection by making a formal statement, its proof
dependencies and compiler outcome explicit. A checked proof answers whether the formal
statement follows within its logical environment. It does not settle whether “recovery”, “offer”
and “available before treatment” were formalized faithfully, or whether the assumptions describe
the bank. The inspected limitations retain unvalidated model judgments about statement
faithfulness and research quality. The appropriate use is to expose a proof obligation and its
assumptions, then review the mapping to the business problem. It is not to treat successful
compilation as a substitute for that mapping (Jiyuan Tan and Vasilis Syrgkanis, 2026).
   These choices lead to a concrete reuse recommendation. Adapt stateful specification and
evidence-reporting ideas, retain a fixed independently reviewed numerical core, and require
typed proposals for changes to the target, variables or graph restrictions. Defer unrestricted
autonomous execution until the full package and operational path is audited. Reject automatic
conversion of an uncertain graph into an asserted DAG merely to enable a downstream
estimator. Keep proof assistance as a separate declared capability whose formal assumptions
remain inspectable. The proposal claims that these boundaries make errors easier to observe;
an empirical claim that they reduce review cost or improve accuracy awaits a matched study.
   This decision is revisable. A more autonomous system could be preferable if a fixed public
or generated evaluation shows that it preserves targets and graph uncertainty with less total
effort. A protected core could be ineffective if most errors occur in the semantic mapping
before the core is called. Both outcomes are plausible hypotheses. The next experiment should
therefore measure where corrections occur and what information was needed to make them,
rather than count the number of agent roles or reward the longest explanation.


38.16      Following the full package path rather than the package
           name
A research package is not interchangeable with an executable operation of the proposed
library. The first path is a selected PC call in causal-learn, its returned graph representation,
a conversion into the shared graph schema, a context-aware diagnostic report and a bounded
CLI or MCP response. The inspected MIT-licensed revision offers a plausible direct integration
route, but its twelve direct dependency declarations do not constitute a full pinned environment.
38.16. Following the full package path rather than the package name                             465


Porting the algorithm now would add maintenance responsibility without a measured embedding
constraint that justifies it. Executable admission is therefore deferred while this path is
completed; the reuse choice itself is concrete and reviewable (cmu-phil/causal-learn; Causal
banking proposal, 2026).
   The PC and FCI profiles must remain distinct. A PC bidirected conflict under an orientation
rule cannot silently become the latent-common-cause assertion of a PAG. The conversion needs
the two proximal endpoint marks, a bijection from input variables to nodes, and isolated nodes.
Unsupported composite endpoint encodings remain unsupported. A Fisher-Z failure due to a
singular inverse, an invalid n−|S|−3 term or a nonfinite numerical value cannot become a valid
independence decision. An α threshold for one query does not supply whole-graph or effect-set
coverage. These are requirements for the first scoped adapter, not benefits already delivered by
listing causal-learn as a dependency (cmu-phil/causal-learn; Causal banking proposal, 2026).
   Tetrad provides a materially different Java path. At the inspected revision, FCI initializes
circle endpoints and invokes orientation code with a flag for excluding selection bias. The
class-level reference to a CPDAG is inconsistent with the PAG-oriented search path and
cannot define the interchange contract. RFCI is a separate procedure with its own graph
meaning. The Edge constructor can reverse the stored order of nodes for a left-pointing edge,
so conversion must bind each mark to its proximal node, not assume that construction order
is stable. Star and null endpoint values exist in the Java enum but are outside the proposed
initial PAG interchange profile (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026c).
   Static inspection also identifies a specific reason to withhold full FCI behavioral qualification
at that revision. In the inspected possible-D-SEP block, the code builds one candidate set
from each endpoint, with a path-length argument of three, and tests that complete set. That
block does not enumerate all of its subsets. Conditional independence is not monotone in the
conditioning set: adding a collider can turn independence into dependence. The existing exact
Gaussian counterexample demonstrates this logical point; it is not an executed counterexample
to the entire Tetrad algorithm, whose earlier skeleton phase and later rules can affect the
actual candidate graph. The required next check follows the whole search on an oracle fixture
that reaches this block (Causal banking research project, 2026x; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026c).
   A second branch matters when configuration is changed. The ordinary finalOrientation
call is inside the possible-D-SEP branch in the inspected search method. Setting that option
false skips that call; a separate optional guarantee-PAG branch is not a substitute for an
unexamined claim of algorithmic equivalence. The conclusion is bounded: the source path
needs qualification, not that every Tetrad release or every returned graph is wrong. The
available local Java 11 runtime and absent compiler also do not meet the Java 21 build profile
previously reviewed. No Java FCI, RFCI or endpoint roundtrip has been executed in this
review (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026c,b).
   The proper alternatives are an isolated, pinned Tetrad environment with method-specific
oracle and numerical tests; the separately reviewed R pcalg FCI/RFCI routes; and a separately
reviewed Python FCI profile. Their settings, selection assumptions, graph classes and conversion
conventions have to be matched before any speed comparison. A benchmark that times a
truncated search against a fuller search without labeling the difference measures a change
in scientific work as well as an implementation difference. A process bridge adds startup,
serialization, memory and recovery costs that belong in the complete workflow comparison.
466                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


38.17      A hidden-risk example with identical observable distri-
           butions
The information bound becomes tangible in a nondegenerate Gaussian example. Here the
banking action is a standardized concession intensity, rather than the binary offer used in the
earlier motivating brief. Consider two centered models. In the first, independent disturbances
have variances Var(U ) = 1/2 and Var(ϵA ) = Var(ϵY ) = 1/2, and

                                 A = U + ϵA ,      Y = U + ϵY .

In the second, A has variance one and is independent of η, with Var(η) = 3/4, and

                                          Y = 21 A + η.

Both produce the bivariate normal law with variances one and covariance 1/2. Both have a
positive observed density on the plane. Their observed regression of Y on A has slope 1/2. In
the first model, intervening on A leaves Y unchanged, so the derivative of the intervention
mean is zero. In the second it is 1/2. Every statistic of the observed pair has the same sampling
distribution in the two models for every sample size. Recovering a precise association does not
decide which intervention response is right.
   The example isolates the role of private borrower information. The first model contains a
common cause that is unmeasured in the supplied table; the second attributes the association
to the concession. An agent given only the same table and an ambiguous description has no
model-specific evidence that selects one. Saying that the concession “obviously affects recovery”
introduces an assumption. It may be reasonable as part of a scenario, but it must be exposed
as such. A PAG over two observed variables can retain unresolved endpoint marks; returning
a single oriented edge removes an uncertainty that the data did not remove.
  Suppose a new predecision score W = U + ϵW is offered as a remedy, with independent
noise variance s. In the common-cause model the residual variance of U given W is
                                          (1/2)s       s
                                     v=           =        .
                                          1/2 + s   1 + 2s
After residualizing A and Y on W , their covariance is v and the residual variance of A is
1/2 + v. The adjusted coefficient is therefore
                                              v        2s
                                  βA|W =           =        .
                                           1/2 + v   1 + 4s
For s = 1/2 it is 1/3 although the true causal response is zero. With an exact score, s = 0,
it becomes zero; as the score becomes uninformative it approaches 1/2. This is a separate
model from the unit-variance text-measurement example in the earlier chapter. The variance
choices and action definition are stated so that the two examples are not mistakenly pooled.
A document extractor can help create W , but the identifying question is what information its
error model and validation sample supply.
   The remedy is specific. Obtain a defensible measurement model with information sufficient for
the proposed correction, a justified assignment restriction, or an intervention that distinguishes
the worlds. A smaller standard error from more observations of (A, Y, W ) does not remove
the residual coefficient when s stays positive. A language agent can explain the alternatives,
request the necessary metadata and prevent a false report of identification. It cannot invent
an independent validation sample by generating plausible labels. The exact covariance and
residual-variance calculations in this section are project derivations, reproduced in rational
arithmetic (Causal banking proposal, 2026m).
38.18. Why a CI threshold is not graph or effect coverage                                       467


38.18      Why a CI threshold is not graph or effect coverage
A discovery interface often exposes one number called alpha. Its scope must be made explicit
to an agent and to a business reviewer. For a particular fixed conditional-independence test,
a level-α statement concerns the probability of rejecting that null when it is true under the
declared sampling law. It does not bound the probability that a whole graph is correct, that
all orientations are right, or that a derived effect interval covers its target. A graph can fail
because a false independence is accepted, an assumption is wrong, a query is numerically
invalid, or an orientation is misinterpreted. Those errors are not all controlled by a single
null-rejection level.
  Even the limited false-rejection claim changes when many queries are possible. For p
observed variables, all unordered variable pairs and all conditioning subsets of the remaining
variables form a family of size                  !
                                               p p−2
                                       M=         2 .
                                               2
If each fixed query has unconditional type-I error at most α, then a union bound controls
at least one false rejection among that fixed finite family by M α, truncated at one. No
independence between query decisions is needed for this inequality. It applies to any adaptively
selected subset of the family only when the procedure uses the same prespecified tests and the
per-query calibration holds for every fixed query; an adaptive prompt that changes the data
or test definition is not covered by that argument.
   With six variables there are 240 possible pair/subset queries. At α = .05 the bound is
uninformative. At α = .0002 it is .048 for the specified false-rejection event. This second
number is still not a 95.2 percent guarantee for the graph: it does not control missed alternatives,
faithfulness violations, latent-variable misspecification or endpoint conversion. The example is
useful because it gives the assistant a precise explanation of what alpha can and cannot mean.
It is not a recommendation to choose a universal threshold of .0002 for bank discovery.
   The same distinction applies to language-response tests. Their sampling law is a law of
model answers under a prompt and decoding configuration. A response frequency can be
estimated under assumptions about repeatability, but it does not inherit the error guarantee of
a numerical CI test. An agent that reads a column named “pvalue” must check the generating
procedure. The response-based variance calculation in the preceding material demonstrates
one implementation hazard; the more fundamental issue is that the response null and the
banking distributional null are different statements.
   For the prototype, every CI result should therefore include the query, sampling unit,
conditioning variables, test method, usable observations and computation status. A singular
matrix produces an unavailable test, not a very strong scientific dependence claim. The search
result should state whether all required queries completed and whether any search bounds or
time limits changed the explored family. The report should retain sensitivity to thresholds and
to permitted restrictions without presenting that sensitivity exercise as a calibrated confidence
set. A qualified effect procedure needs its own identification and uncertainty argument after
the graph step.


38.19      A public evaluation design that can change the proposal
The immediate evaluation should test whether language assistance improves the causal workflow
within a fixed information budget. It can use public documents for realistic vocabulary
and project-generated mechanisms for known truth, with the two origins clearly separated.
468                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


Generation does not create authentic bank assignment evidence, but it makes intervention
effects, measurement error, latent variables and timing failures observable to a held-out scorer.
Private truth must not enter the assistant’s prompt, retrieval corpus, tool output or file tree.
The predeclared deterministic baseline receives the same permitted brief and data as the
assisted workflow.
   A useful task portfolio crosses four dimensions. One varies whether the effect is identified from
the supplied graph and observations. Another varies whether variable names are informative,
neutral or misleading. A third changes whether the document’s reported time and its availability
time agree. A fourth varies whether text contains a valid additional restriction, a contradiction
or no relevant information. This is a design proposal; choosing the generator, sample size,
splits and replication count requires a prospective protocol before any performance study.
A successful run on a few authored examples is a conformance check, not a retrospective
preregistration.
   The banking tasks should include an offer distinct from uptake, a branch-level intervention
with account-level observations, an unrecorded borrower-risk variable, and a postdecision note
that looks like a baseline covariate. They should include a graph with correct but unresolved
endpoints and a case where an apparent numerical failure is caused by exact accounting
identities. A language model that recommends a valid operation but uses the wrong treatment
variable has not answered the task. Conversely, a workflow that retains the right target and
returns a justified nonidentification result can succeed on a case for which no point estimate is
licensed.
   Names and mechanisms should be perturbed separately. Replacing all banking terms with
anonymous labels can remove legitimate intervention and timing information, so that pertur-
bation is scored as a different information regime. Holding the definitions fixed while changing
irrelevant wording probes another kind of robustness. Reversing a generated mechanism under
familiar names tests whether the model follows data or a memorized story. The inspected
work on pretraining relation frequency motivates this distinction, but its findings for accessible
models and commonsense relationships are not a theorem about all language models or all
banking questions (Feng, 2024).
   Document-level leakage also needs a precise split. If the same policy is paraphrased into both
development and evaluation sets, a row-level random split does not produce an unseen policy.
If several accounts share one assignment rule or one customer, independent-row formulas
may overstate the effective sample. The proposed protocol should group related documents,
mechanisms and customers according to the claim it seeks to assess, and say which kind
of transfer remains untested. No generic instruction to “hold out 20 percent” settles these
scientific dependencies.
   For each request the result should contain the target identity, permitted information,
proposed graph class, assumptions added by the agent, formal identification state, numerical
method and final disposition. Metrics should include false causal assertions, missed identifiable
opportunities, unsupported orientations, effect error where meaningful, interval loss and
all-request resource cost. Model-only latency omits retrieval, serialization, review, retries,
corrections and refused jobs. A cheap request that repeatedly needs an analyst to repair a
target can cost more than a slower fixed workflow.
  The proposal changes if the assisted path reliably reduces a specified review burden while
maintaining these scientific boundaries on a frozen task family. It also changes if assistance
adds unsupported restrictions or hides failures, even when the prose improves. A later live
comparison must bind provider and model versions, prompts, decoding, tool identities, custody
and actual prices; none of these results is inferred from this design. An expensive bank
experiment becomes relevant only after the prototype isolates an uncertainty that public or
38.20. Choosing the numerical core before asking an agent to choose                             469


generated evidence cannot answer and shows why resolving it can alter the investment decision.



38.20       Choosing the numerical core before asking an agent to
            choose
The proposed protected core still leaves a substantive choice. Constraint search, score opti-
mization, functional equations and changes of environment can all return a graph, but they
use different information to distinguish directions. An assistant should explain the reason
for choosing among them. Selecting the package that happens to accept the input table is
insufficient. For a branch-pricing problem, the first questions are whether the table records
independent units or a dependent panel, whether omitted common causes are plausible, whether
the action and outcome have a reliable order, and whether the proposed structural restrictions
are defensible for those variables. Only then is it useful to compare runtime and interface
convenience.
   PC uses conditional-independence information with a causally sufficient DAG interpretation
under its assumptions. Its partially directed output preserves orientations that the available
independence information does not determine. FCI permits latent and selection variables under
a different model class and returns PAG information. RFCI trades some adjacency information
for a less expensive search. The differences matter when an analyst asks whether a borrower’s
private assessment jointly influences an offer and subsequent recovery. Selecting PC after
simply deleting that unrecorded assessment from the variable list does not remove the common
cause. Selecting FCI does not make the effect point identified. Its output may correctly retain
precisely the ambiguity that prevents a unique intervention calculation (Colombo et al., 2012;
cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026c).
   A score search instead compares how well candidate structures represent the data after ac-
counting for complexity or prior preferences. A selected DAG can be an effective computational
summary without being the only causal explanation. The score, its statistical interpretation,
the search space and the optimization outcome are separate choices. If two structures have the
same observable implications under the supplied information, an arbitrary tie break does not
become a discovered direction. A language prior can break the tie, but the report must then
attribute the direction to that added restriction or preference. For the proposed bank tool, a
ranked candidate list is useful if its conditional meaning remains visible; an unsupported claim
that the first entry is the true mechanism is not.
  NOTEARS illustrates both the appeal and the limit of a continuous formulation. For data
matrix X with n rows and d columns, the inspected linear formulation uses a coefficient matrix
W and the objective
                      1
          F (W ) =      ∥X − XW ∥2F + λ∥W ∥1 ,        h(W ) = tr exp(W ◦ W ) − d = 0.
                     2n
Here Wij represents a coefficient from variable i to variable j, ◦ denotes entrywise multiplication,
and the exponential is a matrix exponential. This convention differs from a target-row coefficient
matrix. The acyclicity characterization is an inherited result, not an identifying assumption
that language can supply. If S = W ◦ W , every entry of S is nonnegative and each tr(S k ) sums
weighted closed walks. The expansion tr exp(S) = d + k≥1 tr(S k )/k! is equal to d exactly
                                                             P

when the graph has no directed cycle. Squaring the entries prevents positive and negative edge
weights from cancelling a cycle in this argument (Zheng et al., 2018).
  That theorem separates a structural requirement from the inferential question. A small
computed h(W ) is a numerical diagnostic of one constraint. It is not a probability that the
470                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


graph is correct. The original paper expressly distinguishes stationary-point optimization from
global minimization, and its statistical interpretation refers to assumptions studied separately.
The inspected reference implementation also has an ℓ1 penalty, augmented-Lagrangian stopping
rules and a final weight threshold. Each can change the output. An agent that raises the
threshold until a graph looks sparse has changed the analysis; it has not improved a calibrated
confidence level. The exact returned graph needs a structural check after thresholding, and the
fit needs an appropriate scientific interpretation (Zheng et al., 2018; xunzheng/notears, 2026).
   An apparent advantage of one discovery method can also depend on units. Multiplying a
deposit balance column by a thousand changes an unstandardized squared-error objective and
the relative meaning of a common coefficient penalty. A nonlinear transformation changes
the functional model still more. The transformation, back-transformation and intervention
scale should be part of the proposed specification. A rank-based numerical method, a linear
equation method and a language judgment need not have the same invariances. The comparison
should expose this difference instead of assuming that an identical CSV file makes all models
scientifically matched.
   LiNGAM obtains directional information from a different restriction: a linear acyclic system
with mutually independent, non-Gaussian disturbances and no unobserved confounders. Its
original model assumes repeated independent vectors generated with the same equations and
disturbance distributions. The inspected original construction uses independent component
analysis; the currently inspected DirectLiNGAM code is a separate algorithmic route. The
source explicitly notes that this model need not impose faithfulness. Consequently, a failure
of a faithfulness-based argument does not by itself refute LiNGAM. Conversely, apparent
skewness of observed loan balances does not establish the non-Gaussianity and independence
of the structural disturbances in the chosen equations. These are requirements on the model,
not labels that can be inferred from column names (Shimizu, Shohei and Hoyer, Patrik O. and
Hyvärinen, Aapo and Kerminen, Antti, 2006; cdt15/lingam, 2026).
   The Gaussian equivalence example earlier in this chapter intentionally lies outside that
non-Gaussian restriction. It cannot be used as an impossibility proof for every functional
discovery model. This distinction is productive: one can escape an observational equivalence
by supplying additional information or by restricting the admissible structural models. The
proposal should state which of these it is doing and what evidence supports the restriction.
The language component can retrieve a scientific argument for linear mechanisms, question
an independence assumption or compare an alternative model. It cannot verify disturbance
independence merely by producing a coherent explanation.
   For time series, the underlying sampling and causal model changes again. The inspected
PCMCI+ result requires its stated sufficiency, stationarity, faithfulness, lag coverage and test
consistency conditions; selection and measurement error are outside that theorem. Contempo-
raneous directions can remain unresolved. A calendar panel containing common shocks and
repeated accounts cannot inherit the result solely because the records have a date column. The
assistant should identify the sampling unit and candidate lag family, explain which common
causes are represented, and retain uncertainty about contemporaneous effects. Declaring a
lag of one because the prompt is shorter is a substantive restriction, not a harmless interface
choice (Runge, 2020).
   These comparisons imply a staged software decision. Retain method-specific profiles for
PC, FCI/RFCI, functional equations, continuous score search and temporal discovery. Each
profile binds the statistical assumptions, graph meaning, matrix convention, search bounds
and failure behavior. Reuse a reviewed implementation when its complete path can be made
reproducible; consider porting only when a measured deployment or numerical requirement
justifies the maintenance burden. A common result schema can preserve their differences. It
38.21. Faithfulness can fail even with complete measurements                                 471


should not force every method to emit a fully oriented DAG or an effect estimate when that is
stronger than the method supports.


38.21      Faithfulness can fail even with complete measurements
A second exact project example separates missing variables from cancellation. Let A, EM , EY
be independent centered Gaussian variables with unit variance, and define

                     M = A + EM ,        Y = −A + M + EY = EM + EY .

The structural graph contains A → M , A → Y and M → Y . All three variables are observed,
all disturbance variances are positive, and the joint distribution has a nonsingular covariance
matrix. Nevertheless A ⊥ Y : the direct and mediated paths cancel in the marginal law. The
covariance matrix, in the order (A, M, Y ), is
                                 
                        1 1 0
                                                                    1·1   1
                   Σ = 1 2 1 ,          Cov(A, Y | M ) = 0 −          =− .
                             
                                                                     2    2
                        0 1 2

Thus independence at the empty conditioning set and dependence after conditioning can arise
here without the structural collider explanation that a faithful model would use. This is not a
numerical roundoff example. The zero is an exact property of the stipulated population law.
  There is indeed a different structural model with that faithful collider explanation. Take
mutually independent A ∼ N (0, 1), Y ∼ N (0, 2) and η ∼ N (0, 1/2), and set

                                       M = A + 21 Y + η.

It produces exactly the same Σ and therefore the same centered Gaussian distribution. In
the triangle model, changing M while leaving A’s equation intact changes the mean of Y
with derivative one. In the collider model, intervening on M leaves Y unchanged. The target
effects are different despite complete observed-variable measurement in both models. Invoking
faithfulness selects a model class that excludes the triangle; it does not make the observable
covariance itself reveal which structural world generated the records (Causal banking proposal,
2026l).
   For a banking interpretation, A may represent standardized offer intensity, M a subsequent
account-balance response and Y net revenue. A direct cost and an indirect revenue channel
can offset each other. The equations are stipulated and should not be taken as an empirical
model of that mechanism. They explain why an observed zero association can have several
meanings. A reliable chronology establishing M before Y would rule out the second model as
an ordinary acyclic causal explanation. That chronology is additional information. With only
a coarse accounting period, an agent must not assume that the order of columns supplies it.
  Cancellation is also a finite-precision concern. Replace the direct coefficient by −1 + δ. Then
                                                                                  δ−1
            Y = δA + EM + EY ,         Cov(A, Y ) = δ,         Cov(A, Y | M ) =       .
                                                                                   2
The marginal signal can be arbitrarily small while the conditional signal remains appreciable.
A consistency statement for a fixed nonzero signal does not guarantee useful uniform recovery
as δ approaches zero. This explains why the prototype should vary cancellation strength and
retain weak-signal failures. Increasing prompt detail does not increase the numerical separation
between these distributions.
472                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The appropriate remedy depends on the claim. A verified time order can exclude some
candidate graphs. An intervention on the consequential variable can supply new information.
A functional model can use restrictions not present in conditional-independence information,
provided those restrictions are defensible. A conservative report can retain multiple mechanisms
and compare their decision implications. None of these remedies is equivalent to choosing an
orientation because it sounds natural in a bank narrative. The exact example supports a test
of this distinction without paying for live calls or obtaining bank data.


38.22       A search budget changes which separations can be found
The conditioning-set budget has a similarly concrete scientific meaning. Consider mutually
independent unit-variance centered Gaussian disturbances and the structural equations
           A = EA ,      M1 = A + E1 ,       M2 = A + E2 ,         Y = M1 + M2 + EY .
There are two parallel paths from A to Y and no direct edge. Their total intervention derivative
is two. The observed covariance matrix is
                                                          
                                                 1 1 1 2

                                 ΣA,M1 ,M2 ,Y =           .

The Gaussian conditional covariance calculation gives
      Cov(A, Y ) = 2,   Cov(A, Y | M1 ) = Cov(A, Y | M2 ) = 21 ,    Cov(A, Y | M1 , M2 ) = 0.

For the last equality, the mediator covariance inverse is 13 −1     2 ; multiplying the cross-
covariances subtracts exactly two. A search limited to conditioning sets of size at most one
cannot find the separator for this pair, even with an exact oracle and an unlimited sample. A
reported extra adjacency is therefore a possible consequence of the search restriction, rather
than evidence for a direct offer-to-revenue mechanism (Causal banking proposal, 2026l).
   This example also distinguishes a discovery query from an adjustment rule. Conditioning on
the mediators helps discover that a direct adjacency is unnecessary. Adjusting them away when
estimating the total effect of A would remove the very paths that define that effect. An agent
should not copy the variables from a separating set into an outcome-regression adjustment
list without reviewing the target and graph. The same named set can be appropriate for one
computational question and inappropriate for another.
   The proposed comparison should therefore bind the maximum conditioning order, the
admissible variable sets, the CI test and its missing-result behavior. Record the number of
attempted queries as well as completed ones and preserve which search bounds were active. A
faster configuration with smaller search depth is a useful alternative when the user accepts its
scope, but it is not automatically a faster implementation of the same inferential procedure.
For banking data, higher conditioning order can also reduce usable observations and aggravate
singularity or mixed-type test limitations. Relaxing one computational constraint can create
another statistical problem.
  This small model is a conformance reference for a future integration. It can check that the
adapter preserves query variables, reports the configured depth and distinguishes a population
zero from an unavailable test. The calculation does not claim that any inspected package
has been run or that the entire search will visit a particular query in a particular order.
Whole-engine qualification still needs a pinned executable path and an observed trace. The
source-inspected Tetrad branch discussed earlier and this mathematical example answer
complementary questions.
38.23. Several environments need a causal interpretation of their changes                     473


38.23       Several environments need a causal interpretation of
            their changes
An assistant may propose using changes across branches, countries or policy periods to orient
a relation. Invariant prediction provides a substantive alternative to single-environment graph
search. The inspected formulation assumes that, for a suitable predictor subset, the response
mechanism and independent error law remain invariant across environments. In the linear
case, the same coefficients and residual distribution apply in each setting. Under its stated test
and candidate-set assumptions, the intersection of nonrejected subsets controls false inclusions
in that invariant subset; it does not promise recovery of every cause. Connecting the invariant
subset to causal parents requires the corresponding structural assumptions. In particular,
arbitrary changes to the response or its hidden causes are not licensed by the presence of an
environment label (Peters et al., 2016).
  The distinction can be exhibited with another exact project law. Index environments by
a known number m. Let independent variables satisfy U ∼ N (m, 1), EA ∼ N (0, 1) and
EY ∼ N (0, 1/2), and write
                                                            m
                              A = U + EA ,       Y =U−        + EY .
                                                            2
Here A has no causal effect on Y . Yet in every environment

        E(A) = m,      E(Y ) = m/2,     Var(A) = 2,     Cov(A, Y ) = 1,     Var(Y ) = 3/2.

Gaussian conditioning gives Y | A, m ∼ N (A/2, 1), independent of m. A stable conditional
predictor has emerged from changing a hidden common cause and compensating the outcome
intercept. The different model A ∼ N (m, 2), Y = A/2 + η with independent η ∼ N (0, 1) has
the same observed law in every environment and an intervention derivative of 1/2. Thus the
environment-indexed observations do not distinguish these two causal explanations (Causal
banking proposal, 2026l).
   This construction does not contradict the invariant-prediction theorem. It violates the
structural interpretation needed to treat the stable observed regression as the unchanged
causal response mechanism: the hidden cause and the outcome equation change together. It
demonstrates why a test of one observed conditional distribution cannot by itself certify the
provenance of the environment changes. An apparently successful comparison across many
branches can still be uninformative if their changes share this structure. The number of
environments is not a count of independent randomized interventions on the proposed action.
   For a deposit application, a market stress period may change demand, the bank’s pricing
rule and measurement practices at the same time. A dated policy document can establish
that pricing changed, but it may not establish that all other relevant mechanisms remained
fixed. A useful language task is to construct an environment dossier: what changed, when it
became effective, which variables it could affect, and what the sources leave unknown. If the
dossier supports a narrower intervention family, a numerical method can be assessed under
that family. Otherwise the environment comparison remains a predictive or sensitivity analysis
with explicit limits.
   The public prototype can test this reasoning affordably. Generate environments that alter
only an admissible predictor mechanism and compare them with the compensating-change
construction above. Keep the target and permitted documents fixed within each regime, and
hide the generator from the assistant. A successful workflow should distinguish failure to reject
invariance from evidence that the structural assumptions were supplied. A correct refusal
in the second regime and a useful result in the first are different outcomes that should both
474                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


appear in the evaluation. This is a proposed study design; the exact algebra supplies reference
cases without supplying performance estimates for any model.


38.24       Allowing mistakes in extracted restrictions without hid-
            ing them
Hard restrictions become especially fragile when an agent extracts many of them. Let GD be
the graph class retained from numerical evidence, and let R1 , . . . , RJ be proposed predicates
on a graph. The ordinary intersection retains only graphs satisfying every predicate. A more
explicit sensitivity construction allows at most k predicates to be wrong:
                                                                         

This is a proposed deterministic construction, not an implemented general graph solver. If the
true graph lies in GD and violates at most k proposed restrictions, it lies in GD,k . Enlarging
k cannot shrink the retained class. Mapping that class into effect sets makes the decision’s
dependence on the trusted restrictions visible.
   For an exact finite illustration, label four otherwise admissible candidate models Gab by
two binary properties a, b. Suppose the extracted claims assert a = 1, b = 1, and that exactly
one property is one. The joint intersection is empty. Allowing one erroneous claim retains
G01 , G10 and G11 , since each violates exactly one claim; G00 violates two and is excluded.
A nonempty relaxed class has therefore not proved that the true model was retained. If the
truth is G00 , the one-error sensitivity analysis still misses it. The remedy requires either more
trusted evidence or a larger declared error allowance, with the consequent loss of precision
(Causal banking proposal, 2026l).
   A probabilistic guarantee requires actual error control in addition to that logical construction.

38.25       An intervention’s value can be calculated before con-
            ducting it
The perfect-information calculation above is an upper bound. A prospective experiment
normally supplies noisy information, so a prototype should also evaluate the attainable value
under a declared experiment. Return to the chapter’s two binary worlds. In the forward world,
A is a fair binary action and Y equals A with probability .9. In the reverse world, Y is fair and
A equals Y with probability .9. Both have the same observational table. Under a controlled
action A = 1, however, the outcome success probabilities are .9 and .5, respectively. This
difference comes from replacing the action equation, not from resampling the old observational
table.
   Assume, solely for this planning calculation, that independently intervened units can be
drawn from the same structural world, that outcomes are observed without loss, and that
neither interference nor experimentation changes the mechanism. If K successes are observed
in n probes, let                  !                             !

                      fH (k) =     (.9) (.1)    ,    fL (k) =    (.5)n .

the prior odds multiplied by 1.8k .2n−k . Unlike a prompt-vote fraction, this update has an
explicit observation law and an explicit relationship to the two worlds. Its validity remains
conditional on those two worlds and the stipulated intervention protocol.
   Connect it to the earlier offer decision by assigning gross incremental value ten times the
intervention effect and an offer cost of three. The effects are .8 and zero, giving net offer values
five and minus three; no offer has value zero. For a future comparable account, the optimal
action after observing k is to offer when qk > 3/8. Before the probe results are known, the

To obtain this expression, multiply the conditional optimum max(0, 8qk − 3) by the predictive

including evidence that leads to no offer. There is no favorable outcome selection.

a failure leads to no offer; the expected value becomes 3/2, so the expected value of sample
information is 1/2. With two probes, only two successes justify an offer. The expected value
is 33/20, giving sample-information value 13/20. Exact enumeration for larger n appears
